He eyes you. "Yes, I saw the 'cast. Terrorist number one."

"I don't believe half of it, for what it's worth." A pause. "But I believe half of it, because this is you we're talking about."
entries.zh:
他打量着你。"是啊，那则广播我看了。头号恐怖分子。"

"顺带说一句，那里面我一半都不信。\"他顿了顿，\"可另一半我信，因为说的是你。"

o.en: I understand your reticence, but acting now is the right move.
o.zh: 我理解你的顾虑，但现在动手才是对的。

entries.en:
He eyes you. "You're terrorist number one to the Sindrian Diktat."

"I don't believe half of it, for what it's worth." A pause. "But I believe half of it, because this is you we're talking about. What you should do is lay low, like I said."

He fiddles with a crystal glass from his decanter set, but doesn't fill it. Yet.

"And what I should do is have nothing to do with any of this."
entries.zh:
他打量着你。"在辛达强权那里，你是头号恐怖分子。"

"顺带说一句，那里面我一半都不信。\"他顿了顿，\"可另一半我信，因为说的是你。你该做的是低调蛰伏，我说过了。"

他摆弄起酒具里的一只水晶杯，却没有倒酒。暂时没有。

"而我该做的，是跟这一切都不沾边。"

o.en: I understand your reticence, but I need to take the initiative.
o.zh: 我理解你的顾虑，但我必须抢先动手。

o.en: Well never mind, then. I'll lay low.
o.zh: 那就当我没说。我会低调蛰伏。

entries.en:
He eyes you. "You're terrorist number one to the Sindrian Diktat. You should be in hiding, like I said. Best PR move in a crisis like this is to shut up and make yourself scarce. Let the professionals run damage control." He frowns. "Figuratively, I mean."

He fiddles with a crystal glass from his decanter set, but doesn't fill it. Yet.
entries.zh:
他打量着你。"在辛达强权那里，你是头号恐怖分子。你该躲起来，我说过了。这种危机里最好的公关手段就是闭嘴、让自己从视线里消失。让专业人士去做危机管控。"他皱了皱眉，"我这是打比方。"

他摆弄起酒具里的一只水晶杯，却没有倒酒。暂时没有。

o.en: You're right. I'll keep my head down.
o.zh: 你说得对。我会低调藏好。

o.en: I understand your reticence, but I need to act.
o.zh: 我理解你的顾虑，但我必须行动。

entries.en:
"That bloodthirsty, raving blowhard?"

Arroyo holds his look for just a moment.
entries.zh:
"那个嗜血成性、满嘴疯话的牛皮大王？"

Arroyo 迎着你的目光，停了片刻。

entries.en:
"The clone who looks like he didn't finish thawing out from the cryo-pod they keep self-important little officers in? The uniformed puppet dancing for Fortuna Kato?"

Arroyo holds his look for just a moment.
entries.zh:
"就是那个看着像没从冷冻舱里化透的克隆人？那种舱专用来装自命不凡的小军官。还有那个穿着制服、围着 Fortuna Kato 打转的傀儡？"

Arroyo 迎着你的目光，停了片刻。

entries.en:
"That circus dumping-ground of pirates, zealots, and terrorists?"

Arroyo holds his look for just a moment.
entries.zh:
"那个海盗、狂信徒和恐怖分子凑成一堆的马戏团垃圾场？"

Arroyo 迎着你的目光，停了片刻。

entries.en: His expression makes it clear he does not welcome the topic.
entries.zh: 他的神情明摆着不欢迎这个话题。

entries.en: "Then why the big pitch?" He shakes his head, annoyed. "You're just going to lay low and wait after all?"
entries.zh: "那你刚才那一大通说辞算什么？\"他不耐烦地摇头，\"绕了一圈，你还是打算缩起来等？"

o.en: I'm serious. I'm going to try to lay low and see what happens.
o.zh: 我是认真的。我会尽量缩着不出头，看看会怎样。

o.en: No, I still need to deal with the situation in Askonia.
o.zh: 不，Askonia 的局面我还是得处理。

entries.en:
Arroyo slowly spins his chair so he's facing you once more. His look is skeptical, bordering on dismissive.

But he does appear to be listening.
entries.zh:
Arroyo 慢慢转动椅子，重新面向你。他的目光带着怀疑，几乎算得上不屑。

不过他看起来确实在听。

entries.en:
Arroyo slowly spins his chair around, turning his back to you, then returning so he's facing you once more. His look is skeptical, bordering on dismissive.

But he does appear to be listening.
entries.zh:
Arroyo 慢慢把椅子转过去，背对着你，又转回来，重新面向你。他的目光带着怀疑，几乎算得上不屑。

不过他看起来确实在听。

entries.en:
"Okay," he says, crossing his arms.

"Why do I suddenly care about your infantile need for revenge? Why am I supposed to work with you on... whatever this is?"
entries.zh:
"好，"他双臂抱在胸前。

"我为什么会突然在乎你那点幼稚的复仇心？我凭什么要跟你一起干...不管你这是在干什么？"

entries.en:
"Okay," he says, crossing his arms.

"Why do I suddenly care about Askonia? Why am I supposed to help you with... what are you even proposing?"
entries.zh:
"好，"他双臂抱在胸前。

"我为什么会突然在乎 Askonia？我凭什么要帮你...你到底在提什么？"

entries.en:
"Okay," he says, crossing his arms. "That's a bit vague, but now we're beginning to talk sense."

"And it's risky, even in the hypothetical. And you need to convince me why whatever you're proposing is worth it."
entries.zh:
"好，\"他双臂抱在胸前，\"说得有点含糊，不过总算开始讲点像样的话了。"

"而且就算只是假设，这也够冒险的。你得说服我，你提的这套为什么值得。"

entries.en:
"Okay," he says, crossing his arms. "I know you don't believe that - but I do. So I like how you're talking."

"But it's risky. And you need to convince me why whatever this is is worth it."
entries.zh:
"好，\"他双臂抱在胸前，\"我知道你自己都不信这话——可我信。所以你这套说法，我喜欢。"

"但这很冒险。你得说服我，这整件事为什么值得。"

entries.en:
"The right thing." He gives you a withering look. "To do."

"What does that even mean? No - don't explain. I don't care. That's not a business plan. Why am I supposed to work with you on... whatever this is?"
entries.zh:
"该做的事。\"他投来一个能把人看矮半截的眼神，\"我是说，去做。"

"这话到底什么意思？不——别解释。我不在乎。那不算商业计划。我凭什么要跟你一起干...不管你这是在干什么？"

entries.en:
"Really?" He looks at the TriPad again. "Smuggling weapons is more profitable than I thought. And easier, in the current chaos, which contributes to point A."

"Seems like a bad move to quit while we're ahead."

He pauses, looking you over. Looking displeased. Arroyo's frown grows.

"Fine. If you insist, I'll pull the plug - but you have to cover my expenses to pivot the operation. Call it 80,000 credits. Maybe I can sell the extra stock to pirates. Or the Pathers."

"Bet you'd like that," he says under his breath.
entries.zh:
"真的？\"他又看了一眼 TriPad。\"走私军火比我原来想的更赚。而且眼下这乱局让这事更容易——这又正好印证了第一点。"

"正赚着的时候收手，看着可不是好主意。"

他顿了顿，上下打量你。一脸不快。Arroyo 的眉头越皱越紧。

"行。既然你坚持，我就把这摊收了——但你得补我转手生意的开销。就算 80,000 星币。那批多出来的货，说不定能卖给海盗。或者卖给那些左径分子。"

"你肯定乐意看到这个，"他低声嘟囔。

entries.en:
Arroyo's TriPad chimes confirmation of the credits transfer.

"Huh. You really paid." He looks away, brow furrowed.

"Fine. A deal is a deal. Now get out of here before you sell me some other stupid idea."
entries.zh:
Arroyo 的 TriPad 叮咚一响，确认星币转账已完成。

"哼。你还真付了。"他移开目光，眉头拧着。

"行。说好的就是说好的。现在赶紧走，别又给我灌什么蠢主意。"

entries.en:
"Really?"

He gives you a questioning look, then examines his TriPad again.

"The numbers are good. I'm making a nice profit. What's the problem?"
entries.zh:
"真的？"

他狐疑地看了你一眼，又低头去看他的 TriPad。

"账面上的数很好看。我赚得不少。有什么问题？"

o.en: It's not about credits, it's about results.

entries.en:
"It's not about credits? What else is could it be about? Actually, don't answer. I don't care."

He crosses his arms.

"But okay. Fine. The only way I'm going to agree is if you cover my expenses to pivot the operation. Let's call it 80,000 credits."
entries.zh:
"跟星币无关？那还能跟什么有关？算了，别回答。我不在乎。"

他抱起双臂。

"不过好吧。行。要我答应，唯一的办法是你出钱补我转手这摊生意的开销。就算 80,000 星币吧。"

entries.en:
"My answer is no."

He looks thoughtful. "It's not even about the credits. It's about the principle of making a decision about my business and owning it. If this," he flaps a hand, "is how you run your business, more power to you. Let me know how it turns out."

Arroyo crosses his arms. He's not going to budge.
entries.zh:
"我的回答是不。"

他若有所思。"这甚至跟星币无关。这是原则问题：我自己的生意，我自己拿主意，自己担着。要是你，"他摆了摆手，"就是这么打理生意的，那祝你顺风。结果如何，回头告诉我一声。"

Arroyo 抱起双臂。他不会松口。

o.en: I want you to assist Hector, the true heir to Andrada. (transfer credits)
o.zh: 我要你去扶助 Hector，Andrada 真正的继承人。 (移交星币)

entries.en:
"That ice-cold puppet of Gens Kato?"

Arroyo holds his look of contempt for just a moment. His TriPad pings as the credit transfer is confirmed.

"Sure," he says agreeably. "I'll have my people set up the shell companies."
entries.zh:
"Kato 氏族那个冷冰冰的傀儡？"

那份轻蔑在 Arroyo 脸上停了一瞬。他的 TriPad 叮了一声，星币转账已确认。

"当然，\"他爽快地答应，\"我让人去把那些空壳公司搭起来。"

o.en: I want you to back Achilles' faction. He's a reformer. (transfer credits)
o.zh: 我要你支持 Achilles 那一派。他是个改革者。 (移交星币)

o.en: I want you to help supply the rebel uprisings against the Sindrian Diktat. (transfer credits)
o.zh: 我要你帮忙为反抗辛达强权的各起事提供补给。 (移交星币)

o.en: I want you to stop. Cease operations, pull your support.
o.zh: 我要你停手。收掉生意，撤走支援。

entries.en:
"That raving blowhard?"

Arroyo holds his look of contempt for just a moment. His TriPad pings as the credit transfer is confirmed.

"Sure," he says agreeably. "I'll have my people set up the shell companies."
entries.zh:
"那个满嘴胡话的吹牛货？"

那份轻蔑在 Arroyo 脸上停了一瞬。他的 TriPad 叮了一声，星币转账已确认。

"当然，\"他爽快地答应，\"我让人去把那些空壳公司搭起来。"

entries.en:
"That dumping-ground circus of pirates, zealots, and terrorists?"

Arroyo holds his look of contempt for just a moment. His TriPad pings as the credit transfer is confirmed.

"Sure," he says agreeably. "I'll have my people set up the shell companies."
entries.zh:
"那帮由海盗、狂信徒和恐怖分子凑成的垃圾场马戏团？"

那份轻蔑在 Arroyo 脸上停了一瞬。他的 TriPad 叮了一声，星币转账已确认。

"当然，\"他爽快地答应，\"我让人去把那些空壳公司搭起来。"

entries.en:
"Hrm." Arroyo narrows his eyes. "After all of that?"

He shrugs.

"Good," he says. "I guess."
entries.zh:
"嗯。\"Arroyo 眯起眼，\"说完这么一大套，你就这么算了？"

他耸了耸肩。

"好，\"他说，\"大概吧。"

o.en: Yes, I'm going to lay low and see how it pans out.
o.zh: 对，我会先蛰伏，看看事情怎么发展。
不，我们还是谈谈有哪些选择。

entries.en:
"Play it safe, that's what I'd do."

Arroyo still doesn't seem pleased with you, somehow.
entries.zh:
"稳着来，这是我的做法。"

不知怎么的，Arroyo 看上去还是不太满意你。

entries.en:
"Hmm." Arroyo rubs his beard, thinking.

"Sure. If he's been planning this for ten, maybe twenty cycles... He's launching a new enterprise, he's committed his liquid assets. Customers aren't sure about the new value proposition and branding. The investors must be jumpy."

He looks at you, conceding. "It's an interesting point."
entries.zh:
"嗯。"Arroyo 捻着胡须，思索起来。

"有道理。如果他为此筹划了十年，也许二十年...他是在开张一门新买卖，把流动资金全押了进去。客户对新的价值主张和品牌还没底。投资人一定坐不住。"

他看着你，算是让步。"这个点很有意思。"

entries.en:
"Reward, huh." Arroyo rubs his beard. "You... think Dolos Macario is going to come around on all of this and give you a reward?"

"Wait," he makes a show of searching around, as if there was someone nearby that he overlooked. "Is there some other Macario you're talking about? Who isn't a vindictive monster?"

He stops to give you a look through the comms.

"Don't be stupid. At this point you're lucky if he gives you a quick execution."
entries.zh:
"奖赏，是吗。\"Arroyo 捻着胡须，\"你...觉得 Dolos Macario 会在这件事上转变心意，还给你发奖赏？"

"等等，\"他煞有介事地四下张望，像是在找什么被自己漏掉的近旁之人，\"你说的该不会是另一个 Macario 吧？总不会是那个记仇成性的怪物？"

他停下来，隔着通讯盯着你看。

"别犯傻。到这一步，他肯给你一个痛快的处决，你就该谢天谢地了。"

entries.en:
"A strong leader."

He gives you a withering look. "Okay. I suppose."

"Askonia has seen more corruption and unrest every cycle. The bribes are eating into profits. And where's that Supreme Executor who's supposed to keep the system in line?? Personally I don't find the holos convincing- I've faked better."
entries.zh:
"一位强势的领袖。"

他投来一个能把人看矮半截的眼神。"行吧。我想是吧。"

"Askonia 每个星历年的贪腐和动荡都在加剧。贿赂正在吃掉利润。那位本该管住这个星系的最高元首呢？就我个人而言，那些全息影像一点也说服不了我——我伪造的都比他像样。"

entries.en:
"A strong leader."

He gives you a withering look. "Okay. I suppose."

"Askonia has seen more corruption and unrest every cycle. The bribes are eating into profits. And where's that Supreme Executor that's supposed to keep the system in line? Personally I don't find the holos convincing- I've faked better."
entries.zh:
"一位强势的领袖。"

他投来一个能把人看矮半截的眼神。"行吧。我想是吧。"

"Askonia 每个星历年的贪腐和动荡都在加剧。贿赂正在吃掉利润。那位本该管住这个星系的最高元首呢？就我个人而言，那些全息影像一点也说服不了我——我伪造的都比他像样。"

o.en: Maybe we can figure this out later... (back)
o.zh: 这事也许以后再想吧... (返回)

o.en: Maybe I'll just wait and see what happens...
o.zh: 也许我就先等等，看看会怎么样...

o.en: I'm a profitable business contact, aren't I? That must count for something.
o.zh: 我是个能赚钱的商业伙伴，不是吗？这总该算点什么。

o.en: I'm a profitable business contact, aren't I. That must count for something.
o.zh: 我是个能赚钱的商业伙伴，对吧。这总该算点什么。

entries.en:
After a short silence, and a sigh.

"I suppose. But that's not enough."
entries.zh:
沉默了片刻，然后是一声叹息。

"我想是吧。可这还不够。"

o.en: Macario is distracted - he's trying to run a coup. Now is the time to push.
o.zh: Macario 正分身乏术——他在操办一场政变。现在正是加码的时候。

o.en: Once I prove to Macario he made a mistake he'll reward me - and you.
o.zh: 只要我让 Macario 明白他看错了人，他就会奖赏我——还有你。

o.en: Askonia needs stability, a strong leader, for profits to be ensured. It needs Achilles Andrada.
o.zh: Askonia 需要稳定，需要一位强势的领袖，利润才有保障。它需要 Achilles Andrada。

o.en: Askonia needs stability, a strong leader, for profits to be ensured. It needs Hector Andrada.
o.zh: Askonia 需要稳定，需要一位强势的领袖，利润才有保障。它需要 Hector Andrada。

o.en: Ending Macario's corrupt reign of terror is simply the right thing to do.
o.zh: 终结 Macario 那套贪腐的恐怖统治，本来就是该做的事。

o.en: I want to show Macario why trying to make me his patsy will be his downfall.
o.zh: Macario 想拿我当替罪羊，我要让他明白，这就是他的覆灭之因。

o.en: I want to stop Macario's reign of terror and corruption.
o.zh: 我要终结 Macario 的恐怖统治和贪腐。

o.en: It's an opportunity. One side's downfall provides another's ascension, right?
o.zh: 这是个机会。一边倒下，另一边就能上位，对吧？

o.en: This is an opportunity to make credits from the chaos! (pander)
o.zh: 这场乱局正是赚星币的机会！ (谄媚)

o.en: Askonia's is underutilized. Suppression and uprisings are holding back an economic boom.
o.zh: Askonia 的经济远没有被充分盘活。镇压和暴动压着一场经济繁荣。

o.en: With upheaval comes opportunity. Credits moved. Old deals broken, new deals made.
o.zh: 动荡带来机会。星币在流动。旧约作废，新约签成。

entries.en: "No," he says. "We're not."
entries.zh: "不，\"他说，\"我们没说定。"

entries.en:
He stares at you for a moment.

"Yes, we're agreed. There are credits to be made."

"What's the plan?"
entries.zh:
他盯着你看了片刻。

"对，我们说定了。这生意有星币可赚。"

"计划是什么？"

entries.en:
"Mm. The old Lion hasn't been running a tight ship, it's true."

Arroyo considers this for a moment.

"Instability lowers demand. Low investment in secondary and tertiary sectors... any surplusses invested go to low-return weapons technology - profitable for sections of Tri-Tachyon, sure." He looks over at you. "Not my department and not my portfolio, however. Low return for me. They can crash and burn, for all I care."

"If there's a new chief executive in Askonia, maybe I can get in on the ground floor of new budget allocations."

He rubs his hands together.

"They just need leadership that isn't some drooling idiot..."
entries.zh:
"嗯。那头老狮子掌舵确实不够严。"

Arroyo 琢磨了一下。

"动荡会压低需求。二、三产业投资不足...投出去的盈余都流向了低回报的武器技术——对速子科技的部分部门来说当然赚钱。\"他看过来，\"可那不是我的部门，也不在我的投资组合里。对我来说回报太低。他们烧光、垮掉，我都不在乎。"

"要是 Askonia 换个新的首席执行官，也许我能在新预算分配的起步阶段就插进去。"

他搓了搓手。

"他们只需要一个不是流着口水犯傻的领导人..."

entries.en:
"True," he admits. "It's a high-risk market, but the potential to open new segments is equally high. There'll be some big investments made in bold initiatives."

"Weapons, ships, mercenaries, fuel, supplies - up, up, up."

He also stands up, now, getting excited.

"Supply chain stability will take a short-term hit, but heavy industry futures in stable zones... you can't lose."

Arroyo stops himself and gives you a look. Is that something like respect? He turns away before you're sure.
entries.zh:
"没错，\"他承认，\"这是个高风险的市场，可开出新板块的潜力一样高。会有一批大钱投到大胆的举措上去。"

"武器、舰船、雇佣兵、燃料、补给——涨，涨，涨。"

他也站了起来，兴致上来了。

"供应链的稳定短期内会受些冲击，可稳定地带的重工业期货...稳赚不赔。"

Arroyo 收住话头，看了你一眼。那里面是不是有点类似敬意的东西？你还没看清，他就转开了脸。

entries.en:
Academician Sebestyen taps at a datapad. "Let me look at what we’ve got lined up for you today... Oh." He puts down the datapad and looks to you, confused.

"It's, the, um, Provost Baird wants to speak with you," he says. He picks up the datapad again, examines it, and puts it down.

"In person. Um. As soon as possible."
entries.zh:
Sebestyen 院士敲击着一个数据平板。"让我看看我们今天为你安排了什么... 哦？" 他放下数据平板，困惑地看着你。

"这... 看来 Baird 院长想和你谈谈，" 他一边说着一边拿起数据平板，再次确认一番后又放了下来。

"是当面会谈。对，越快越好。"

entries.en:
Academician Sebestyen taps at a datapad. "Let me look at- Oh." He puts down the datapad.

"I'm sorry captain, you're blocked out of everything until you meet with Provost Baird. I'm, um. She can be... well, you should hear her out at least, right?"

"Um." He clears his throat. "I guess that's everything for now?"
entries.zh:
Sebestyen 院士敲击着数据平板。"让我看看 —— 哦。" 他放下数据平板，面露歉意地说道。

"很抱歉，舰长。在你见到 Baird 院长前，我没法为你提供其他任务。呃，她可能是... 您至少应该听听她的说法，对吧？"

"嗯。" 他清了清嗓子。"我想目前就这些了？"

entries.en: "Welcome back captain, it's good to see you!" Sebestyen says cheerfully.
entries.zh: "欢迎回来，舰长！很高兴见到你！" Sebestyen 高兴地说道。

entries.en:
"What um, um, other business would you like to talk about?" Sebestyen asks cheerfully.
OR
"I, I'm sure we have another item to discuss before wrapping up, don't we?"

Sebestyen looks at you hopefully.
entries.zh:
"那个，呃，您还想谈点、谈点别的什么吗？" Sebestyen 问得兴致勃勃。
OR
"我、我敢说收尾之前咱们还有一桩事没聊完，对吧？"

Sebestyen 满眼期待地望着你。

entries.en:
The comms connect after a moment.

"Oh, hello, it's you!" Your contact almost looks surprised that you're calling, but manages to launch into an upbeat introduction.

"My name is Alviss Sebestyen. The new provost - that is, Provost Baird - assigned me to be your liaison with the academy. I hope you're as excited to work with me as I am to be working with you!"
entries.zh:
短暂等待后通讯接通了。

"哦，你好，是你！" 联络人对你的通话非常惊喜，并进行了非常积极的介绍。

"我是 Alviss Sebestyen。新院长 —— 即 Baird 院长 —— 指派我为你与学院的联络员，合作愉快！"

o.en: Shall we get on with it?
o.zh: 我们可以开始谈正事了吗？

entries.en:
Sebestyen jumps as if he just realized something.

"Captain! You might, ah, I've been authorized to provide you with a Neutrino Detector for the mission. Um, a technical crew is transferring the necessary equipment to your flagship, and," he taps his datapad, "I've sent your sensors officer the documentation."

"We've found the Neutrino Detector very helpful for pinpointing interesting, um, all sorts of things while surveying distant systems. Power sources show up especially well, though sometimes you get a false signal. Oh, and one more thing! We haven't figured out a way to quite close the regenerative loop on the plasma reflector uh... and just be sure to stock extra volatiles in your cargo bay to keep the detector running."
entries.zh:
Sebestyen 仿佛想到了某些事情般地跳了起来。

"舰长！你也许，呃，我被授权为你提供一个{中微子探测器}。嗯，技术人员正在把必要的设备转移到你的旗舰上，并且，" 他敲击着数据平板，"我已经把文档发给了你的传感器技官。"

"我们发现中微子探测器在勘探远方星系时非常有用，它能精确定位，唔，各种有趣的事物。它特别适合用来寻找能量源，不过有时会收到假信号。哦，还有件事！我们还没办法很好地闭合等离子反射器上的正反馈回路... 呃，所以必须在你的货舱里准备好额外的{挥发物}来保持探测器的运行。"

entries.en:
"Oh no, that's quite impossible. I mean, she's ah- that is, I literally can't give you anything until the provost enables your contract code again." Sebestyen holds up his datapad which practically glows with a string of bright DENIED codes. "See?"

"So. Um. A landing slot has been cleared for whenever you're ready."
entries.zh:
"哦，那不太可能。我的意思是，她...呃...总而言之，在院长再次启用你的合同代码前，我不能为您提供任何东西。" Sebestyen 举起数据平板，上面确实闪烁着大写的 "拒绝" 字样，"看到了吗？"

"所以，嗯。一个着陆泊位已经空出来了，等候你随时到来。"

entries.en:
"Right, yes, um." He seems nervous to be meeting a real-life space captain. You wonder idly how he even got this position.

"...different departments within the Galatia Academy tell me what they need done, then I coordinate with freelancers like yourself to procure, uh, the necessary services. Oh, and I run jobs by the finance office. We have to make sure you get paid; that's very important."

"At any time there may be various jobs open to you, you just have to check with me. Or sometimes there might be no jobs if they’re all fulfilled." He reads something on a tablet, "But um, it looks like Provost Baird wants you to have first priority. She must like you."

You're not so sure of this.
entries.zh:
"哦对，是的，嗯。" 正面面对一位太空舰长，他显得有些紧张。你漫不经心地想着他到底是怎么坐上这个位置的。

"...Galatia 学院里每个不同的部门会告诉我他们需要做什么，然后我再和像你一样的自由职业者联系，以取得，呃，必要的服务。哦，我还会干财务科的事。我们会确保你拿到钱的；这很重要。"

"随时都可能会有各种各样的任务对你敞开，你只要来我这确认一下。不过有时任务全都被完成了的话就没了。" 他读了读数据平板上的东西，"但是呃，看来 Baird  院长想给你优先待遇。她肯定很中意你。"

这你倒不太确定。

entries.en: He taps at a datapad. "Let me look at what we’ve got lined up for you today... "
entries.zh: 他轻敲数据平板。"让我看看我们今天为你准备了什么任务..."

entries.en:
"Great! Is there anything else I can do for you today?"
OR
"Wonderful! I'll transmit the relevant information."
OR
"Good to hear. I'll make sure you have everything you need."
OR
"Always a pleasure to work with you, captain."
OR
"Glad to hear it! Is there anything else you need?"
entries.zh:
"好的！还有什么能为你效劳的吗？"
OR
"非常好！我会传达相关消息的。"
OR
"听起来不错。我会确保你有所需的一切。"
OR
"很高兴与你共事，舰长。"
OR
"乐意之至！你还需要其他的吗？"

entries.en:
He looks a bit crestfallen, but makes an effort to put on a smile. "Do let me know if you change your mind!"
OR
"Oh," he says, disappointed for a moment. But he quickly cheers up, "Maybe something else?"
OR
"Um, of course. I understand completely." Sebestyen rapidly scans his datapad, "Let's see what else there is here... "
OR
"Great! You can- " he seems to realize that you declined the mission after a moment.

"You don't want to do it? Oh. Okay. Well. Maybe," he taps his datapad on his desk, "Maybe we can find something else for you?"
entries.zh:
他看上去有些沮丧，但仍努力挤出微笑。"如果你改变主意，一定要告诉我！"
OR
"哦，" 他说道，失望了一会儿。但他很快振作起来，"也许还有别的可能？"
OR
"嗯，当然。我完全了解。" Sebestyen 扫了一眼他的数据平板，"让我们看看还有什么..."
OR
"可以的，你能做到 ——" 他似乎意识到你不久就取消了任务。

"你不想做这个吗？噢。好吧。也许，" 他点击了桌上的数据平板，"也许我们能为你找到别的任务？"

entries.en: You open comms to Academician $personLastName.
entries.zh: 你接通了 $personLastName 院士的通讯链接。

entries.en: "So those sound nice. Interested in anything?"
entries.zh: "这些看起来都不错，有什么感兴趣的吗？"

entries.en: He can't help but put on a glowing smile.
entries.zh: 他忍不住露出灿烂的笑容。

entries.en: "Oh, that's too bad. It looks like there aren’t any current requests," he says. He sounds genuinely sorry for you, but manages to perk up, "Maybe next time?"
entries.zh: "哦，很遗憾。当前似乎没有任何请求。" 他说道。他的声音听起来为此感到非常抱歉，但最终振作起来，"也许你改天再来？"

entries.en:
"Ah," says Sebestyen. You can tell instantly that he has some kind of bad news. "... Captain $playerName," he says, then fakes a small cough to delay the inevitable.

"It is good to see you. Um. It's always good to see you. The provost, however," he coughs again, then leans close. "She's, um, put a... hold on your contract code." He turns his datapad for you to see; it's lit up with bright DENIED alerts.

"So." He taps his fingers on the console. "Everything is going well for you?"
entries.zh:
"哦。" Sebestyen 一开口你就知道他有些坏消息要说了，"... $playerName 舰长。" 他说道，然后咳嗽了一声。

"很高兴见到你。嗯。见到您总是很高兴。可是，院长她..." 他又咳嗽了一声，凑了过来，"她，呃...暂停了你的合同代码。" 他把数据平板展示给你看；"拒绝" 字样的警告闪烁在屏幕上。

"所以。" 他在终端上敲击着手指，"你一切都还顺利吗？"

entries.en: "I have just the one request here. $mh_firstInlineBlurb", he looks to you expectantly, "It's yours if you want it."
entries.zh: "我这只有一个任务。$mh_firstInlineBlurb " $heOrShe期待地看着你，"如果你需要，它就是你的。"

entries.en: "Wonderful!" Sebestyen says, unable to suppress  his smile. "I'll just fill this out for you..."
entries.zh: "太好了！" Sebestyen 说道，抑制不住嘴角的笑容，"我这就帮您填好这个..."

entries.en: "Fantastic!" Sebestyen beams a smile at you. "That's so, so... you're a very generous captain, um, captain. This will do so much to provide for our students who don't come from families of means..."
entries.zh: "太棒了！" Sebestyen 向你展露出一个灿烂的笑容，"这真是，真是...您真是位慷慨的舰长，呃，舰长。这将极大地帮助那些出身贫寒的学子..."

entries.en:
"I, I, I-" Sebestyen gapes, at a loss for words at your generosity.

You patiently allow him a few moments to recover, because he needs them.

"I, of course, yes, absolutely captain. Wow! This is incredible! I don't know what to say." He looks around, smiling, and a bit dazed.
entries.zh:
"我，我，我 ——" Sebestyen 结巴地说，因你的慷慨而一时语塞。

你耐心地给予他片刻平复的时间，因为他确实需要。

"我，当然，是的，绝对是的舰长。天啊！这太不可思议了！我不知道该说什么好。" 他环顾四周，微笑着，有些恍惚。

entries.en: "Ah, I- of course, yes." Sebestyen taps a key, closing the work he already started. "If you change your mind, just let me know at any time."
entries.zh: "啊，我 —— 当然，好的。" Sebestyen 轻触了一个按键，关闭了正在进行的工作，"如果你改变主意了，随时可以告诉我。"

entries.en: "Oh!" He looks at his terminal for a moment. "You have an opportunity to, um, is there some particular cause you would like to promote through your scholarship trust? As the patron, it's up to you."
entries.zh: "噢！" 他看了会终端机，"你有机会，呃，是否希望通过奖学金基金支持某项特定事业？作为资助人，这完全由你决定。"

o.en: I wish to help those who cannot afford to attend the Academy on their own.
o.zh: 我希望帮助那些无力独自承担学院学费的人。

entries.en:
"Oh, that's very good of you! ...Which I said, uh, already."

He's nearly flailing his hands. "But, that is, I myself benefitted from just such a scholarship, so I know how it is to be... to be given this chance, and, um. Sorry captain, I uh," his voice cracks and he wipes his eyes.

"Must be... something in the atmo system. Sorry, um," he taps at his terminal, with a sniffle. "There. All set."
entries.zh:
"噢，您真是太好了！...我刚才，呃，好像说过这话了。"

他几乎手舞足蹈起来。"但，那个，我自己就曾受益于这样的奖学金，所以我深知被给予这个机会意味着什么...并且，嗯，抱歉舰长，我，呃..." 他的声音哽咽，擦了擦眼睛。

"一定是...空调系统里有东西。抱歉，嗯，" 他吸着鼻子敲击终端，"好了。全部设置完毕。"

o.en: Space exploration, to recover old knowledge and discover new.
o.zh: 太空探索，以寻回失落的知识并发现新事物。

entries.en:
"Oh, adventurous! I would expect nothing less from a dashing spacer captain," he says happily, tapping away at his terminal. "Nothing easier. Um, except all the exploration work of course. Very difficult. And, oh, possibly dangerous. But you know what I... uh, what I mean is, you're all set!"

He smiles.
entries.zh:
"噢，充满冒险精神！对一位英姿飒爽的太空舰长来说，这正是意料之中的选择，" 他愉快地说着，一边快速敲击着终端，"没有比这更简单的了。呃，当然除了所有实际的探索工作。那非常困难。而且，哦，可能还很危险。但您明白我的... 呃，我的意思是，全部设置完成！"

他微笑着。

o.en: I want to promote AI research, as a powerful tool for humanity to use.
o.zh: 我希望推动 AI 研究，将其作为人类可用的强大工具。

entries.en:
"Oh, um, interesting," he says. "We're going to have to, um. You understand that the Hegemony has certain..."

He coughs; a transparent excuse to not finish his sentence.

"It all comes down to the wording, don't worry." He taps away at the terminal for a minute. "There. That should make everyone happy." He smiles.
entries.zh:
"噢，呃，很有意思，" 他说道，"我们必须，呃...你知道 霸主 有某些..." 他轻咳一声，显然是为了回避说完这句话。

"关键在于措辞，别担心。" 他忙活了一分钟来敲击终端，"好了。这样应该就能让各方都满意了。" 他微笑道。

o.en: I want to promote AI research, as a partnership between conscious minds.
o.zh: 我希望推动 AI 研究，作为有意识心智间的伙伴关系。

entries.en:
"Oh, um, interesting," he says. "We're going to have to, um. You understand that the Hegemony has certain..."

He coughs; a transparent excuse to not finish his sentence.

"It all comes down to the wording, don't worry." He taps away at the terminal for a minute. "There. That should make everyone happy." He smiles.
entries.zh:
"噢，呃，很有意思，" 他说道，"我们必须，呃...你知道 霸主 有某些..." 他轻咳一声，显然是为了回避说完这句话。

"关键在于措辞，别担心。" 他忙活了一分钟来敲击终端，"好了。这样应该就能让各方都满意了。" 他微笑道。

o.en: Study of the Luddic Word so students will remember their connection to Creation.
o.zh: 研究卢德的圣言，以让学生们铭记他们与造物主的联系。

entries.en:
"Luddic? Oh yes, of course. I just-" He flashes an awkward smile, then drops it after he realizes it's not clear why he should be smiling so much.

"It's, that's just... unexpected. We can just, uh, there you go," he says, tapping at his terminal.
entries.zh:
"卢德？哦对，当然。我只是 ——" 他露出尴尬的笑容，随即意识到没有理由如此发笑，便随即收起了笑容。

"这，只是...有点意外。我们就这样，呃，好了，" 他说着，一边敲击着终端。

o.en: The Gate system. We need to recover what was lost.
o.zh: 星门系统，我们需要寻回失落的遗产。

entries.en:
"Oh! Um." Sebestyen's expression flutters away from... something. You can see him making a conscious effort to present a blandly pleasant countenance.

"What an interesting idea," he coughs, and clears his throat. "I'll just... there, it's done."
entries.zh:
"噢！呃。" Sebestyen 的表情从...某种情绪中飘忽移开。你能看出他在刻意摆出一副平淡愉悦的面容。

"真是有趣的想法，" 他轻咳一声，清了清嗓子，"我这就...好了，完成了。"

o.en: Weapons research. And I want results I can exploit as soon as possible.
o.zh: 武器研究，而且我需要能够尽快利用的成果。

entries.en:
"Oh," he hides his disappointment well. "Um, of course. An interesting choice. I'll just... there. We're all set."

He forces a smile.
entries.zh:
"噢，" 他很好地掩饰了自己的失望，"呃，当然。真是个有趣的选择。我这就...好了。全部设置完毕。"

他挤出了一个微笑。

o.en: Could you help me set up a scholarship trust for promising students?
o.zh: 你能帮我为有潜力的学生设立一个奖学金基金吗？

o.en: Baird told me to talk to you about setting up a scholarship...
o.zh: Baird 让我来跟你谈谈设立奖学金的事...

entries.en: "On behalf of the Galatia Academy," Sebestyen says, "-its faculty, students, and um, administrators, I wish to offer you my heartfelt thanks for your contribution to the future of humanity."
entries.zh: "我谨代表 Galatia 学院，" Sebestyen 说道，"—— 包括其教职员工、学生，以及，呃，行政人员，衷心感谢您为人类未来作出的贡献。"

entries.en: "On behalf of the Galatia Academy," Sebestyen says, "-its faculty, students, and um, administrators, I wish to offer you my heartfelt thanks for your contribution to the future of humanity."
entries.zh: "我谨代表 Galatia 学院，" Sebestyen 说道，"—— 包括其教职员工、学生，以及，呃，行政人员，衷心感谢您为人类未来作出的贡献。"

entries.en: "On behalf of the Galatia Academy," Sebestyen says, "-its faculty, students, and um, administrators, I wish to offer you my heartfelt thanks for your contribution to the future of humanity."
entries.zh: "我谨代表 Galatia 学院，" Sebestyen 说道，"—— 包括其教职员工、学生，以及，呃，行政人员，衷心感谢您为人类未来作出的贡献。"

entries.en:
"What a wonderful idea, captain!" Sebestyen starts tapping away at his terminal, pulling up forms.

"I feel, um, personally," he says, "that giving a chance to the brilliant up-and-coming minds of the next generation is perhaps the noblest thing someone of means can do to contribute to, to you know. Our future?"

He clears his throat.

"So, it's only really worth doing if we can put at least 100,000 credits into a trust..." He watches through the link to see how you react.

You have $player.creditsStrC available.
entries.zh:
"绝妙的主意，舰长！" Sebestyen 开始敲击终端以调取表格。

"我个人，呃，认为，" 他说道，"给予下一代杰出的新锐人才以机会，或许是富有者能为，你知道的，我们的未来所作的最高尚的贡献？"

他清了清嗓子。

"所以，只有当我们能向信托基金注入至少 100,000 星币时，这件事才真正值得做..." 他透过通讯链接观察着你的反应。

你目前持有 $player.credits 星币。

o.en: I'll give 100,000 credits. For our future.
o.zh: 我将捐赠 100,000 星币，为了我们的未来。

o.en: Let's talk about setting up a scholarship again...
o.zh: 让我们再谈谈设立奖学金的事...

entries.en:
"Of course, I'm more than happy to discuss a scholarship." Sebestyen starts tapping away at his terminal, pulling up the required forms.

"You have the chance to provide real opportunities to the up-and-coming minds of the next generation, a truly noble cause!"

He clears his throat. "So, um. It's only really worth doing if we can put at least 100,000 credits into a trust..."

You have $player.creditsStrC available.
entries.zh:
"当然，我非常乐意讨论奖学金的事宜。" Sebestyen 开始敲击终端以调取所需的表格。

"你有机会为下一代的新锐人才提供真正的机遇，这实在是崇高的事业！"

他清了清嗓子。"那么，呃，这值得做的前提是我们至少能将 100,000 星币投入基金..."

你目前持有 $player.credits 星币。

o.en: I'll give 100,000 credits. For our future.
o.zh: 我将捐赠 100,000 星币，为了我们的未来。

entries.en: A very well-dressed $manOrWoman is regaling the subdued bartender with complaints about a missed transport of some kind.
entries.zh: 一位衣着考究的$manOrWoman正为一趟错过的行程之类的事大吐苦水，以此 '招待' 着闷不吭声的酒保。

entries.en:
You meet the VIP on the way out the airlock to a waiting private shuttle. It seems the politick thing to do, especially because the promised payment just cleared.

"The commander here," $heOrShe indicates the officer you assigned to the VIP (an officer-trainee, in fact, who drew the short straw and was given a fancy uniform), "Performed acceptably, such that I might endorse a commendation."

With that, $heOrShe says merely, "Captain," then turns on $hisOrHer heel and exits the ship, the small fleet of $hisOrHer luggage wheeling itself behind obediently. The airlock seals mercifully shut.
entries.zh:
在离开气闸前往穿梭机的路上，你遇到了 VIP。这似乎是某些政治上的事情，尤其是因为之前许诺的付款刚刚结清了。

"这位指挥官，" $heOrShe指的是你指派给 VIP 的军官 (实际上，那不过是一名不幸抽中签的军官培训生，只是套上了一身花哨的制服)，"表现尚可，鉴于此，我或许会签署一项表彰。"

说完，$heOrShe只是抛下一句 "舰长"，就直接转身离开了这艘船，身后的行李像小型舰队一样恭恭敬敬地自动跟随。谢天谢地，气闸总算是关上了。

entries.en: You're unable to safely deliver your very important passenger right now.
entries.zh: 你现在无法安全地运送 VIP。

o.en: Try to calm the well-dressed $manOrWoman bothering the bartender
o.zh: 试着让那个衣着考究的$manOrWoman冷静下来，别再纠缠酒保

entries.en:
You manage to insert yourself into the $manOrWoman's field of attention with a friendly greeting. The bartender gives you a thankful nod behind $hisOrHer back.

"These people, these space-pilots, are so addled by rocket fuel and zero-g that they simply cannot comprehend respectful! Customer! Service!"

Each of these three words is accompanied by an open handed slap on the bar. You watch as a small splash leaps over the rim of an otherwise untouched drink at each impact.
entries.zh:
你友善地打了个招呼，顺势吸引了那个$manOrWoman的注意。酒保趁着$hisOrHer转身的时候感激地向你点头道谢。

"这些人，这些太空飞行员，全都给火箭燃料和零重力灌糊涂了！他们根本不懂什么叫尊重！顾客！服务！"

最后的三个词，每个都伴随着对方的巴掌狠狠地拍在吧台上。你看着每次拍击过后，旁边那杯本就没动过的酒水都有小小的浪花飞溅出杯缘。

o.zh: 展现一下你的领导魅力

entries.en:
You put on a look of stern and stoic authority, that look your bridge officers whisper about as your 'captain face' when they think you can't hear them.

This seems to do the trick.

This individual - wealthy, important, and well-connected, by their own description - paid $avipt_reward credits upfront for priority transport within $avipt_timelimit days to $avipt_marketName, but the ship left port early last night without a word for reasons you cannot fathom. This is 'a shocking disgrace' which 'besmirches the already dubious name of all space-captainry'.

You nod, your expression suitably grim at hearing of such terrible treatment.
entries.zh:
你摆出一副严肃沉稳的威严神情，就是那个被舰桥军官私下称为 "舰长脸" 的样子。

看来这招很管用。

这位自称家财万贯、名声显赫且人脉广阔之人士，已经预先支付了 $avipt_reward 星币，要求在 $avipt_timelimit 天内专程前往 $avipt_marketName。然而，预定的舰船却在昨晚悄然离港，连任何能让你为其辩解的音讯都没留下。这完全是 "一桩骇人听闻的丑闻"，让 "全体太空舰长本就狼藉不堪的声誉再次雪上加霜"。

听罢这段糟糕的经历，你点了点头，脸上适时浮现出凝重而同情的神色。

o.en: Offer to transport the VIP for the same fee
o.zh: 提出以相同费用为 VIP 提供运输服务

o.en: Try to withdraw from the conversation
Explain to the VIP that they probably deserved this
o.zh: 向 VIP 解释为什么$hisOrHer活该被撇下

entries.en:
Your offer manages to stop the $manOrWoman from talking at you for several seconds as $heOrShe considers your demeanor and your offer.

"I accept," $heOrShe says with the enunciation of royalty, "Though I shall only be paying after we arrive at $avipt_marketName. And I shall require some of your crew to handle my luggage. I need not remind you that these are my valuable personal goods, not crates of... of common space-bolts to be tossed about by half-drunken dockworkers."

As you confirm final details over a free round from the bartender, you consider which of your junior officers to assign to babysitting duty...
entries.zh:
在$heOrShe考虑你的举止和提议的时候，你的提议让$manOrWoman沉默了几秒钟。

"我接受，" $heOrShe带着皇室般的口吻说道，" 然而我只有在我们到达 $avipt_marketName 后才会付款。我要求你们的船员来帮我搬运行李。我应该不需要提醒你，这些是我的贵重个人物品，不是什么...什么喝得半醉的码头工人能随意扔来扔去的一箱箱普通太空螺栓。"

在酒保为你免费倒酒时，你确认了最终细节，同时考虑着要指派哪位下级军官去当保姆...

entries.en:
You stand as if at attention, give the alleged VIP a formal farewell, and march to the other end of the bar without a backward glance.

$HeOrShe is too confused by your formality to express outrage until it is too late and you are well out of range.

From the corner of your eye, you can see the well-dressed $manOrWoman slowly start working $himOrHerself into another, slightly different rage.
entries.zh:
你站姿端正，仿佛在立正敬礼，向这位所谓的 VIP 致以正式道别，随后径直走向酒吧的另一头，全程没有回头。

直到你已走远，超出$HeOrShe的视线范围，这位 VIP 才从你过于正式的态度中反应过来，想要表达愤怒却为时已晚。

用眼角的余光，你能看到那位衣着考究的$manOrWoman又一次陷进了愤怒里，不过这一次火气稍稍换了副模样。

o.en: Avert your eyes before you are forced to re-engage
o.zh: 别过头去，免得惹火烧身。

entries.en:
The VIP stares at you, appalled at your manners. Behind, the bartender is doing an admirable job suppressing a grin.

The well-dressed $manOrWoman, confronted directly, seems to be at a complete loss. $HisOrHer mouth opens, then closes, opens again - and then $heOrShe storms out of the bar.

There's a pause as your ears adjust to the relatively muted din of the establishment before cheers and hurrahs erupt from the other patrons.
entries.zh:
这位 VIP 盯着你，对你的举止感到震惊。身后的酒保正努力忍笑，做得十分巧妙。

面对你的直接回应，这位衣着考究的$manOrWoman似乎彻底不知所措。$heOrShe嘴巴张了张，又闭上，接着再次张开 —— 随后便怒气冲冲地冲出了酒吧。

你的耳朵先适应了这家场所相对减弱的嘈杂声，片刻安静过后，其他顾客爆发出一阵欢呼与喝彩。

entries.en:
Your connection is accepted immediately. An assistant appears, and they seem to recognize you without the need for introduction. "Just a moment $PlayerSirOrMadam, the Provost will be with you shortly."

After a short wait, the comms open to Provost Baird in her office. She takes just a moment to finish with some work on another holoscreen then turns to you.

"Ah, $playerName. What brings you to me at this hour?"
entries.zh:
你的通讯立即被接通了。你看到一位助手，对方看起来不需要你自我介绍就认出了你。"请稍等片刻 $PlayerSirOrMadam，院长很快就会来。"

又等了片刻，通讯被接通到了在办公室里的 Baird 院长。她花了些时间完成另一个全息屏上的工作，接着转向你。

"啊，$playerName。你这个时间点来找我是有什么事呢？"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted by an automated responder.

"You've reached the offices of Provost Anahita Baird. To secure a number in the appointment queue, please inquire with your administrative contact. This call will be terminated in three seconds."

The machine is true to its word.
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被自动应答器接受了。

"您已连接至 Anahita Baird 院长的办公室。请联系您的行政联系人以取得预约队列号码。该通话将于三秒后结束。"

这机器还真是言出必行。

entries.en:
The junior agent leads you through a series of back hallways and secure lifts toward the administrative suite occupied by Provost Baird at the core of the station.

You are led past diamond-matrix windows through which you can see vistas of the curving internal canyons of Galatia Academy Station. The light dims, and you approach the waiting room of the office of the provost. It is filled with representatives of the most well-connected of the Persean Sector, whose eyes focus on you, the interloper, like the beam array of a Paladin PD system.

The self-assured march of the junior agent seems to project the impression that you're performing some adjutant role - your presence is immediately ignored.
entries.zh:
这位初级代理带着你穿过一系列的走廊和安全电梯，向着空间站中心 Baird 院长的办公室走去。

你被领着走过金刚石方窗，透过它们你可以看到 Galatia 学院空间站弯曲绵延的内部凹凸结构。光线渐暗，你来到了院长办公室的等候区。里面都是英仙座星域名门望族的代表，他们的目光就像保卫者 PD 系统一样聚焦在你这位闯入者身上。

初级代理自信的步伐让你看起来就像个副手 —— 你立刻被忽略了。

entries.en:
"Ah, Captain $playerName." Provost Anahita Baird taps something away on her desk interface and turns to address you.

"I am pleased that you've come to meet with me. And for all the work you've done for my project already."

She lowers her head just a degree, "You didn't think I'd be wasting your time with make-work, did you?" She considers this for a moment, "Well, there was some. Noise had to be introduced to the system to ensure that an outside observer would not immediately identify you as my agent."
entries.zh:
"啊，$playerName 舰长。" Anahita Baird 院长在她的办公桌界面上敲了敲什么，然后转身对你说。

"我很高兴你能来见我。也感谢你到目前为止为我的项目所做的一切。"

她微微低下了头，"你不会认为我要用杂活来浪费你的时间吧？" 她考虑了一小会儿，"嗯，当然之前是有一些，不过主要是为了在各种情报中制造杂音，以确保学院外的观察者不会立即察觉到你是为我办事的。"

entries.en:
"Which brings us to the subject I wish to discuss. Please, make yourself comfortable."

Baird motions to a set of seats around a table carved from the root structure of some great tree. Hand-carved by the looks of it. The work of Luddic artisans.

"They do fine work," she says, "Whatever their misplaced devotion."

She clasps her hands together, turning to business. "You've proven you can be trusted. So now I ask that you take a more active role in my great work."
entries.zh:
"这就不得不提我接下来要讲的这件事。请坐，放松点。"

Baird 看向一边的座椅，示意你坐下，这些座椅围绕着一张由某种大树的根部结构雕刻而成的桌子，看上去是卢德工匠手工雕刻的作品。

"他们的手艺很精妙，" 她说，"尽管那份虔诚用错了地方。"

她十指交叉，谈回到正事上。"你已经证明自己值得信任。所以现在我希望你在我的宏伟事业中发挥更积极的作用。"

o.zh: 那么，这项 '伟大工作' 是什么呢？

entries.en:
"Saving the Persean Sector." She is content to let the words hang in the air for a moment.

"I don't ask that you like me and I won't make a sanctimonious appeal to emotion. What I ask is that you recognize, rationally, that I am pursuing a course of action unburdened by factional demands. Indeed, this will be the foremost effort to ensure the survival of our civilization from utter collapse."

"We will not be saved by a retreat to homesteads on fragile balls of rock, nor by an arms race which throws precious resources into the fires of interfactional squabbling. We have to reach beyond the known, develop theories that shatter all that has come before, and apply radical new technologies to ensure our survival. We must reach further and higher than the Domain ever dared!" As she speaks, she raises her eyes up toward some abstraction.

This, you think, is something she believes in.
entries.zh:
"拯救英仙座星域。" 她让这句话在你脑中回响了好一会儿。

"我不需要你喜欢我，我也不是要假惺惺地打感情牌。我要的是你理性地认识到，我正追求一条不为任何势力所干扰的行动路线。事实上，这将是确保我们的文明免于彻底崩溃的前提。"

"龟缩回脆弱岩球上的家园里无法拯救我们，把宝贵的资源扔进势力冲突的火堆中也无法拯救我们。我们必须超越已知的边界，建立起粉碎旧时代造物的新理论，并运用革命性的新技术来确保生存。我们必须超越 人之领 的成就！" 当她说话时，目光投向上方，就像是看着那抽象的概念。

你感觉，这就是她所笃信的对象。

entries.en:
"What matters is that once the mess was finally cleared up, the Hegemony descended on the Galatia Academy with a technological inspection fleet. They tore the place apart, arrested the heads of the hyperphysics department and several labs, and of course took Provost Kallichore in for questioning."

She turns away. "And, with little delay, sentencing."

"He was a fool, and too trusting," Baird says with contempt. "We lost good people and good research. Scientific breakthroughs are built on the development of theory and, yes, even negative results."
entries.zh:
"重要的是，当这个烂摊子最终收拾干净的时候，霸主就派遣了科技审查舰队来到 Galatia 学院。他们把这个地方拆得七零八落，逮捕了超空间物理学部门和几个实验室的负责人，当然还有 Kallichore 院长，一并抓去审问。"

她面向一旁。"然后，几乎马上就判刑了。"

"他是个傻瓜，而且太信任别人了，" Baird 轻蔑地说。"我们失去了优秀的人和优秀的研究资料。科学突破建立在理论发展上以及，没错，甚至是负面的成果。"

entries.en:
"I need you to recover Kallichore's secret archive. We need his data from that experiment, and all the others that led up to it. The Hegemony will have kept it. They keep everything. Evidence, you see."

"We shall also need Academician Scylla Coureuse. She was a hyperspace physics researcher, the keystone of the theory team behind the jump-point experiments. The Hegemony, small-minded as they are, only arrested team leaders in the first sweep. They didn't understand that the underlying theory being tested was largely written by one particular academician who was... not suitable for leadership."

"I need you to find her."
entries.zh:
"我需要你找回 Kallichore 的秘密档案。我们需要他那次实验的数据，以及所有导致那次实验的其他前置数据。霸主肯定会把这些资料留在手上。他们保存一切。作为证据，你懂的。"

"此外我们还需要 Scylla Coureuse 院士。她是一位超空间物理学研究员，跳跃点实验背后理论小组的基石。霸主向来目光短浅，在一开始只逮捕了项目负责人。他们想不到，当时测试的基础理论主要是由一位... 不适合担任领导的院士撰写的"

"我需要你找到她。"

o.en: How can I get the Kallichore Archive from the Hegemony?
o.zh: 我怎样才能从 霸主 手上拿到 Kallichore 的档案？

o.en: Do you have any leads on this Scylla Coureuse?
o.zh: 关于这个 Scylla Coureuse，你有什么线索吗？

entries.en:
"Not at all. I," she says this with emphasis. "I was simply attentive when a certain Tri-Tachyon executive compromised corporate security to advance his career over a rival."

"He understands the value of the deal he made and he has come out ahead compared to the alternative. You will find him quite cooperative."
entries.zh:
"不完全是。我，" 她说这句话时加重了语气，"我只是单纯地注意到一位 速子科技 的高管为了在事业上超过竞争对手而损害了公司安全。"

"他明白这个交易的价值，何况比起其他选择，他已经算是赚的盆满钵满了。你会发现他相当愿意合作。"

entries.en:
"He compromised corporate security to advance his career over a rival. He understands the value of the deal he made with me."

She almost smiles.

"You will find him quite cooperative once you get past his inflated sense of self-importance."
entries.zh:
"他为了在竞争中胜出，不惜损害公司安全来推动自己的职业生涯。他很清楚与我达成的这笔交易的价值。"

她几乎要露出笑容。

"一旦你忽略他那膨胀的自我感，就会发现他其实相当配合。"

o.en: Do you have any leads on this Scylla Coureuse?
o.zh: 你有关于 Scylla Coureuse 的任何线索么？

o.en: How can I get the Kallichore Archive from the Hegemony?
o.zh: 我该如何从 霸主 手上拿到 Kallichore 的档案？

entries.en:
"Of course not."

She puts on a smile that isn't entirely friendly.

"And I would never ask it of you. This is exactly why I want to give you so much leeway- so you can do this your way. The right way. You've shown that it works; I cannot deny the evidence in front of my eyes."
entries.zh:
"当然不了。"

她摆出一个并不完全友好的笑容。

"我也不会要求你这样做。这正是我想给你这么多周旋余地的原因 —— 让你能用你的方法来办事。正确的方法。你已经证明了你方法的可行性；我不能否认放在我眼前的证据。"

entries.en:
"Find the Kallichore Archive. Find Scylla Coureuse. Once you have accomplished both of these missions, the project can proceed to the next phase."

Baird smiles, "And that's when things get exciting."
entries.zh:
"找到 Kallichore 的档案以及 Scylla Coureuse 本人。一旦你完成了这两项任务，项目就可以进入下一阶段。"

Baird 微笑着，继续道，"到那时，事情就会变得有趣了。"

o.zh: 所以这项目到底是什么？

entries.en:
She turns to her desk display and starts inputting a command sequence, done with you for now.

"Good day, captain," she says without looking up, "You may check in with me via comms for additional analysis as the operation develops, though I expect you to use your initiative."

"Oh, and I've re-authorized Academician Sebestyen with mission assignment access for your file. Carrying out his little jobs might be a good cover for your real work, and allows us to funnel additional credits to you."

You feel the subtle movement of air as the doors open silently behind you. Mirror-masked guards flank a junior agent who waits to escort you back to your shuttle.
entries.zh:
她转向她办公桌上的显示器，开始输入某个命令序列，看来她和你的谈话暂时结束了。

"祝你好运，舰长，" 她头也不抬地说，"行动开展的同时，你随时可以通过通讯器与我联系，以获得其他建议，尽管我希望你能更多地发挥你的主观能动性。"

"哦，还有，我已经重新授权 Sebestyen 院士向你发布任务。处理他的琐事应该能很好地掩盖你的真实任务，同时也能让我们有渠道向你输送额外的星币。"

你察觉到一丝动静，门在你身后无声地打开。一位初级代理站在戴着镜面面罩的警卫身边，等待着送你回到穿梭机上。

entries.en: Baird's smile does not reach her eyes. "You'll see."
entries.zh: Baird 笑了，但她的眼睛中却没一丝笑意。"你会知道的。"

entries.en:
"Of course you are."

She smiles, and you almost believe it.

"That's why I asked you to help: the ability to set your feelings aside and view the situation objectively. You know what it takes to lead and to prevail. I've seen it."
entries.zh:
"当然了。"

她微笑着，你差点就相信她的说辞。

"这就是为什么我请你帮忙：你拥有将个人情感放在一旁，客观看待事态的能力。怎么带队，怎么取胜，你心里有数。我很清楚。"

entries.en:
"Ah, the skeptic; of course. As an intellectual, I respect that you don't simply accept my demands due to my authority. I wouldn't have called you here if I wanted an obsequious minion to leap at my every request. I already have those."

"To your question: you would miss out on the opportunity of your life."

She speaks almost casually, like it doesn't matter what you think. But there's an edge to her voice that suggests she does care, very much. "Whatever your feelings, first hear what I have to say and then consider - rationally - what is best. I am confident that you will discover that our interests align."

"So. Hear me out."
entries.zh:
"啊，怀疑主义者；当然。作为一个知识分子，我尊重你不因为我有权力就接受我的要求。如果我想要一个言听计从的谄媚奴才，我也不会叫你来。何况我不缺那种人。"

"现在来回答你的问题：你会错过一生仅有一次的机遇。"

她说得很随意，就像你怎么想并不重要。但她的声音里有一丝紧张，表明她确实在乎，非常在乎。"不管你怎么想，先听听我要说的，然后 —— 理性地 —— 考虑一下何为最佳。我相信你会发现我们的利益是一致的。"

"那么。请听我说完。"

entries.en:
"My predecessor, Provost Tomas Kallichore, led a series of misguided hyperspace manipulation experiments. Ah, how to put it in layman's terms?"

Baird looks troubled to have to do this, sighs, then speaks: "Captain. Your ships fly through hyperspace with special engines. The Gate network of the Domain was similar, but also very different. Kallichore thought there might be a way to use starship hyperdrives to re-open the Gates."

"Obviously it went terribly wrong, and the Galatia system was cut off from hyperspace when the jump-points were disrupted beyond usability. Though we hear some yahoo found a way to cross unstable jump-points; an act well beyond irresponsible considering the chance of a cascading resonance event- ah, I apologize. That is irrelevant."
entries.zh:
"我的前任，Tomas Kallichore 院长，领导了一系列错误的超空间操纵实验。呃，怎么说得通俗一点呢？"

看起来这确实让 Baird 很伤脑筋，她叹了口气，然后开口："舰长，你的舰船全都利用着特殊的引擎以在超空间航行，这和 人之领 的星门网络有点类似，但也非常不同。而 Kallichore 当时认为可能有办法利用星舰的超空间引擎来 重新打开星门。"

"显然这些实验出了大问题，当跳跃点被扰乱到无法使用时，Galatia 星系也与超空间隔绝了。虽然我们听说一些疯子找到了穿越不稳定跳跃点的方法，但考虑到可能引发级联共振事件的风险，这种行为已经不能只用不负责任来形容了 —— 啊，抱歉，这与当前的话题没什么关系。"

entries.en:
"Following the aftermath of the Galatia Experiment, the Hegemony technological inspectors seized everything, all of our records and data."

"The most direct approach would involve accessing the data vaults of the Ministry of Technology Standards. They're who you might call the 'AI Inspectors', and they serve that role, among others, for the Hegemony. It would not be trivial." An amused look crosses her face. "But their security has been breached before..."

"I have an old... acquaintance who has been climbing the Tri-Tachyon executive ladder. His name is Rayan Arroyo, and he is based out of Eochu Bres. He may be compelled to assist us with a human asset on this front. I'll forward you the contact information." She taps for a moment on her desk-interface.
entries.zh:
"Galatia 实验之后。霸主 的科技审查员查封了一切，包括我们所有的数据与记录。"

"最直接的方法是进入科技标准部的数据库。他们是你可能称之为 'AI 稽查员' 的人，并同时在其他职位服役。这可不是小事，" 她看起来有些想笑，"但曾经也有人办到过。"

"我的确有个...老熟人，他在 速子科技 的行政梯队中上升很快。他的名字叫 Rayan Arroyo，在 Eochu Bres 办公。或许我们能说服他在这一目标上提供人力支援。我会把联络信息转发给你。" 她在她的桌面终端上敲了一会儿。

entries.en:
"Let us say that Arroyo's future career opportunities are on the line," she says.

"Mention me to him," she says. "If you are firm but discreet, I believe you will find him more than willing to assist."
entries.zh:
"这么说吧，这事关乎他未来的职业生涯。" 她说道。

"向他报我的名字，" 她接着说，"如果你的态度足够强硬而谨慎，我相信你会发现他非常乐意提供帮助。"

o.en: You want me to blackmail a Tri-Tachyon executive?
o.zh: 你想让我去勒索一位 速子科技 的高管？

entries.en:
Your connection is accepted immediately. A junior assistant appears, and they recognize you without the need for introduction. "Just a moment $PlayerSirOrMadam $playerName," and the display flicks to a holding pattern displaying the crest of the Galatia Academy.

The junior assistant re-appears. "I'm very sorry, but the Provost requests your physical presence for a meeting as soon as possible." Two taps on a datapad, and they continue, "A landing slot has been set aside for your arrival, $PlayerSirOrMadam. I'm sure we will be delighted to see you shortly. Please have a wonderful day."

With that, and you having not spoken a word, the line goes dark.
entries.zh:
通讯立即被接通了。你看到一位下级助手，对方看起来不需要你自我介绍就认出了你。"请稍等片刻 $playerName $PlayerSirOrMadam，" 显示屏闪烁了一下，变为显示着 Galatia 学院徽标的等候界面。

片刻后，那位助手再次出现，"我很抱歉，但是院长要求和您当面会谈，越快越好。" 他在数据平板上按了两下，继续说道，"已经为您专门安排好了一个着陆泊位，$PlayerSirOrMadam。我们很快就能恭候您的光临。祝您愉快。"

就这样，你一句话还没说，通讯线路就中断了。

o.en: What do you need me for?
Point made. What do you need me for?
o.zh: 明白了，那么为什么需要我呢？

o.en: And why should I help you?
I guess we'll just have to see.
o.zh: 那我们只能走一步看一步了。

entries.en:
"Your tasks will not be so simple from here on out. I expect you to self-adapt to circumstances in pursuit of the objectives I lay out. And."

She pauses for a moment, considering, before continuing in a tone colder than before, "No matter what you have to do, as long as you pursue the mission goal, I will see that you are rewarded. Securing the future is worth... everything."
entries.zh:
"从此以后，你的任务就不会这么简单了。我期望你能够紧跟我设定的每一个目标，自己主动地去随机应变。还有..."

她停顿了一会儿，思索些许，然后换上了更为冷厉的语气继续说道："不管你采取了什么你认为必要的措施，只要你贯彻了任务的最终目标，我就会确保你得到报酬。为了确保未来... 一切都值得。"

o.en: I'm not willing to sacrifice all sense of morality for your 'future'.
o.zh: 我不愿意为了你的 '未来' 牺牲我所有的道德底线。

o.en: I'm willing to do whatever it takes to safeguard the future.
o.zh: 为了守住未来，我愿意不惜一切代价。

o.en: And what if I don't want to help you?

entries.en:
"You have proven yourself to be... capable," she says.

"These people," she waves a hand to indicate the Galatia Academy, "are very good at very specific things over which they have obsessed all their lives. But they've kept themselves too long in the ivory tower. They're soft. The world is out there," her voice rises, "And we must change it."

She lowers her voice again, speaking directly to you, "And that is why I need you."
entries.zh:
"你已经证明自己...能力卓越。" 她开口说道。

"这些人，" 她单手一挥，暗指整个 Galatia 学院，"他们心无旁骛，在自己的专业领域有很高的造诣。然而，他们呆在象牙塔里闭门不出，久而久之就变得畏手畏脚，明明大千世界近在眼前。" 她的声音越发高亢，"因而，我们必须做出改变。"

她接着又把声音放低，直接对着你说道："那，就是我需要你的原因。"

entries.en:
"I imagine your self-interest would provide sufficient motivation. As you well know, we pay in credits. The prospect of the continuity of technological civilization is an added benefit, is it not?"

"Unless," she pauses, then looks at you over her AR-spex, speaking evenly, "I've gravely misjudged you, and your heart is set on liquidating your fleet, donating the proceeds to charity, and taking up with a flagellant order on Hesperus... no, I've got it- you've been doing a lot of reading; well, watching dark-channel holovids mostly- and have half a mind to enlist as a political enforcer smashing teeth in for the 1000-cycle reign of the 'Lion of Sindria'. Did I get it right?"

Your shields hold firm under the broadside of sarcasm deployed by the Provost.
entries.zh:
我觉得你的自身利益就是你最好的动力。你明明很懂，我们以信用点支付。反正对你来说，技术文明的传承和延续只是顺便，不是吗？

“除非...” 她顿了一下，一边隔着 AR 眼镜仔细打量着你，一边不紧不慢地说到，“除非我完全看错你了。搞不好其实你心意已决，打算彻底变卖你的舰队，把全部收益捐给施善会，然后去 Hesperus 加入某个自笞者修会...不，我懂了。你看了很多宣传，大部分都是什么地下频道里的全息视频之类的。你现在完全按耐不住自己想要加入政法部队的冲动，要为维护 “辛达瑞亚之狮” 的千年统治而大杀四方。我猜对了么？”

犹如用护盾牢牢地挡下了激烈的侧舷排炮火力一般，你面不改色地接下了院长的一连串冷嘲热讽。

entries.en:
"I imagine your self-interest will provide sufficient motivation. As you well know, we pay in credits. The prospect of the continuity of technological civilization is an added benefit, is it not?"

"Unless," she pauses, then looks at you over her AR-spex, speaking evenly, "I've gravely misjudged you, and your heart is set on liquidating your fleet, donating the proceeds to charity, and taking up with a flagellant order on Hesperus... no, I've got it- you've been doing a lot of reading; well, watching dark-channel holovids mostly- and have half a mind to enlist as a political enforcer smashing teeth in for the next 1000-cycle reign of some new 'Lion of Sindria'. Did I get it right?"

Your shields hold firm under the broadside of sarcasm deployed by the Provost.
entries.zh:
我觉得你的自身利益就是你最好的动力。你明明很懂，我们以信用点支付。反正对你来说，技术文明的传承和延续只是顺便，不是吗？

“除非...” 她顿了一下，一边隔着 AR 眼镜仔细打量着你，一边不紧不慢地说到，“除非我完全看错你了。搞不好其实你心意已决，打算彻底变卖你的舰队，把全部收益捐给施善会，然后去 Hesperus 加入某个自笞者修会...不，我懂了。你看了很多宣传，大部分都是什么地下频道里的全息视频之类的。你现在完全按耐不住自己想要加入政法部队的冲动，要为维护 “辛达瑞亚之狮” 的千年统治而大杀四方。我猜对了么？”

犹如用护盾牢牢地挡下了激烈的侧舷排炮火力一般，你面不改色地接下了院长的一连串冷嘲热讽。

entries.en: "Indeed." She leans back, interpreting your response as a stand-down.
entries.zh: "确实如此。" 她向后靠去，将你的回答视为一种退让。

entries.en:
"Coureuse was always an odd fit. Brilliant, yes, but she had a way of being distracted with involvement in, hmm, antagonistic subcultures." Baird waves a hand, dismissing the matter as sociological fluff. "Perhaps the Hegemony crackdown cured her of that childish affectation."

"Her family and, presumably, friends," you wonder for a moment if Baird has any of those, "-are from Fikenhild, in the Westernesse system. You could start there."
entries.zh:
"Coureuse 一直都是个异类。她确实才华横溢，但她总是会分心于参与...嗯...制造对立的亚文化中。" Baird 挥了挥手，仿佛这些不过是社会学上的细枝末节。"或许 霸主 的镇压使她摆脱了那种幼稚的影响。"

"她的家人，以及想必还有朋友，" 听到这里，你忽然好奇 Baird 自己是否也有这类关系，"都来自 Westernesse 星系的 Fikenhild，你可以从那里开始找。"

entries.en:
Baird thinks for a moment. "If you are observed looking for Coureuse, you may be contacted by others who are looking for her. That could be useful. You could cut a deal, get some leads."

"Alternatively, her department was operating experimental packages in the $gaFC_starName system. We have detected some ongoing telemetry that suggests these instruments are still in use, though it isn't clear by whom." She taps her desk interface, "I've sent you the coordinates."

The provost looks at you over her spectacles. "How do you want to handle this, captain? Are you a diplomat or an explorer? Do you want to find the probes in the $gaFC_starName system or talk your way through this on Fikenhild?"
entries.zh:
Baird 沉思了片刻，"如果有人发现你在寻找 Coureuse，其他也在找她的人可能会联系你。这可能会对你有所帮助。你可以试着做笔交易，换点线索。"

"此外，她所在的部门曾在 $gaFC_starName 星系部署实验组件。我们侦测到某些仍在传回的遥测数据，表明这些仪器仍在使用中，尽管使用者身份不明。" 她轻点桌面界面，"坐标已经发送给你了。"

院长透过眼镜审视着你。"你打算如何处理此事，舰长？是当外交官还是探险家？你是想去 $gaFC_starName 星系搜寻探测器，还是想在 Fikenhild 靠口才解决这件事？"

entries.en:
Baird nods, "Of course. You are, at heart, a... an adventurer, shall we say, aren't you."

"If you want to change your approach, you must let me know so that I can ensure you have all the information you require."
entries.zh:
Baird 点点头，"当然。你本质上是一个...一个冒险家，不是么。"

"如果你想换一个方法，你必须让我知道，这样我才能确保你掌握所有必要的信息。"

entries.en:
Baird nods, "I thought so. There's no problem you don't believe you can talk your way through, is there."

"If you want to change your approach, you must let me know so that I can ensure you have all the information you require."
entries.zh:
Baird 点点头，"我想也是。在你看来，这世上没有不能用你口才解决的问题，对吧。"

"如果你想换一个方法，你必须让我知道，这样我才能确保你掌握所有必要的信息。"

entries.en:
"Your status in the Persean League could be useful. Officials might be willing to assist you. The League intelligence apparatus might even provide assistance." She gives you a knowing look. "If they think they're working for the benefit of the League, that is."

"Alternatively, her department was operating experimental packages in the $gaFC_starName system. We have detected some ongoing telemetry that suggests these instruments are still in use, though it isn't clear by whom." She taps her desk interface, "I've sent you the coordinates."

The provost looks at you over her spectacles. "How do you want to handle this, captain? Are you a diplomat or an explorer? Do you want to find the probes in the $gaFC_starName system or talk your way through this on Fikenhild?"
entries.zh:
"你在 英仙座联盟 的地位或许能派上用场。官员们可能会愿意协助你。联盟情报机构甚至可能会提供支持。" 她投来心照不宣的目光，"前提是他们认为这是在为联盟的利益服务。"

"此外，她所在的部门曾在 $gaFC_starName 星系部署实验组件。我们侦测到某些仍在传回的遥测数据，表明这些仪器仍在使用中，尽管使用者身份不明。" 她轻点桌面界面，"坐标已经发送给你了。"

院长透过眼镜审视着你。"你打算如何处理此事，舰长？是当外交官还是探险家？你是想去 $gaFC_starName 星系搜寻探测器，还是想在 Fikenhild 靠口才解决这件事？"

entries.en:
"When you do find Scylla Coureuse, I expect her to be unwilling to cooperate. I have provided you with an encrypted message. It is an, ah, a personal appeal from myself to her," she says.

"It should prove persuasive."
entries.zh:
"当你真的找到 Scylla Coureuse 时，我预计她不会很配合。我已经向你提供了一份加密信息。这是一个，啊，我以个人名义对她发出的呼吁。" 她说道。

"这应该有些说服力。"

o.zh: 我相信这会起到作用的。

o.en: Will I be blackmailing Coureuse for you?
o.zh: 需要我帮你去威逼利诱 Coureuse 吗？

entries.en:
"You need not be so conspiratorial, captain," Baird admonishes, "Not everything is cloak and dagger, blackmail and bribes."

"Our wayward academician has avoided all contact with the Galatia Academy since the Hegemony arrested her colleagues. I appreciate the rational response to a campaign of scientific suppression, but now she is needed for the role she was always meant to play."
entries.zh:
"你大可不必这么热衷于阴谋论，舰长。" Baird 告诫道，"世上并不只有敲诈勒索和阴谋诡计。"

"自从 霸主 逮捕了她的同事后，我们的这位倔强的学者就避免了与 Galatia 学院的所有接触。我欣赏她对那场压迫科学的运动的理性反应，但现在需要她发挥她应有的作用，一如既往。"

entries.en:
"Indeed," says Baird, looking at you closely. "Her trepidation is a rational response to previous events; the investigations, arrests, the show-trial of Kallichore. But conditions have changed, and she is needed if we are to escape from stagnant local maxima."

Baird turns to the window. "I will call, Scylla will answer," she says. A proclamation?
entries.zh:
"确实，" Baird 说道，一边仔细看着你。"她的惶恐不安是对之前情况的合理反应，Kallichore 被调查、逮捕、公开审判。但现在情况变了，如果我们要突破停滞不前的上限，就必须要找到她。"

Baird 转向窗户。"我将呼吁，而 Scylla 将会响应，" 她说道。这是一句宣告吗？

entries.en:
"As for the prodigy of Galatia..." Baird trails off.

Is that regret? The look quickly disappears.
entries.zh:
"至于 Galatia 的那位奇才..." Baird 欲言又止。

她脸上的是遗憾吗？这个表情很快就消失了。

entries.en: You enter the bar, leaving the noisome propaganda broadcasts of the throughway behind. Off-duty laborers drink away their ration credits dutifully at benches set beneath Diktat insignia. In one corner a cadre of finely dressed officer-bureaucrats calls for another round. Even here, a larger-than-life holo of the Lion of Sindria looks down on you as you decide what to do.
entries.zh: 你进入酒吧，把宣传政治大方向的嘈杂广播抛在了身后。下班的劳动者们聚在 辛达强权 标志下方的长凳上，尽职尽责地喝掉他们的粮票。角落里，一群衣着光鲜的军官和文职人员叫嚣着要再来一轮。就算在这种地方，也有个比真人更伟岸的辛达瑞亚之狮全息投影俯视着你，等着你做出下一步的决定。

entries.en: You enter the bar, leaving the noisome propaganda broadcasts of the throughway behind. Off-duty laborers drink away their ration credits dutifully at benches set beneath the new Diktat insignia. In one corner a cadre of finely dressed officer-bureaucrats calls for another round.
entries.zh: 你走进酒吧，把通道里那吵人的宣传广播关在了身后。歇了工的劳工坐在新换的强权徽记下的长凳上，本分地把配给信用点喝个精光。角落里，一伙衣冠考究的军官官僚又招呼着再来一轮。

entries.en: As you enter the bar you are buffeted by the human white-noise of conversation and revelry. Ad-holos buzz softly from ceiling-mounted units, shining garish highlights through glasses and bottles as spacer crews mingle with merchants and locals trading drinks for rumor, jobs, and opportunities.
entries.zh: 刚踏入酒吧，人群的嘈杂与喧嚣立即扑面而来。天花板上的全息广告装置发出柔和的嗡嗡声，将艳俗的广告铺撒在杯盏交错之间。宇宙民们混杂在生意人和本地人当中，用酒水换取流言、工作和机遇。

entries.en:
As you enter the bar you are buffeted by the white-noise of conversation. A spacer at a cheap table looks at you and shock crosses their face. They nudge the merchant on the seat beside, and point. A hush falls over the bar. The ad-holos buzz softly, shining garish highlights through glasses.

Several groups rise and leave, glaring acidly; one spacer spits at your feet, muttering curses. Your guards' hands find their weapons, but nothing more is necessary. You enter the bar, quieter than you found it; most drinkers do their best to pretend they didn't see you.
entries.zh:
刚踏入酒吧，谈话的喧嚣立即扑面而来。一个坐在廉价吧台后的宇宙民看到了你，脸上不由自主地掠过一丝震惊。他和同伴推了推坐在一旁的商人，还指了指你。一片寂静开始在酒吧里蔓延开来，只有全息广告装置依旧轻声作响，在杯盏之间投射着艳俗的广告。

有几群人起身离开了，临走前不忘酸溜溜地瞪了你一眼。一个宇宙民向你的脚下吐了口唾沫，低声咒骂了一句什么。你的卫兵把手放到了武器上，但暂时没有拔出来的必要。你找到了明显比之前安静了许多的吧台，在你走向那边时，大部分的酒客都尽力假装没看到你。

entries.en: You enter the crowded, well-lit space and take in the rows of taps adorning the wall under bottles from every one of the Core Worlds - and a few from elsewhere. Merchant-captains mingle with off-duty officers at the bar, served efficiently by the uniformed staff. In one corner, a pack of navy cadets shout and sing, desperately enjoying their last work-shift of freedom.
entries.zh: 刚踏入这明亮而拥挤的地方，你的目光就被缀满墙上的一排排酒水龙头吸引过去。龙头上的瓶装酒产地遍布核心世界的每个星球，甚至还有几种出自边缘地带的酒水。商船舰长和休班军官在酒吧里打成一片，穿着制服的工作人员麻利地穿梭其间。在一个角落里，一群海军学员正高唱呐喊，拼命地享受着他们最后一班的自由。

entries.en:
As you enter the bar you are buffeted by the white-noise of conversation. A spacer at a cheap table looks at you with a double-take of recognition. They elbow their drinking companions, stand, and aggressively - unsteadily - approach you. At three meters they halt as they just now spot your guards, who have made themselves less inconspicuous.

"You! You can't go doing what you're doing," the spacer finds words are preferable now to a physical altercation. "Throwing i-pulses at the hyperspace beasties and the ghosties. It's bad luck. Bad, bad luck going shoutin' at things yer not meant to!" They've begun shouting at you, which you feel violates the generalized principle. "-'ll be the death of us all!"

The spacer's comrades, eyeing you, pull their loud companion back toward a quiet corner. A few onlookers make corrupted motions of Luddic blessing; spacer signs against ill-omen.
entries.zh:
刚踏入酒吧，谈话的喧嚣扑面而来。一个坐在廉价吧台后的宇宙民看到了你，脸上不由自主地掠过一丝震惊。他们用手肘顶了顶喝得醉醺醺的同伴，站起身，不怀好意地靠过来。注意到你身边乔装打扮过的警卫后，他们在三米开外的地方停了下来。

"你！你做那些事情是会遭报应的！" 那个宇宙民没法动手，就转而寻找些适合当下的言语开骂了过来，"朝那些超空间野兽和幽灵丢阻断脉冲是会倒大霉的。晦气！太晦气了！干这一行的都知道不该朝这些东西大吼的！" 对方的言辞逐渐激烈，让你觉得自己好比犯下了基本原则方面的大错一样。"这会害我们所有人送命的！"

这个宇宙民的同伴一边盯着你，一边把他们的大嗓门同伴拉回安静的角落。一些围观的人做着各种有些走样的卢德教派祈福动作，这是宇宙民驱邪的动作。

entries.en: You duck past notices encouraging temperance and restraint as you enter the bar. Someone is playing a stringed instrument in an alcove. A row of handworked samovars suggests that tea is served as often as the weak grain-brew favored by the crew of rough-looking laborers at the bar. Many of the patrons at tables or booths seem to be off-worlders or local unbelievers huddling in the closest analog to a den of sin that can be found.
entries.zh: 你低头避开了鼓励节欲与克制的告示牌，走入酒吧。角落的凹室里有人在演奏着某种弦乐器。吧台旁边一排手工制作的茶炊，提醒你这里经常供应茶水，销量可能和吧台上那些劳工大老粗们爱喝的淡啤酒差不多。不少看起来像是外星访客的人和不信教的当地人聚集几张桌台附近，交流买卖着情报，构成了这里最像罪恶巢穴的地方。

entries.en: A weathered brute from the local vice squad stares rudely as you pass, but does not stop you as you enter the door. They want you to know that they could shut the place down at any time - but an illicit teahouse-bar is a useful conduit with the commerce required to carry out holy war. Inside it is dim, the ceiling low, and the crowd packed. The stench of drug fumes and cheap liquor competes with bodies that disdain modern enzyme soaps.
entries.zh: 在你经过时，当地惩戒团的一头饱经沧桑的彪形大汉狠狠地瞪了你一眼，但并没有阻止你进门。他们只是想让你知道，要不是能为开展圣战提供有利的交易渠道，这样一个违禁的茶楼酒肆他们随时都可以取缔掉。在这昏暗压抑且拥挤不堪的地方里，因不屑使用现代酶制香皂而产生的独特体臭四处弥漫，与毒品烟雾和廉价烈酒的恶臭争奇斗艳。

entries.en: As you enter the bar you are struck by the lack of conversation and revelry. Ad-holos promoting Mbaye-Gogol cryosanctum packages buzz softly from ceiling-mounted units, shining cool highlights through glasses and bottles as subdued spacer crews mingle. A few merchant-captains hold a low conversation while ignoring the few local employees who seem mostly content to drink alone.
entries.zh: 你一进门便觉出这里既无谈笑，也无喧闹。天花板上装的装置低低嗡鸣，播着 Mbaye-Gogol 低温圣所套餐的广告全息影像，冷光透过杯盏瓶罐洒下，几群神色收敛的太空人船员在其中走动。几位商船船长压低了嗓子交谈，对那几个本地雇员不理不睬，而他们倒也多半乐得独饮。

entries.en: As you enter the bar, you sense a lively tension between the crews from across the League worlds. Dour Kazeronians in fine uniforms drink spirits while proud but poor Mayasurans down pints of rice-beer. A crew of Tylians trade rounds and boasts with a couple Zaganian bridge officers who are making a poor example of Luddic temperance. Glowing displays show media feeds from all the worlds of the League, and their speakers contribute to a dull roar of human white noise.
entries.zh: 从进入酒吧的那一刻起，你就感受到了来自联盟世界各地的船员之间求同存异的氛围。不苟言笑的 Kazeron 人身着光鲜的制服喝着烈酒，旁边高傲但落魄的 Mayasura 人则一扎又一扎地灌着稻啤酒。一群 Tyle 船员与几名 Zagan 舰桥军官边吹牛边拼酒，为卢德教规提倡的节制立了个坏榜样。众多显示屏五光十色地展示着来自联盟各个行星的媒体资讯，而它们的扬声器也为这众人的喧哗平添了一分吵闹。

entries.en: The space is dark and filled with shouts, sweat, and pulsing music. Every wall and surface is pitted and stained by rough spacers banging their mugs and laughing as a couple of pirate crews posture for a fight. You can only assume that one of the heavily augmented bouncers will spoil the fun before weapons are drawn. Gangers and pirate captains watch the scene smugly from smoke-filled booths at the back.
entries.zh: 昏暗的空间里塞满了呐喊、汗臭和律动着的音乐。正好有两拨海盗船员摆出了要干上一架的样子，惹得酒吧里这群粗野的太空佬们大笑起哄，抄起他们手中的杯子给所有的墙和桌面又敲上了一层坑洼和污渍。看来你只能指望在有人拔枪干起来之前，那群全身堆满生化改造的看场保安里会出来个人扫一扫大家的兴头。在后面烟雾缭绕的隔间里，帮派分子和海盗舰长们看着这场面有些满意地笑了起来。

entries.en: The lounge is adorned on all surfaces in richly gilt geometrics; black marble columns underlit by cool light-tubes seem to hang effortlessly in the air. Corporate climbers, either slick Tri-Tachyon careerists or wannabes in crisp suits, negotiate deals while buying one another increasingly unlikely cocktails. A few spacers engage in subdued drinking in the low seats, glancing uneasily at what is either abstract art or some kind of holo-projection rig looming from the ceiling.
entries.zh: 酒座里的各个墙面都装饰着富丽堂皇的镀金几何图形。黑色大理石柱沐浴在冷光管的柔光之下，雍容华贵地悬在空中。在速子科技名利场里打拼的家伙们全都西装革履，在谈生意的同时不断买来价格越来越离谱的鸡尾酒请客。一些宇宙民则在矮靠背椅上低调地喝着酒，有些局促地瞥着那些若隐若现地从天花板上投影下来的不知是抽象艺术还是全息投影的东西。

entries.en: You take a shuttle down to the main concourse and quickly find a likely-looking establishment.
entries.zh: 你搭乘穿梭机来到主港区内，很快就找到了一家看起来还不错的店。

entries.en:
As soon as you step into the light, faces turn toward you and a particularly burly patron stands and stares directly at you.

You're still mid-threat assessment when the cheers break out. "Captain $playerName!" someone shouts, then spills half of a mug of something as their companions raise their arms.

It appears as though you have some admirers.
entries.zh:
你刚一出现，就有几人看向了你，还有一位格外壮实的顾客站起身，直直地盯着你。

正当你评估当前情况有多危险时，大家开始欢呼。" $playerName 舰长！" 有人喊了起来，随后洒掉了半杯什么东西，而其他人也是扬起手臂开始庆祝。

看来有人很仰慕你。

o.en: Join them for a round and bask in adulation
o.zh: 和他们喝几杯，享受一下他们的奉承
优雅地让他们冷静下来

o.en: Sternly nod an acknowledgement and get on with your business
o.zh: 严肃地点点头，表示你知道了，然后继续干正事

o.en: This is altogether too much. Leave immediately.
o.zh: 你可受不了这种事，立刻离开

entries.en: You join the crew at the table to their uproarious delight, patrons shoving over to make room.
entries.zh: 你坐在桌边，加入喧哗的人群，看来你能来让他们很高兴。熟客们纷纷挤到一边，给你留出空间。

o.en: The stage is yours, why not use it? Give a speech!
o.zh: 既然有了舞台，那为什么不开演呢？来段演讲！

entries.en:
You leap up onto a table and are handed a drink, which you raise high to a new round of cheers.

"Speech, speech!" the crowd chants, and you make a show of reluctance before giving in to their demands.
entries.zh:
你跳上桌子，有人给你递了杯酒水，于是你顺势把酒水举了起来，引得大家又开始碰杯庆祝。

"演讲！演讲！" 大家喊了起来，你装作不情愿的样子几度推脱，最后还是按照他们的意思行事。

o.en: Focus on the local VIPs and tell some flattering anecdotes
o.zh: 以本地要员为主题，讲些讨好他们的八卦

o.en: Compliment the crowd and make a connection with the crews
o.zh: 夸奖一下在场的大家，讲讲你和船员们的联系

o.en: You're the star! Talk about yourself
o.zh: 你才是主角！讲讲你自己的事

entries.en:
Smiling, you try to calm this table. Unfortunately, this just feeds their enthusiasm. Crews sitting at more tables turn to look, patrons whispering to one another and pointing, and others raising their voices to call out.

It's going to be very difficult to find any contacts here with all this attention.
entries.zh:
你笑了笑，尝试让桌边的大家安静下来，但结果却是大家变得更加热情了，其他桌边也有人转身看向你，熟客们互相低语，冲着你这边指指点点，甚至有人高声喊了起来。

所有人都注意到你的情况下，再想单独联络某一个人可就相当困难了。

o.en: Might as well join them for a round
o.zh: 不如就和他们一起喝几杯吧

o.en: This is too much; wave politely as you leave
o.zh: 这太过火了，和善地挥手离开吧

entries.en:
You give a sedate wave of acknowledgement, turn right around, and walk out of the bar.

The cheers and shouts, only growing louder, are muffled as you step into the outside corridor.
entries.zh:
你平静地挥了挥手，表示自己知道了，顺势转身走出了酒吧。

酒吧里仍有人欢呼、大喊，声音越来越大，不过当你走出酒吧的时候，酒吧里的声音也就听不清了。

entries.en:
You give a stern nod, the very face of stoicism.

Your example triggers a rush of somewhat tipsy salutes and over-exuberant return nods. More drink is spilled in this process, but at least they've quieted down.
entries.zh:
你摆出一脸沉稳，波澜不惊地微微点头示意。

如此表率引来了一片伴着微醺的回礼和过分热情的点头回应。虽然又洒了些酒水，但好歹所有人都安静下来了。

entries.en:
You quietly inquire about what the group is drinking to, setting off laughter and good cheer. You're handed a drink, and as you sip, hear several versions of your latest exploits, each more unlikely than the last.

You do your best to correct the worst exaggerations, but the consensus has clearly formed that you're playing it down.
entries.zh:
你打听起大家在为什么干杯，顿时引发了一阵欢笑与喝彩。你一边抿着别人递来的酒水，一边听着人们谈论你最近的光荣事迹的好几种说法，一个比一个更离谱。

你极力想纠正那些最离谱的吹嘘，但大伙明显都只当你是在谦虚罢了。

entries.en:
With the round complete, you make your apologies to much good-natured booing, and tactfully make for a dark corner to recover your thoughts and take in the bar- the bartender, with a nod, ensures you have a tall glass of cold water at hand.

Refreshed, and having quieted things down, you have a chance at last to look around.
entries.zh:
你喝完了酒，为你本就没什么恶意的小小玩笑道了个歉，然后委婉推脱着找了个昏暗的角落坐下，开始复盘你在酒吧的所见所想。服务生点了点头，为你盛上了一大杯冰水用来醒酒。

等你精神恢复了，周围也安静下来了，你终于有机会四处看看了。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent local officials, earning quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent local officials, earning quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments.

You shift the monologue toward a light-hearted review of each of the Luddic shrines you visited, earning tense laughter, but you manage to turn what at first appeared to be subversive implications into a heartfelt conclusion which results in earnest applause from spacer and Faithful alike.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。

说着说着，你停止了自说自话，开始轻轻松松地 "评鉴" 你一路上走过的每个卢德圣地，在引得大家哄堂大笑的同时，你还隐去了你某些初见有些颠覆性的暗示，转而以深切的感受作结，于是太空佬们和虔诚信徒最后都诚挚地鼓起掌来。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent local Hegemony officials, earning quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments. A pack of cadets in the corner is especially taken with an aside about meeting High Hegemon Daud.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地 霸主 高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。房间角落里的一帮学员听你讲述自己和至高霸主 Daud 会面的故事，听得尤其出神。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent gens and officials, earning quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments.

Your impression of Reynard Hannon's accent draws particular divisions between his supporters and detractors in the crowd, but you manage to defuse the tension with a well-timed joke, transforming scowls into self-deprecating smiles.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。

中途你模仿 Reynard Hannan 的口音，加深了酒馆人群里他的支持者与批评者之间的分歧，但你又恰到好处地开了个玩笑，于是原本怒目而视的两拨人也只好难为情地一笑而过。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent local officials, earning quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments.

You transition into an anecdote about drinking tea with Brother Livewell Cotton and the bar goes quiet indeed - one particular spacer at the front goes pale and makes to look for the closest exit. You pivot, reassuring the spacer with the finer points of tea etiquette, prompting laughter and earning the fearful spacer good-natured ribbing from their drinking companions.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。

说着说着，你开始讲述你与 Livewell Cotton 修士一同喝茶的经历，酒吧当场一片寂静，甚至在前排有个太空佬已经开始面色苍白，望向最近的安全出口。你话锋一转，讲起茶艺的细微之处，安抚刚刚害怕的太空佬，于是大家又开始大笑，那个太空佬也被同桌酒友们善意地嘲弄起来。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few off-color quips and a story involving some of the more prominent local pirates, earning quiet or cheers at the appropriate moments.

A hush falls over the bar as you recall your meeting with Kanta herself; you manage to break the tension with an unflattering aside about her 'doctor', Cydonia, prompting laughter and pounding of tables.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点荤段子，俏皮话，还分享了本地大海盗们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时机都选得很恰当。

你开始回忆自己和 Kanta 会面的经历时，酒吧里突然鸦雀无声，见势不妙，你毫无奉承成分地讲了讲 Kanta 的 '医生' Cydonia，于是大家又开始狂笑，笑到直拍桌子。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You share a few flattering quips and a story about some prominent local Tri-Tachyon figures, earning moments of quiet, cheers, or laughter at the appropriate moments. A joke suggesting that Artemisia Sun is an AI core lands particularly well with the crowd despite earning you a deadly look from a finely-dressed executive sitting alone near the back of the room.

Some of the stories might even be true. Or not. What's important is the connections you're making - or pretending you already made - with the local power-players.
entries.zh:
你讲了一点带讨好意味的俏皮话，还分享了本地高官们身上的一个故事，人们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选的很恰当。你中途开了个玩笑，暗指 Artemisia Sun 其实是一个 AI 核心，大家都听得很开心，除了酒馆后排单独坐着的某个西装革履的高官 —— 听到你的这个笑话，那人用想杀人的眼神看了你一眼。

你讲的故事里，有些甚至可能是真的，但无论真假，故事本身并不重要，重要的是你以此建立了 —— 或者说假装建立了 —— 与本地高官之间的联系。

entries.en:
You speak about the hard-working spacers that make everything you've done possible, sharing a story of daring, danger, and victory. Moments of quiet, cheers, or laughter come at the appropriate moments as you connect the experiences of your crew with the individuals at the tables around you.

Some time later, in a quiet corner, the bartender hands you a tall glass of cool water with a nod.

Your personnel officer pings your datapad with a surprised message about a number of enthusiastic, and slightly drunk, spacers choosing to sign on to your $shipOrFleet while waiving the usual contract signing bonus.
entries.zh:
你开始讲述勤勤恳恳的宇宙民如何帮助你成就了现如今的一切，顺势分享了一个关于果敢、危险、胜利的故事。你由自己船员的经历又联想到了桌边喝酒的各位，他们时而安静，时而欢呼，时而大笑，时机都选得很恰当。

过了有一阵子，在酒吧安静的角落里，服务生为你递上了一大杯冰水用来醒酒，还对着你点了下头。

在数据平板上，舰队人事官惊讶地呼叫你，表示有不少热情满满还有点微醺的宇宙民决定加入你的$shipOrFleet，他们连通常的签约奖金都拒绝了。

entries.en:
You start slow, and quiet, forcing the crowd to quiet themselves and one another to hear you.

Having caught their attention, you lay it on about the dangers and trials you have faced - how is it possible you're here, alive, to tell the tale? Through laughter, cheers, and hushed moments you speak of your deeds to the rapt audience and, in a roaring conclusion, somehow connect it all to the greater glory of $theMarketFaction, to applause from the entire bar.

Somehow you're the hero of the day, though only a handful here knew it when you first walked in.
entries.zh:
你开始讲话了，声音很低，语速很慢，暗示酒吧的大家要安静，顺带还得让其他人也安静，才能听清你讲的话。

正当大家都注意到你的时候，你开始添油加醋地讲述你一路上遇到的种种危险，经历的种种试炼 —— 你到底是怎样，才能一直活到现在，来到这里，向大家讲述自己的传奇。你讲述着自己一路上的所作所为，台下观众全神贯注，时而大笑，时而欢呼，时而沉默。临近末尾，你情绪愈发高涨，不知怎的就将你的所有成就与 $theMarketFaction 的荣耀联系起来，引得满堂喝彩。

不知为何，你就成了今天的主角，虽然刚刚进入酒吧的时候只有少数几个人知晓。

entries.en:
Some time later, in a quiet corner, the bartender hands you a tall glass of cool water with a nod.

Refreshed, and things having quieted down, you have a chance at last to look around.
entries.zh:
过了有一阵子，在酒吧安静的角落里，服务生为你递上了一大杯冰水用来醒酒，还对着你点了下头。

等你精神恢复了，周围也安静下来了，你终于有机会四处看看了。

entries.en: Refreshed, and things having quieted down, you have a chance at last to look around.
entries.zh: 等你精神恢复了，周围也安静下来了，你终于有机会四处看看了。

entries.en:
The chaos begins to spread outward, crew and locals alike staring, and those drunkest and angriest standing.

You hear your name spoken like a curse, and a makeshift missile shatters on the support column behind you.

Your bodyguards form a human wall to cover your path toward the exit. Stumbling outside, you can hear the alarms which signal the rapid approach of local MuniSec. There'll be no quiet business done in this bar for the shift, that much is clear.
entries.zh:
混乱蔓延开来，船员和本地人都瞪着你，还有几个最醉的 —— 也是最愤怒的人，站了起来。

你听到有人像骂脏话一样吼出你的名字，同时，一发临时制成的投掷物在你背后的承重柱上轰然碎裂。

你的保镖们组成人墙，护卫你走出酒吧。你刚跌跌撞撞地跑出门，就听到了警笛声，看来本地的地方安全部正在快速赶来。很明显，今天酒吧里没什么能安静谈事的地方了。

entries.en:
The chaos spreads outward, crew and locals alike staring, and those drunkest - clearly, this bar doesn't only serve tea and small-beer - and angriest standing.

You hear your name called like a curse, and a makeshift missile smashes against a samovar behind you. It tips, slowly, and falls to the ground with a crash. A small wave of hot water washes over your boots, and a cloud of steam envelopes you.

Your bodyguards form a human wall to cover your path toward the exit. Stumbling outside, you can hear the ringing of alarm bells which signal the rapid approach of the local MuniSec squad led by a Knight of Ludd. There'll be no quiet business done in this bar for the rest of the shift, that much is clear.

The chaos begins to spread outward, crew and locals alike staring, and those drunkest and angriest standing.

You hear your name spoken like a curse, and a makeshift missile shatters on the support column behind you. A pack of cadets rushes the exit, eager to avoid a potential military discipline for involvement in a bar brawl.

Your bodyguards form a human wall to cover your withdrawal. Stumbling outside, you hear the buzz of riot control drones which signals the rapid approach of gendarmerie. There'll be no quiet business done in this bar for the rest of the shift, that much is clear.
