你从 $lpt_sourceName 带来的朝圣者的领头人非要 "杰出的舰长" 来为他们送行。"你应该去看看圣地，舰长。" $lpt_hisOrHer坚持道。"我也曾是个无信者；那是段脱胎换骨的体验。"

他露出了一个完美的微笑，"当然，我也知道这是个必须由你自己选择去行的旅道。" $lpt_HeOrShe做了一个虔诚的手势，然后搭上了$lpt_HeOrShe为他们一行雇来送他们去圣地的私人穿梭机。

o.en: Perhaps a larger tithe could inspire a broader arrangement.
o.zh: 说不定一笔更高的什一税可以让我们达成更多的共识。

entries.en:
"Perhaps your soul is not yet lost to the machine."
OR
"Truly, Ludd's hand has guided you."
entries.zh:
"也许你的灵魂还未被机械伪神夺走。"
OR
"平心而论，卢德之手刚刚引导了你。"

entries.en:
"Submit and repent! Your use of sinful technologies may be forgiven, for a tithe of $entity.LP_titheDGS credits.

Resist, and only God's holy vacuum will show you mercy."
OR
"Servant of Moloch! Redemption is not out of reach even for you. A tithe of $entity.LP_titheDGS credits may set you upon the first step of the Path of Ludd."

"Forswear this penance and be met with annihilation, cursed by Ludd in the next life. The choice is yours."
entries.zh:
"服从并忏悔！你们需要献上 $entity.LP_titheDGS 星币作为什一税，才能祈求你们的科技罪业被宽恕。

倘若负隅顽抗，那唯有造物主神圣的虚空能给你们带来解脱。"
OR
"恶魔摩洛克的奴仆！或许救赎对你们来说还并非遥不可及。献上 $entity.LP_titheDGS 星币的什一税可以让你踏上卢德之道的第一步。"

"放弃这次忏悔的机会将遭受灭顶之灾，来生也必被卢德诅咒。斟酌定夺皆由你。"

o.en: Approach the pilgrim wearing fine Luddic robes
o.zh: 靠近穿着精致卢德袍的朝圣者

o.en: Approach the Luddic pilgrim wearing ragged robes
o.zh: 接近那个身着破烂卢德朝圣者服装的人

entries.en:
You approach the pilgrim. Finally seeing someone who looks like they want to talk, $lpt_heOrShe produces a crooked smile and puts $lpt_hisOrHer calloused hands together.

"May Ludd bless you, $playerSirOrMadam," $lpt_heOrShe says, bowing. "I beg of you for passage for myself and a small party to the shrine of $lpt_entityName. We are but poor pilgrims and cannot pay, so we beg this as charity from you."

"Perhaps you are already traveling to the $lpt_systemName? The $lpt_visitTargetName would be but a short detour." $lpt_HeOrShe looks up at you hopefully. "We will cause no trouble, and will pray for Providence to bless you with prosperity and health."
entries.zh:
你靠近了朝圣者。见终于有人愿意谈谈了，$lpt_heOrShe合起了$lpt_hisOrHer满是老茧的手，露出了一个歪斜的微笑。

"愿卢德赐福于您，$playerSirOrMadam，" $lpt_heOrShe说着鞠了一躬。"我恳请您为我和一小队同伴开一条去 $lpt_entityName 圣地的道。我们都只是清苦的朝圣者，没法付钱，所以请您行行善举。"

"或许您已经在去 $lpt_systemName 的路上了？圣地只是绕个小路。" $lpt_HeOrShe抬头满怀希冀地看着你。"我们不会惹麻烦的，而且会向上天祈祷，愿您成功富足。"

entries.en:
You approach the pilgrim, who smiles and puts $lpt_hisOrHer hands together. From $lpt_hisOrHer confident disposition and quality clothing it is clear that $lpt_heOrShe comes from wealth somewhat at odds with Ludd's ascetic reputation.

"Blessed day. Captain, I presume?" $lpt_heOrShe says. "I wish to arrange transport for myself and my party to the $lpt_visitTargetName - on $lpt_entityName, of course - in the $lpt_systemName. Naturally I shall provide payment. Would $lpt_reward credits be worth a journey of $lpt_dist light-years?"
entries.zh:
你靠近了朝圣者，$lpt_hisOrHer微笑着合起了双手。从$lpt_hisOrHer自信的气质和优质的服饰来看，$lpt_hisOrHer显然出身优渥，而这与卢德作为苦修的名声也颇有些格格不入。

"愿您蒙福。舰长，我猜？" $lpt_hisOrHer说道，"我想为我和我的队伍安排一趟去 $lpt_systemName 的 $lpt_entityName 圣地的旅途。当然，我会付钱，$lpt_reward 星币值得你走 $lpt_dist 光年吗？"

entries.en: You have your purser make arrangements, with instructions to keep the pilgrims from interfering in $shipOrFleet operations.
entries.zh: 你让你的事务长去安排了，同时也指示他别让朝圣者打扰$shipOrFleet的运行。

o.en: Repair your ships at the dockyard
o.zh: 前往船坞修理你的舰船

o.en: Repair your ships at the dockyard
o.zh: 前往船坞修理你的舰船

o.en: Repair your ships at the dockyard
o.zh: 前往船坞修理你的舰船

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet approaches $entityName.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet靠近了 $entityName。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet finishes offloading crew, supplies, and machinery $onOrAt $marketName, and the crew soon busy themselves erecting temporary shelter and basic infrastructure.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet完成了对船员、补给以及重型机械的卸载工作，船员们很快就开始忙着在 $marketName 搭建起临时住所和其他基础设施。

o.en: Take a shuttle down to visit a dockside bar
o.zh: 乘坐穿梭机前往港口边的酒吧
考虑可以采取的军事行动

entries.en: You connect to the local comm directory and browse the public and otherwise known listings.
entries.zh: 你与本地通讯目录建立连接，并浏览公共列表和其他已知列表。

entries.en: You establish a linkup with the dockyard and transmit your $shipOrFleet status.
entries.zh: 你与当地船坞建立连接，并传输了你的$shipOrFleet状态。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet undergoes full repairs and is restored to maximum combat readiness, at the cost of $global.repairSupplyCost supplies.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet通过全面维修已恢复到最大战备状态，共消耗 $global.repairSupplyCost 单位补给。

entries.en: You establish a linkup with the port authority's cargo management system and browse the inventory.
entries.zh: 你与港务局的货物管理系统建立连接，并开始浏览当地的存货。

entries.en: You establish a linkup with the dockyard and see what's available.
entries.zh: 你与当地船坞建立连接，并开始浏览可供购入的船体。

o.en: Trade goods or hire crew [I], buy or sell ships [F], or refit [R]
o.zh: 进行货物贸易或雇用船员 [I]，买卖舰船 [F]，或改装舰船 [R]。

entries.en: The port authority refuses your $shipOrFleet docking clearance until the customs inspection is resolved. Making contact with any underground parties willing to trade is also impossible due to the patrol breathing down your neck.
entries.zh: 在海关检查结束之前，港务局拒绝你的$shipOrFleet的停靠许可。且由于巡逻队紧盯着你，你也不可能与任何有交易意愿的地下组织取得联系。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet transmits identification codes via the transponder and you are soon granted docking clearance.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet通过应答器发送了识别代码。很快便收到了停靠许可。

entries.en: Tapping into the comm network for local news, you learn that there was a recent and protracted food shortage. Though the shortage is now over, the local situation is still highly destabilized.
entries.zh: 你通过当地新闻网络得知最近发生了长期的食品短缺。虽然短缺已经结束，但当地局势仍极不稳定。

entries.en: Thanks in part to your efforts, the recent food shortage is over. Your standing with $theMarketFaction should improve slightly.
entries.zh: 由于你的帮助，食品短缺现已结束。这略微改善了你与 $theMarketFaction 间的关系。

entries.en: Tapping into the comm network for local news, you learn that there was a recent food shortage. Though the shortage is now over, the local situation is still somewhat destabilized.
entries.zh: 你通过当地新闻网络得知近期发生了食品短缺。虽然目前短缺已经结束，但当地局势仍不稳定。

entries.en: Thanks to your efforts, the food shortage is now over. Its impact on $marketName's stability is reduced.
entries.zh: 由于你的帮助，食品短缺现已结束。它对 $marketName 造成的稳定性影响已被缓解。

entries.en: Thanks to your illicit efforts, the food shortage is now over. Since much of the food you've delivered went through channels of questionable legality, there's not much hope - or, indeed, desire - for official recognition.
entries.zh: 由于你的法外援助，食品短缺现已结束。鉴于你大部分带来的食品是通过非法途径流入市场，所以本次援助行为并不被官方所认可。

entries.en: Thanks to your efforts, the food shortage is now over before it had a chance to cause much chaos. $marketName's long-term stability is unaffected by the shortage.
entries.zh: 由于你的帮助，食品短缺在造成进一步损失之前就已结束。而 $marketName 的长期稳定性将不会受到影响。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet transmits identification codes via the transponder and you are soon granted a slot in a parking orbit.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet通过应答器发送了识别代码。很快便在停泊轨道中被分到了一个空位。

entries.en:
$TheFactionLong $factionIsOrAre $relAdjective towards you, and the port authority refuses your request for docking clearance after you identify yourself.

You might be able to establish contact with underground parties if you come in with the transponder turned off.
entries.zh:
鉴于 $TheFactionLong 与你处于 $relAdjective 关系，港务局拒绝了你的停靠许可。

不过你要是{关闭应答器}的话，倒是有可能与这儿的地下组织建立联系。

entries.en: Your recent actions around $marketName have generated a lot of local interest, and simply coming in with the transponder off is no longer sufficient to go unnoticed. Judging from the current level of comm chatter and news reports, you estimate it'll take $playerHostileTimeoutStr until the commotion dies down.
entries.zh: 你最近在 $marketName 附近采取的行动已经引起了广泛的关注。关闭应答器已经无法蒙混过关。从目前的传言和新闻来看，你恐怕得等 $playerHostileTimeoutStr 才能指望骚乱平息。

entries.en: Your recent actions around $marketName have generated a lot of local interest, and engaging in open business is impossible. Judging from the current level of comm chatter and news reports, you estimate it'll take $playerHostileTimeoutStr until the commotion dies down.
entries.zh: 你最近在 $marketName 附近采取的行动已经引起了广泛的关注。目前已无法进行公开交易。从目前的传言和新闻来看，你恐怕得等 $playerHostileTimeoutStr 才能指望骚乱平息。

entries.en:
$TheFactionLong $factionIsOrAre $relAdjective towards you, and the port authority refuses your request for docking clearance after you identify yourself.

The refusal is rather perfunctory and you get the impression that turning off your transponder to prevent identification might yield better results.
entries.zh:
鉴于 $TheFactionLong 与你处于 $relAdjective 关系，港务局拒绝了你的入港许可。

对方拒绝的理由相当敷衍，你觉得只需{关闭你的应答器}就可轻松混入。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet goes into orbit around $marketName.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet进入了环绕着 $marketName 的轨道。

entries.en:
Your $shipOrFleet goes into orbit around $marketName.

At least one $faction patrol is tracking your movements, and the port authority refuses your request for docking clearance until the matter is resolved.
entries.zh:
你的$shipOrFleet进入了环绕着 $marketName 的轨道。

至少有一支 $faction 的巡逻队正在追踪你的动向，且在事态解决之前，港务局拒绝批准你的停靠许可。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet goes into orbit around $marketName. The local port authority seems to take no issue with your explanation for why your transponder, regrettably, can't be turned on.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet进入了环绕着 $marketName 的轨道附近，港务局对你谎称自己的应答器 "非常抱歉地无法开启" 的理由没有提出任何质疑。

entries.en:
Your $shipOrFleet goes into orbit around $marketName, ignoring requests from the $faction port authority to identify yourself.

At least one $faction patrol is tracking your movements, and no underground parties are willing to run the risk of doing business.
entries.zh:
你的$shipOrFleet进入了环绕着 $marketName 的轨道，并无视了 $faction 港务局所发出的身份识别要求。

至少有一支 $faction 巡逻队正追踪你的舰队，导致地下组织没人愿意冒险与你暗中交易。

entries.en:
Your $shipOrFleet goes into orbit around $marketName, ignoring requests from $theFaction port authority to identify yourself.

No $faction patrols seem to be aware of you just yet, and you have a window of opportunity for doing business with parties untroubled by your lack of docking clearance.
entries.zh:
你的$shipOrFleet进入了环绕着 $marketName 的轨道，并无视了 $theFaction 港务局所发出的身份识别要求。

目前似乎没有 $faction 巡逻队注意到你，这也给无法取得靠港许可的你一次暗中交易的机会。

entries.en: You leave the bar and take a shuttle back to your $shipOrFleet.
entries.zh: 你离开酒吧，乘坐穿梭机回到了你的$shipOrFleet当中。

entries.en: "Some new targets have come up on the docket," $heOrShe says with a sigh. "If you took a contract to handle one of these bounties, it might just get the brass off my case."
entries.zh: "赏金清单上又有了一些新目标。" $heOrShe叹了口气，"如果你能从里边挑一份，我负责处理的事可能会少些麻烦。"

entries.en: A military officer is holding court at one of the nicer tables; you watch a merc captain approach for a perfunctory exchange of words and mutual tap of datapads. They appear to be acting as some kind of system patrol liaison contracting out bounties.
entries.zh: 一位军官正在一张看起来不错的桌子上接待着来者。你看到一个雇佣舰长走了过去，双方简单地说了几句话，还敲了敲数据平板。对方似乎是某种星系巡逻队的联络人，负责将赏金任务外包出去。

entries.en: "New targets have come up from intel," $heOrShe says. "I would like them handled with more initiative and discretion than my subordinates are accustomed to."
entries.zh: "情报那边报上来几个新目标，\" $heOrShe说道。\"我希望办得比我那些手下惯常的更主动、也更不着痕迹。"

entries.en: "Some new targets have come up on the docket," $heOrShe says with a sigh. "If you took a contract to handle one of these bounties, it might just get a senior VP off my case."
entries.zh: "单子上新挂了几个目标，\" $heOrShe叹了口气。\"你要是接下一桩赏金合同去办了，说不定能让某位高级副总裁别再盯着我。"

entries.en: "New targets have come up from intel" $heOrShe says. "I would like them handled with more initiative and discretion than my subordinates are accustomed to."
entries.zh: "情报那边报上来几个新目标，\" $heOrShe说道。\"我希望办得比我那些手下惯常的更主动、也更不着痕迹。"

o.en: I'd prefer a more manageable target.
o.zh: 我想要个更容易拿捏的目标。

o.en: Whatever you've got works for me.
o.zh: 随便什么你觉得适合我的都行。

o.en: I can handle a more challenging target.
o.zh: 我觉得可以来个更难搞的目标。

o.en: I'd prefer a more manageable target.
o.zh: 我想要个更容易拿捏的目标。

o.en: Whatever you've got works for me.
o.zh: 随便什么你觉得适合我的都行。

o.en: I can handle a more challenging target.
o.zh: 我觉得可以来个更难搞的目标。

o.en: Ask about what's available on the bounty docket
o.zh: 问问赏金清单里有什么

o.en: Talk to the $mcb_manOrWoman from the military offering bounties
o.zh: 和负责军方悬赏任务的$mcb_manOrWoman谈谈

entries.en:
You approach and $Rank $personLastName gives you a perfunctory nod. "Captain," $heOrShe says, all business.

"I have several assignments on the docket," $heOrShe looks down, scrolling $hisOrHer datapad. A coffee, black, certainly no sugar, is cooling on the table beside $hisOrHer hand. "What sort of job can you handle?"
entries.zh:
你走过去，$personLastName $rank 敷衍地点了点头。"舰长。" $heOrShe带着公事公办的语气说。

"这里有几项任务要处理。" $heOrShe低下头，用手在$hisOrHer的数据平板上划动着。一杯肯定没加糖的黑咖啡正放在$hisOrHer手边的桌子上晾着，"你能胜任怎么样的工作？"

entries.en:
"We've got a few options here," $personLastName says, pulling up a shared display with a table of intel reports.

"We've got an op timeslot coming up for an HK squadron that'll handle whatever you don't, so it's really your pick of the bunch. What sort of job do you think you can handle?"
entries.zh:
"这里有几个目标。" $personLastName $post 推送过来一个共享显示界面，上边显示着一系列的情报。

"我们有个猎杀小队也马上就要出动了。它们会处理掉你不接的单子，所以你可以随便挑。你认为你能胜任什么样的工作？"

entries.en:
"We have several options," $personLastName says, pulling up a shared display with a table of intel reports.

"An operation timeslot for a realiable HK squadron, another merc, is coming up and they'll handle whatever you don't. You may pick any target you consider appropriate."
entries.zh:
"咱们有几个选择，" $personLastName说着，调出一幅共享显示屏，上面列着一张情报报告表。

"另有一支靠得住的 HK 中队，也是雇来的，行动窗口就要开了，你没接的那些都归他们收拾。目标随你挑，看着哪个合适就定哪个。"

o.en: Ask about one of the other targets
Ask about one of the other targets

entries.en:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam," your comms officer calls your attention. "Port authority is... they were acting strangely. Contact's mood shifted after the $shipOrFleet was identified."

Comms look up from their console. "I think we've been quietly flagged by the authorities for some reason."
entries.zh:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam，" 你的通讯军官对你示意。"港务局那边... 他们行为很奇怪。识别到$shipOrFleet后联络人情绪就变了。"

通讯军官从控制台上抬起头。"我觉得官方因为某些原因悄悄盯上我们了。"

entries.en:
The comms connect to a holding pattern, the crest of Gens Yaribay. And wait.

It soon becomes clear that Menes Yaribay is ignoring your request.
entries.zh:
通讯接入了一个等候界面，屏幕上有个 Yaribay 氏族的徽标。随后开始等待。

很快你就意识到 Menes Yaribay 无视了你的请求。

entries.en:
The comms connect to a holding pattern, the crest of Gens Yaribay. And wait.

Menes Yaribay is not acknowledging your request at this time.
entries.zh:
通讯接入了一个等候界面，屏幕上有个 Yaribay 氏族的徽标。随后开始等待。

Menes Yaribay 目前没有理会你的请求。

entries.en:
"Greetings, commander! My contracted time is up, and I'd like to think we've both benefited from the arrangement.

Now, I think I'll have a go at spending all the credits I've earned - little chance to do that cooped up on a ship in the middle of nowhere, is there?"
entries.zh:
"您好，指挥官！我的合同期满了。我有幸感到我们双方都从这个合约中受益匪浅。

现在我打算去挥霍一下自己挣到的这些星币，毕竟一直呆在远离文明世界的船里可没什么机会这么做，不是吗？"

entries.en:
"Ah, commander." $HeOrShe has put on a slightly pained expression, but is clearly willing to power through an uncomfortable conversation.

"Please accept my condolences for your current state of financial insolvency."

"As per the conditions set out in our agreement, I now have the option to terminate our contract - an option that I am choosing to exercise."
entries.zh:
"啊，指挥官。" $HeOrShe一开口就换上了略显沉痛的语气，但却又很明显地想要尽快完成这段让人感到不自在的对话。

"请容许我向您目前面临的资不抵债的财务问题深表同情。

依照我们先前在合约里立下的条款，在目前的情况下我有权选择终止我们的合约。虽然很遗憾，但我不得不选择行使这一权力。"

entries.en: With a charismatic display of appeal to $hisOrHer ambition and ego, along with the implication - not promise - that good fortune is just around the corner, you're able to convince $himOrHer to sign an extension to the contract.
entries.zh: 你展现出非凡的领袖气质，迎合$hisOrHer的雄心壮志把对方好好夸奖了一番。同时你旁敲侧击，让$himOrHer觉得再坚持干一会儿就会有更好的收获 (当然你没给出具体承诺)。于是你说服$himOrHer延长了合同的期限。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet docks at $entity.name, you receive a high-priority call from one of the mercenary officers in your employment.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet在 $entity.name 停靠时，你收到了来自你的一名雇佣军官的高优先级通讯请求。

entries.en: You accept $hisOrHer decision professionally and, after exchanging a few pleasantries, cut the comm link.
entries.zh: 你公事公办地接受了$hisOrHer的决定，互相调侃了几句之后就切断了通讯链接。

entries.en: The mercenary seems none too pleased by the dressing-down, as evidenced by $himOrHer cutting the connection while you were in the middle of a particularly scathing analysis of $hisOrHer ancestry.
entries.zh: 雇佣兵明显对这种斥责非常反感，当你还在仔细问候$hisOrHer的祖宗的时候，对方就切断通讯挑明了这一点。

entries.en:
How old must it be, thousands of cycles?

If you had been asked a shift ago, your reasonable reply would have been to call it a myth. The Onslaught Mk.I could easily be a just-so founding narrative element of the Human Domain, a story about united struggle and hardship against an implacable Other with a shiny bit of military kit in center stage. An imagined avatar of the empire's holy trinity: military, industry, gate system.

Yet here that avatar appears, unbelievably far and wayward from the heart of the Human Domain - or even what was once the Domain's frontiers a thousand cycles ago.

Your ops chief, unperturbed, looks to you for confirmation. Words are unneeded, the question is clear: send in the salvors?
entries.zh:
它究竟存在了多久？成千上万个星历年？

如果在一个星历日前被问及，照理，你会称其为一个传说。攻势 Mk.I 很容易被当作 人之领 恰到好处的创世叙事元素 —— 一个关于团结抗争无情异族的艰辛故事，核心点缀着一件闪亮的军事装备。那是帝国三位一体的想象化身：军事、工业、星门系统。

然而这个化身此刻正现身于此，并难以置信地远离 人之领 的中心 —— 甚至比一千个星历年前的 人之领 边疆更加遥远荒僻。

你的行动长官神色如常，等待着你的确认。他的问题不言自明：是否要派遣打捞员们？

entries.en:
Ops nods, then turns to bark commands on the salvors' command frequency.

Junior officers scurry to cajole crew prepping cargo-handling drones while Sensors puts one analysis team on careful outward watch and another on the hulk to ensure there are no surprises.

Within short minutes, the first salvors dock their open-vacuum shuttle frames and utility drones at various entry points identified along the vessel's massive hull.

Ops gives the go-order.
entries.zh:
行动长点了点头，然后通过指挥频道向打捞员们下达命令。

下级军官动员着准备装卸无人机的船员，传感器技官则分派一队分析小组严密监视外围，一队留守残骸应对意外。

几分钟后，第一批打捞小组驾驶着真空穿梭机和辅助无人机，在巨大船体上预选的各个入口处就位。

行动长下达了行动指令。

entries.en:
You notice your comms officer furiously working their interface, then turn and call a report to you.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam! Salvor-four is picking up something on an open frequency- um, radio-only. Very low power. Some kind of analogue encoding? We did this in... training..."

A few more taps, and a message is formed from noise, letter by letter, across your display.
entries.zh:
你注意到通讯军官正忙着操作界面，然后转身向你汇报。

"$PlayerSirOrMadam！第四打捞小组在一个开放频率上接收到信号 —— 呃，仅限无线电频率。功率很低，像是某种模拟编码？我们在...训练中遇到过这种情况..."

又敲了几下，嘈杂的噪声中，一条信息在屏幕上逐字逐句地排列起来。

entries.en:
This gives your officers pause - Ops calls a hold order while the situation is assessed. Internal self-defense systems activating? War-drone deployment?

Only silence.

Then acoustics picks up a few taps as salvors secure themselves to bulkheads, powering down their tools and, no doubt, reaching for what small-arms they do carry.

Still, no movement.

Low, steady EM activity - just the repeater, a chorus of them in fact, mechanically intoning the same message to one another.
entries.zh:
这让军官们犹豫起来 —— 行动长下达了暂停指令，等待态势评估。自卫系统启动？战斗无人机部署？

一片寂静。

随后，声学设备捕捉到几声轻敲，那是打捞员们正在舱壁上固定自己，关闭电子工具，以及毫无疑问的，掏出随身的小型武器。

仍然没有任何动静。

低而稳定的电磁活动 —— 只有中继器，一群中继器的合唱，机械地向彼此发出相同的信息。

entries.en:
Fevered analysis proceeds. In the midst of what appears to be structured noise buried in the analog waveform - datasets which are insensible without context - analysis teams discover a set of coordinates; a position at some distance from the small gravity well you're orbiting in archaic but parseable Domain astrogation units. The message still repeats itself.

"The signal is weak," your sensors officer says. "Unlikely to be picked up by anything that isn't in close-order formation with the... the hull. Tactical telemetry to coordinate distributed systems?"
entries.zh:
分析工作火热地进行着。在看似结构性噪音的模拟波形深处 —— 那些缺乏上下文便无法理解的数据集 —— 分析团队发现了一组坐标；一个用古老但可解析的 人之领 天文导航单位标注的位置，与你正在环绕的小型重力井保持着一定距离。信号仍在持续重复着。

"信号很微弱，" 你的传感器技官说道，"除非与...船体保持密集编队，否则任何设备都难以捕捉。是协调分布式系统的战术遥测信号吗？"

entries.en:
Cautiously, team by team, your operations chief reactivates exploration and assessment of the hulk.

Bafflingly crude automation is wormed throughout the ship, whispering to itself. Interfaces are built on familiar fundamental principles, but aesthetically red-shifted, seemingly from an alien culture.

What records remain are damaged where they aren't missing entirely. The logs tell of aeons of war in the darkness between the stars. Human crew in and out of cryo, continually diminished, replaced by the augmented wounded, then the cyborg rebuilds, and then, and then... this exhausted humming, clicking thing threaded throughout the ship.
entries.zh:
慎之又慎，一队接一队，你的行动主管重启了对残骸的勘探与评估。

令人费解的原始自动化系统在整艘舰船中蔓延，低声自语。交互设施用熟悉的基本原理而构成，但其设计美学发生了红移，仿佛源自异界文明。

残存的记录大多损坏，或干脆完全缺失。那些日志诉说着恒星间黑暗深渊里绵延万古的战争。人类船员在低温休眠中进进出出，持续减员，先由强化过的伤员接替，然后是机械和生物的重构体，再然后，再然后...只剩下这遍布舰体、精疲力竭的嗡鸣声与咔嗒声。

entries.en:
The logs are empty for long periods- dark, hibernating leaps. Then there is a noted uptick in activity less than 200 standard cycles ago. The enemy is only identified as "Threat". A datastore reference leads to blocks of information decayed by time. But the reconstruction algorithms leap into action and, despite troublingly low reliability ratings, sew together a set of files.

Patch notes.

The hardware specs are arcane, the software obtuse and plagued by null library calls, but the common language of human mathematics sketches out the intent. There, your technology officer's team assembles a new spec of the sensor modifications required to detect this "Threat".

Adapting these requirements on your relatively modern systems is a far easier task than the labors described by the ancients.
entries.zh:
日志存在多段很长时间的空白 —— 应该是停止活动的休眠期。在接下来在距今 200 个标准星历年之内，活动记录出现了显著激增。敌人仅被标识为 "威胁"。数据存储索引指向的几个信息块已经被时间侵蚀损坏。但随着重建算法的介入，一组文件还是被拼凑了出来，尽管可靠性评级低得令人不安。

补丁说明。

虽然硬件配置写得晦涩难懂，一团糟的软件里还充斥着无效库调用，但人类数学的通用语言还是勾勒出了设计意图。凭借那些，你的技术军官团队整合出一套探测此 "威胁" 所需的新传感器改装需求方案。

将这些需求方案适配到你相对现代的系统上，远比古人描述的艰巨工程要轻松得多。

entries.en:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam, I'm not sure it's working." Your sensors officer speaks, standing at a control console to demonstrate a first test of the adaptations. Line after line is dumped into an output log.

The characters sprout and repeat. Your technology officer's face is underlit by their glow.
entries.zh:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam ，我不确定它是否起效了。" 你的传感器技官站在控制台前说道，一边展示着适配方案的首次测试。一行行字符不断灌入输出日志。

那些符号不断涌现、重复，你的技术军官的脸庞也被它们的光芒所照亮。

entries.en: "Got a long-range hit..." Sensors reports. "Something is approaching our orbit. Without maneuvers we have one shift? Two? Half a day, max. What are your orders, $playerSirOrMadam?"
entries.zh: "远距接触..." 传感器技官报告。"有什么东西正高速向我们靠近，不进行规避的话我们会在一两个...不对，最多半个星历日的时间相遇。$playerSirOrMadam？你的命令是？"

entries.en:
Your sensors officer begins a preliminary high-power scan of the dark mass as your operations chief preps salvor teams.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, this looks... there's nothing quite like this on file, but..." Sensors gives up on words and pulls a detailed false-color scan into the primary display.

Someone lets out a gasp.

The database assistant algorithm won't provide a positive ID, but that form is unmistakable to the human eye.

This is the Onslaught Mk.I, the ship of legend.
entries.zh:
你的传感器技官准备对这漆黑的大块物体进行高功率扫描，同时行动长官也正在组织打捞小组。

"$PlayerSirOrMadam，档案中...没有匹配这玩意的条目，但是..." 传感器技官放弃用言语解释它，转而将详细的伪彩色扫描图像导入主显示器。

有人倒吸一口冷气。

尽管数据库无法提供匹配的信息，但任何人都能一眼辨认出它的轮廓。

那是 攻势 Mk.I，传说般的战舰。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet approaches the planetoid.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet靠近了小行星。

entries.en:
Your $shipOrFleet approaches the planetoid. Your sensors officer runs a standard sweep.

"Planetoid shows signs of heavy orbital bombardment by a warship, or a fleet," they report. "No atmo or tectonics. Not picking up any of the usual signs of rad-fallout. Looks like an old action. Very old."
entries.zh:
你的$shipOrFleet靠近了小行星。你的传感器技官进行了一次常规扫描。

"有迹象表明，这颗小行星经受过战舰或舰队的猛烈轨道轰炸。" 对方汇报说，"没有大气，没有地壳运动，没有任何常见的辐射尘。这是以前发生的事情，非常久以前。"

entries.en: The ancient war machine drifts, it's hull battered and scarred by aeons-old war. Power signs are minimal.
entries.zh: 这台战争机器漂流着，船体饱经沧桑，战痕累累。能源信号微乎其微。

entries.en: The vessel, heavily battered and with a minimal power signature, drifts through space. The silhouette is instantly recognizable but somehow crudely foreign.
entries.zh: 这艘战痕累累，几乎没有能量读数的舰船在太空中漂流着。它的轮廓极具辨识度，却又带着几分异样的粗犷感。

entries.en:
The image flickers and holds.

"Where is he, where is Dolos? I send scouts, agents, mercenaries, bribes, demands! Where is he!"

Maeus pounds his console - the image flickers precipitously, then stabilizes itself.
entries.zh:
影像闪了几下，稳定下来。

"他在哪儿，Dolos 在哪儿？我派了侦察艇、密探、雇佣兵，送贿赂、下通牒！他到底在哪儿！"

Maeus 一拳砸在控制台上——影像猛地一闪，随后又自行稳住。

entries.en:
"Strategy?" He laughs.

"I did as you said, captain. I came here to 'work with others'. I don't like it much. But this Achilles, he spoke to me. He's so like-"

Something catches in Maeus' throat, and for a moment, he just looks sad.
entries.zh:
"战略？"他笑了。

"我照你说的做了，舰长。我来这儿是为了'跟别人合作'。我不太喜欢。可这位 Achilles，他跟我说话了。他太像——"

Maeus 的喉咙一紧，有那么一刻，他只是显得很悲伤。

o.en: He reminds you of your son.

entries.en:
"Strategy?" He laughs, wildly.

"All these fleets, mercs, navies - they open comms and then officers squawk about 'tactics' and 'strategy', but are they the screams of Dolos Macario?"

He shakes his head.

"Until that I hear, I hear nothing. The wolves are hungry, captain." Moroz looks distant, now. "I must go to battle."

The comms cut, leaving you with his fading image.
entries.zh:
"战略？"他放声大笑，笑得有点疯。

"这么多舰队、雇佣兵、海军——他们打开通讯，军官们就嚷嚷什么'战术'、什么'战略'，可那里面有 Dolos Macario 的惨叫吗？"

他摇了摇头。

"在我听见那声音之前，我什么也听不见。狼群饿了，舰长。\"Moroz 此刻目光飘远。\"我得去打仗了。"

通讯切断，只留给你他那道渐渐消散的影像。

entries.en:
Some clever device provided by the mercs convinces the port authority automated scanners that two particular cargo containers are half-filled with mildly radioactive silicate gravel and nothing else.

Your logistics officer sneaks them aboard your $shipOrFleet without inconvenience.
entries.zh:
佣兵所提供的某种精巧装置骗过了港口当局的自动扫描仪，使其认定两个特定货柜内仅仅只是装有半满的微弱放射性硅酸盐砾石。

你的后勤官顺利将他们秘密装载至你的$shipOrFleet上，没有引起任何注意。

entries.en: A table of tattooed marine mercenaries bearing mil-grade cybermods are drinking alarming amounts of liquor.
entries.zh: 一桌有纹身的陆战队员正喝着数量惊人的烈酒。他们都植入了价值不菲的军用级生化改装部件。

entries.en: You wake up the next day in a small room above the bar with no particular memory of how you got there. How many more rounds was it with the mercs, one? Three?
entries.zh: 第二天，你在酒吧上面的一个小房间里醒了过来，根本回想不起自己是怎么到这的了。到底是又和那些佣兵喝了多少？一轮？三轮？

o.en: Join the table of tattooed mercs and see if their contract is up
o.zh: 你向这群带有纹身的佣兵走去，看看他们的雇佣合同是否到期

entries.en: With a word, any objections from the port authority disappear and your logistics officer arranges to have the mercs, looking worse from the night of drinking, board your $shipOrFleet the next morning.
entries.zh: 仅仅一句话，就让港口当局的所有异议烟消云散。这些因彻夜豪饮而更显颓态的佣兵，在你的后勤官安排下于次日清晨登上了你的$shipOrFleet。

entries.en:
$HeOrShe gives a wary smile.

"I can't do that, boss. I look after my squad, one and all, and they look after me. S'how it works."

$HisOrHer hand picks up an empty glass, as if to drink, pauses, then sets it back down.

"If you feel like you have to call MuniSec, then call MuniSec. Won't hold it against you."
entries.zh:
$heOrShe露出戒备的微笑。

"这可不行，老大。我得照看全队弟兄，他们也罩着我。规矩就是这样的。"

$hisOrHer用手拿起空杯似乎要喝，却又在停顿片刻放回原处。

"你要是觉得必须呼叫地方安全部，那就叫吧。我不会记恨的。"

entries.en:
You wake up the next day in the break room of the local security post, the lights dimmed for your benefit. You have no particular memory of how you got there. How many more rounds was it with the mercs, one? Three?

A senior munisec officer stands at stiff attention as you stumble out the door mumbling into your comms to arrange pickup.
entries.zh:
第二天，你在本地安保哨站的休息室里醒了过来，灯光也已被避免打扰你而被调暗。你根本想不起自己是怎么到这里的了，又到底是和那些佣兵喝了多少？一轮？还是三轮？

你跌跌撞撞地走出门口，从一位笔直立正的地方安全部高级官员身旁略过，含糊不清地对通讯器安排接应。

entries.en:
You give the order through your personal comms unit. A security squad will be there soon.

The merc leader sighs, looking remarkably accepting of $hisOrHer fate.

"Let us have this one last round?"
entries.zh:
你从你的个人通讯装置下了指令，一对安保人员很快会抵达。

佣兵领队叹了口气，显然已经接受了$hisOrHer命运。

"能让我们再喝最后一轮吗？"

o.zh: 允许佣兵们最后的狂欢

entries.en:
The band of rogue marines perform their last 'orbital drop' and are still cheering as security officers file into the bar.

There are alarmed looks, and hands reach toward hidden weapons, but they are stayed with a small motion from the merc leader.

"End of the line, my hardies. Go easy. We had a good run, and maybe we'll get out there once more."
entries.zh:
这群流氓陆战队员在安保警队进入酒吧时还是欢饮着，进行最后的 "轨道轰炸"。

有人露出惊恐的表情，伸手掏向隐藏着的武器，但被雇佣军领队一个小小的手势阻止了。

"闹剧到头了，伙计们。放松点，我们也玩的够开心了，也许我们会有天能重回天日。"

entries.en:
Security officers file into the bar. There are alarmed looks exchanged between the mercs, and scarred hands reach toward hidden weapons.

They are stayed with a small motion from the merc leader, who gives you one last sad look.

"End of the line, my hardies. Go easy; we had a good run."
entries.zh:
在安保警队进入酒吧时，有些惊恐的佣兵相互一视，用他们有伤痕的手伸向隐藏的武器。

但他们被雇佣军领队一个小小的手势制止了，而$hisOrHer用悲伤的眼神看了你最后一眼。

"闹剧到头了，硬汉们。我们玩得够开心了。"

o.en: Buy the contract. You're the boss, after all.
o.zh: 买下雇佣军的合同，反正在这里你说了算。

o.en: I have a duty here. I'm going to need to know why you're in trouble.
o.zh: 我对这里有着责任，我得知道为什么你们犯了什么事。

o.en: Call security to have the mercs locked up.
o.zh: 让安保人员把这些雇佣兵关起来。

o.en: Decline the proposal, but stay for an 'Orbital Bombardment' to soften the blow"
o.zh: 拒绝这个提议，但留下来与佣兵们来轮 "轨道轰炸" 缓和气氛

entries.en:
You prove yourself worthy of association by partaking in a round of 'Atmo Drops', a drink centered around consuming eye-watering liquor as quickly as possible.

The mercs are drunk, for sure, but composed enough to speak around the details of why they're being investigated by local authorities.

After a couple of the mercs head up to order a round of 'Orbital Bombardments' their leader pulls you aside and sketches out a proposal. "We've got $motr_numberOfMarines suits, experienced operators. We can fight in vac or atmo, one to five gee." He smirks at the look you give, "Okay, three. Four if it's quick and there's a bonus." A scarred hand dismisses this, "Details!"

"What matters is I'll offer our contract for $motr_priceText credits. Practically charity, isn't it? Put us to work, or sell it off elsewhere, doesn't matter to me if you can get us outta this fix. What'dya say?"
entries.zh:
你陪着喝了一轮 "大气圈直降"，一种主要比谁能最快灌完辣眼睛烈酒的喝法，证明了自己是个值得打交道的角色。

佣兵们肯定都喝高了，但还算保持着能谈吐的清醒，聊起了为什么他们被地方政府所追查的细节。

趁着几个雇佣兵起身去点一轮 "轨道轰炸" 的工夫，他们的领队把你拉到一边，给了一个提议："我们有 $motr_numberOfMarines 套装甲的人整装待发，个个都是经验丰富的好手。甭管是真空还是地面，一个G还是五个G，都能出动。"他对你的怀疑的样子笑了下，"好吧，最多三个G，如果有奖金而且只是简短行动的话，四个G也行。" 一只有疤痕的手挥过，"细枝末节就甭谈了！"

"重要的是我们的合同只要 $motr_priceText 星币。简直是在做慈善，对吧？给我们找点活干，或者在别的地方把合同再转让掉，只要能让我们摆脱这个困境就行，其他的我都不在乎。你怎么说？"

o.en: Buy the mercenary marine contract and sneak them off $entity.name
o.zh: 买下雇佣军的合同，然后偷偷溜出 $entity.name

o.en: Decline the proposal, but stay for an 'Orbital Bombardment' to soften the blow
o.zh: 拒绝这个提议，但留下来与佣兵们来轮 "轨道轰炸" 缓和气氛

entries.en:
You prove yourself worthy of association by partaking in a round of 'Atmo Drops', a drink centered around consuming eye-watering liquor as quickly as possible.

The mercs are drunk, for sure, but maintain their composure enough to speak around the details of why they're being investigated by local authorities - your local authorities.

After a couple of the mercs head up to order a round of 'Orbital Bombardments' their leader pulls you aside and sketches out a proposal. "We've got $motr_numberOfMarines suits, experienced operators. Be a shame if we couldn't see action, instead got locked up."

"I'll offer our contract for $motr_priceText credits. Practically charity, isn't it? Put us to work, or sell it off elsewhere, doesn't matter to me. After all," $heOrShe winks, "You're the boss around here, yeah? You can get us out of this fix."
entries.zh:
你陪着喝了一轮 "大气圈直降"，一种主要比谁能最快灌完辣眼睛烈酒的喝法，证明了自己是个值得打交道的角色。

佣兵们肯定都喝高了，但还算保持着能谈吐的清醒，聊起了为什么他们被地方政府所追查 —— 也就是所属于你的地方政府。

趁着几个雇佣兵起身去点一轮 "轨道轰炸" 的工夫，他们的领队把你拉到一边，给了一个提议："我们有 $motr_numberOfMarines 套装甲的人整装待发，都是经验丰富的好手，要是不能重回行动，而是被关进牢里的话就太可惜了。"

"重要的是我们的合同只要 $motr_priceText 星币。简直是在做慈善，对吧？给我们找点活干，或者在别的地方把合同再转让掉，我都不在意。毕竟话说回来，" $heOrShe向你眨了眨眼，"你就是这的头儿，对吧？你搞得定我们的烂摊子。"

entries.en: "Greetings! I've been waiting for this $mpm_commodityName shipment."
entries.zh: "您好！我一直在等这批 $mpm_commodityName。"

entries.en: "Greetings! I've been waiting for this $mpm_commodityName shipment. ... and I see that you don't have it yet. Well, you still have some time."
entries.zh: "您好！我一直在等这批 $mpm_commodityName ...但我看你现在还没有把它们送过来。好吧，你还有些时间。"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

"Greetings! I've been waiting for this $mpm_commodityName shipment."
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

"你好！我一直在等着这批 $mpm_commodityName。"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

"So, I hear you've got the stuff."
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

"不错，我听说你搞到了货。"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

"What? A shipment of $mpm_commodityName? I'm afraid I wouldn't know anyone interested in that sort of thing."

On the balance of things, perhaps waltzing into port without you turning your transponder off in order to get in touch with an underworld figure, wasn't the best idea you've ever had.
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

"什么？一批 $mpm_commodityName？恐怕我不认识对这种东西感兴趣的人。"

平心而论，你没有{关闭你的应答器}，就亮着你的身份大摇大摆地进入太空港去和一位黑道人物碰头，这恐怕算不上什么你这辈子最好的主意。

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

"Greetings! I've been waiting for this $mpm_commodityName shipment. ... and I see that you don't have it yet. Well, you still have some time."
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

"你好！我一直在等这批 $mpm_commodityName。... 但我看你现在还没有把它们送过来。好吧，你还有些时间。"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

"You haven't got the stuff, so why are we even talking?"
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

"货你都还没搞到手，我们谈个鬼？"

o.en: Explain that you don't have the $mpm_commodityName

entries.en: The comm link is cut before you have a chance to offer much of an explanation.
entries.zh: 在你有机会作出解释之前，通讯链接就被切断了。

entries.en:
The pirate $personRank looks up from $hisOrHer console.

"Well, now. Just hand over the $mpm_commodityName shipment we both know you've got in your cargo holds, and I'll let you be on your way."
entries.zh:
海盗 $personRank 从$hisOrHer控制台后抬起头来看向你。

"好了，现在。咱俩都知道的你的货舱有一批 $mpm_commodityName，只要把货物交出来，我就放你走。"

entries.en: The comm link is cut before you have a chance to say much of anything else.
entries.zh: 你还没来得及再开口说话，通讯链接就被切断了。

entries.en: Select the campaign difficulty level. "Easy" is recommended for a first-time player.
entries.zh: 选择生涯模式的难度。"简单" 适合初次游玩的玩家。

o.en: An explorer, leading a salvage expedition from aboard an Apogee-class cruiser (faster start)
o.zh: 一名探险者，在一艘至高点-级巡洋舰上指挥着一支打捞探险舰队 (轻松开局)

o.en: A mercenary, leading a small force from aboard a Hammerhead-class destroyer (faster start)
o.zh: 一名雇佣兵，在一艘锤头-级驱逐舰上指挥着一支小型部队 (轻松开局)

entries.en: In addition, your fleet includes...
entries.zh: 此外，你的舰队还包括...

o.en: A Kite-class shuttle, under the command of an experienced subordinate
o.zh: 一艘风筝-级穿梭机，由一名经验丰富的军官指挥着。

o.en: A Shepherd class drone tender, with a cargo of heavy machinery
o.zh: 一艘牧羊人-级无人机补给舰，运载了一些重型机械。

o.en: A freelancer, doing whatever jobs you've been able to find (randomized start)
o.zh: 一名自由职业者，接手你能找到的任何工作 (随机开局)

o.en: A mechanic, taking a desperate chance and buying a broken-down Hyperion-class frigate from a client
o.zh: 一名机械师，孤注一掷，从客户手里买下一艘破旧的 亥伯龙-级 护卫舰

o.en: A mercenary, recently acquiring a high-tech vessel (randomized start)
o.zh: 一名雇佣兵，刚弄到一艘高科技舰船 (随机开局)

o.en: A freelancer, cobbling together a modest fleet (randomized start)
o.zh: 一名自由从业者，东拼西凑出一支不大的舰队 (随机开局)

o.en: A spacer. A broken-down shuttle. A lifelong debt. (very hard)
o.zh: 一个太空佬，一架破穿梭机，以及一笔终身债务。 (困难开局)

o.en: A spacer. A broken-down shuttle. A lifelong obligation. (very hard)
o.zh: 一名太空人。一艘破穿梭机。一笔还不清的债。 (极难)

o.en: A scavenger, commanding a Wayfarer-class combat freighter
o.zh: 一名拾荒者，指挥着一艘远行者-级武装商舰

o.en: A bounty hunter, commanding a Wolf-class frigate
o.zh: 一名赏金猎人，指挥着一艘野狼-级护卫舰

o.en: Weren't you the portmaster for Nomios? What happened?
o.zh: 你以前不是 Nomios 的港务长吗？出了什么事？

entries.en:
"You," $heOrShe says. $HisOrHer anger is obvious. "You happened.

"You ruined everything. My career, the lawsuit... I should never have answered the comms."

"Don't speak to me ever again."

$HeOrShe slams the comms cut-off.
entries.zh:
"你，"$heOrShe 说。$HisOrHer 的怒气毫不掩饰。"就是你惹出来的。"

"你毁了一切。我的前程，那场官司...我当初就不该接那通通讯。"

"再也别跟我说话。"

$HeOrShe 猛地切断了通讯。

o.en: Didn't you used to be the quartermaster?

entries.en:
$PersonName sighs. "Yeah. Was a good gig for a while, wasn't it."

"Mister Blanc took exception to my talking with you," $heOrShe says with a shrug. "Never seen him that mad. Probably good for his circulation, if you ask me."

$HeOrShe trails off, looking downcast.
entries.zh:
$PersonName 叹了口气。"是啊。有一阵子这差事挺好，不是吗。"

"Blanc 先生对我跟你说话很不满意，\"$heOrShe 耸耸肩，\"从没见他气成那样。要我说，对他血液循环说不定还有好处。"

$HeOrShe 话音渐低，垂下眼去。

o.en: Need a job? You could crew with me.
o.zh: 要份差事吗？可以到我的船上干。

o.en: Good luck, I'm sure you'll find a good orbit soon.
o.zh: 祝你好运。你肯定很快就能找到条好轨道。

entries.en:
"Way the stars fall sometimes." $HeOrShe shrugs.

"Well, I've gotta get on with packing up my berth. Burn bright, captain."
entries.zh:
"星星有时候就是这么落的。"$HeOrShe 耸了耸肩。

"好了，我得去收拾铺位了。烧得亮些，舰长。"

entries.en:
$HeOrShe looks up.

"Yeah. Yeah, wouldn't mind that. That's very decent of you, captain."
entries.zh:
$HeOrShe 抬起头。

"行。行，我不介意。你真是厚道，舰长。"

o.en: Comms your purser and make the arrangements
o.zh: 联络你的事务长，把事情安排妥当

entries.en: The arrangements are made and $personName joins your crew. You make sure that the seniority $heOrShe earned working for Mbaye-Gogol is respected.
entries.zh: 安排妥当，$personName 加入了你的船员。你确保 $heOrShe 在 Mbaye-Gogol 任职时挣下的资历得到尊重。

entries.en:
"Yeah." $HeOrShe shrugs. "Maybe."

"Well, I've gotta get on with packing up my berth. Burn bright, captain."
entries.zh:
"是啊。\"$HeOrShe 耸耸肩。\"也许吧。"

"好了，我得去收拾铺位了。烧得亮些，舰长。"

entries.en:
The comms resolve to $post $PersonLastName sitting stiffly.

"Welcome to Nomios. On behalf of the Mbaye-Gogol corporation," $heOrShe says, "I would like to welcome you to the 'Sanctuary of the Persean Sector'."
entries.zh:
通讯接通，画面里是坐得笔直的 $post $PersonLastName。

"欢迎来到 Nomios。我代表 Mbaye-Gogol 公司，\"$heOrShe说，\"欢迎你来到'英仙座星域的圣所'。"

entries.en: "Welcome... again, captain. On behalf of the Mbaye-Gogol corporation, is there anything else you needed?"
entries.zh: "再次... 欢迎你，舰长。代表 Mbaye-Gogol 公司——你还需要别的什么吗？"

entries.en:
The comms resolve to $Post $PersonLastName.

"Welcome... to Nomios," $heOrShe says stiffly. "On behalf of the Mbaye-Gogol corporation."

"I don't think we have anything else to discuss."
entries.zh:
通讯接通，画面里是 $Post $PersonLastName。

"欢迎... 来到 Nomios，"$heOrShe生硬地说，"我代表 Mbaye-Gogol 公司。"

"我想我们没什么别的可谈了。"

entries.en:
The comms resolve to $post $PersonLastName sitting stiffly.

"Welcome to-"

$HisOrHer eyes narrow. "You. What could you possibly want?"
entries.zh:
通讯接通，画面里是坐得笔直的 $post $PersonLastName。

"欢迎来到——"

$HisOrHer眯起眼睛。"你。你还想要什么？"

entries.en:
"I see, I see," $heOrShe puts $hisOrHer hands together, considering $hisOrHer next words.

"There's an official process. Find a sponsor, send a delegation to meet the League Council, a question period, a vote." $HisOrHer eyes turn to you now, somehow meeting yours through the comms. "But what you're going to want to do is talk to Reynard Hannan. Nothing will move through the League Council unless Gens Hannan allows it." $HisOrHer eyes turn away again, and $heOrShe gives a small shrug.

"Welcome to Kazeron."
entries.zh:
"我明白，我明白。" $heOrShe把$hisOrHer的手插在一起，斟酌$hisOrHer的下一个答复。

"这里需要办理一个官方手续。诸如找一个担保人，派一个代表团与联盟理事会会晤，过一个问答环节，过一个投票。" 此时$HisOrHer的视线朝向了你，透过通讯偶然间与你的视线交汇。"但是你真正要去做的是和 Reynard Hannan 谈一谈。联盟理事会的任何决议都不会通过，除非获得了 Hannan 氏族的准许。" $HisOrHer的眼神再次飘了出去，然后耸了耸肩。

"欢迎来到 Kazeron。"

entries.en: You decline the comms request and continue on your way.
entries.zh: 你拒绝了通讯请求，继续上路。

entries.en: Your comm link buzzes angrily - it's a priority message from one of your fleet officers.
entries.zh: 你的通讯链接恼火地嗡嗡作响 —— 是你麾下一名舰队军官发来的优先通讯。

entries.en:
It takes quite some time - describing what you do as "pleading" would sound more undignified than the fictions all parties involved tacitly agree to maintain - but you do your best to smooth over hard feelings, rebuild trust, and some make not-quite-promises about the future which finally convince them to stick with your operation.

After all, they could be guarding ore shipments from starving pirates. At least you present a glimpse of ambition, a glimmer of possibility, a chance at glory!

They may roll their eyes at such talk, but you can tell it sparks at something primary. These are mercenary officiers, not accountants; they live for this.
entries.zh:
这颇费了些工夫 —— 若把你做的事称作"恳求"，未免比各方心照不宣维持的那套说辞更失体面 —— 可你还是尽力抚平了芥蒂、重建了信任，又半真半假地许下些关于往后的诺言，总算劝得他们留在了你的麾下。

说到底，他们本可以去给矿石船队当护卫，防些饿疯了的海盗。至少你这儿还摆着一点野心、一线可能、一个博取功名的机会！

这类话他们兴许会翻个白眼，可你看得出它戳中了某种最本真的东西。这些是雇佣兵军官，不是账房先生；他们就为这个活着。

entries.en: You cut the comm link, shake your head, and consider your options.
entries.zh: 你切断通讯，摇了摇头，盘算起眼下的选择。

entries.en:
There's nothing to be done but accept the resignation.

They'll go off-duty until your $shipOrFleet docks at a port of call then go their own way.
entries.zh:
事已至此，唯有接受辞呈。

他们会先歇岗，等你的$shipOrFleet靠上某处停靠港，便各奔前程。

entries.en:
A nod. "Thank you, $playerSirOrMadam. I won't let you down."
OR
"Glad to hear it, $playerSirOrMadam," $heOrShe says. "I'll let my bridge crew know you've taken a personal interest."
OR
"I appreciate your transparency, $playerSirOrMadam."

$HeOrShe performs a salute.
OR
"Understood, $playerSirOrMadam. I'll ensure that my performance exceeds expectations."
entries.zh:
点了点头。"多谢您，$playerSirOrMadam。我不会让您失望。"
OR
"这话我爱听，$playerSirOrMadam，\" $heOrShe说道。\"我会让舰桥上的弟兄知道，您亲自过问了这事。"
OR
"多谢您把话讲得这么透，$playerSirOrMadam。"

$HeOrShe敬了个礼。
OR
"明白，$playerSirOrMadam。我保证往后表现超出您的预期。"

entries.en:
"Look, $playerSirOrMadam. This has happened before and I can't do my job if you won't let me," $heOrShe says.

"It's not just a matter of credits, it's a matter of pride... and respect. If you can't respect me enough to lead in combat, then perhaps your organization is not the right place for my expertise."
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam," $hisOrHer look is more than skeptical. "I want to believe you, but I value actions over words. And with all due respect, I've heard these words from you before."
OR
"I'm not in the business of making excuses, $playerSirOrMadam. What am I supposed to tell my subordinates? That you don't have confidence in my ability to lead them in combat?"

$HeOrShe shakes $hisOrHer head dismissively. "I'm a professional. I cannot do my work if I am not treated as such."
entries.zh:
"您听我说，$playerSirOrMadam。这种事不是头一回了，您再这么不放手，我这活没法干，" $heOrShe说道。

"这不光是钱的事，是脸面...也是敬重。您若连让我带兵打仗都不肯给这份尊重，那您这摊子，怕是容不下我这身本事。"
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam，\" $hisOrHer神情岂止是怀疑。\"我愿意信您，可我看重的是行动，不是空话。恕我直言，这些话我从前就听您说过了。"
OR
"我向来不替自己找借口，$playerSirOrMadam。您让我怎么跟手下交代？说您信不过我带他们打仗的本事？"

$HeOrShe不以为然地摇了摇$hisOrHer头。"我是个职业军人。不把我当职业军人待，我这活就干不了。"

o.en: Look, we're going to figure out how to make this work...
o.zh: 听我说，这事咱们总能把办法想出来...

entries.en:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam," $heOrShe begins with a stern look, "I must respectfully inquire if you've lost confidence in my command ability."

"You've revoked my assignment to $reassignedShipName for a fleet action, then placed me back in command of the same vessel. This undermines my authority with subordinate officers and crew alike."
OR
"I thank you for taking the time to personally discuss this matter," $heOrShe begins. "You assigned me to $reassignedShipName, pulled me from command during battle, then re-assigned me to that same ship."

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, if I've let you down, I accept judgement and will take appropriate corrective action. But I cannot commit to your standards of excellence if you cannot commit me to a command."
OR
"I wish only to serve with distinction, $playerSirOrMadam," $heOrShe says. "But I cannot commit to the discipline and consistency required for successful command if you pull me from $reassignedShipName for combat, then place me back in command after it is concluded."

"With all due respect," $heOrShe says with a tone of self-justified affront, "it makes me look bad. I am sure we both understand the importance of building a culture of respect in one's subordinates. I cannot do that if I am ordered absent for the most critical periods of leadership."
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam, thank you for taking the time," $heOrShe begins.

"I wish to, respectfully, bring complaint regarding your order to assign me away from $reassignedShipName during an important combat action. I've put a great deal of effort into building a rapport with my junior officers and crew, and to appear to abandon them... $playerSirOrMadam, it has a negative impact on morale and readiness which does not meet my professional standards."
entries.zh:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam，\" $heOrShe神色严峻地开了口，\"我得冒昧问一句，您是不是对我的指挥能力失去了信心。"

"舰队行动前，您撤了我对$reassignedShipName的任命，转头又让我回去指挥同一艘船。这让我在下级军官和全体船员面前都立不住威信。"
OR
"多谢您肯抽空亲自谈这件事，\" $heOrShe开了口。\"您把我派到$reassignedShipName，战斗中又撤了我的指挥权，仗打完再把我派回同一艘船。"

"$PlayerSirOrMadam，若是我有负所托，我甘领处分，也会照章纠偏。可您若连一支部队都不肯交给我带，我也就没法向您那套卓越标准看齐了。"
OR
"我只想建功立业地效力，$playerSirOrMadam，\" $heOrShe说道。\"可您若临战把我从$reassignedShipName调走、事毕又让我官复原职，我就没法守住带兵所必需的那份纪律与一贯。"

"恕我直言，\" $heOrShe语气里带着自觉受了冒犯的委屈，\"这让我面上难看。在下级心里养出敬重的风气有多要紧，想必你我都很清楚。可最该由我坐镇的时候偏把我支开，这风气我养不起来。"
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam，多谢您抽空，" $heOrShe开了口。

"我想郑重提一桩申诉：在一场要紧的战斗里，您下令把我从$reassignedShipName调离。我花了大把心力才同手下的年轻军官和船员处出默契，这么做像是临阵抛下了他们... $playerSirOrMadam，士气与战备因此受的损，够不上我的职业标准。"

o.en: Acknowledged. I'll avoid unnecessary re-assignments in the future.
o.zh: 明白。往后我会避免不必要的调动。

o.en: Look, I was just trying to save a bit on combat pay.
o.zh: 唉，我不过是想省点战斗津贴罢了。

entries.en:
$HeOrShe nods skeptically. "Um. Understood, $playerSirOrMadam."
OR
"Acknowledged, $playerSirOrMadam."

$HisOrHer tone is distinctly unimpressed.
OR
"I see, uh, $playerSirOrMadam," $heOrShe says uneasily, then performs an unenthusiastic salute.
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam," $heOrShe answers robotically. You can see the disappointment in $hisOrHer eyes.
entries.zh:
$HeOrShe将信将疑地点了点头。"呃。明白，$playerSirOrMadam。"
OR
"明白，$playerSirOrMadam。"

$HisOrHer语气里明摆着不以为然。
OR
"这样啊，呃，$playerSirOrMadam，" $heOrShe局促地说道，随后有气无力地敬了个礼。
OR
"$PlayerSirOrMadam，" $heOrShe木然应道。你看得见$hisOrHer眼里的失望。

o.zh: 那要看情况。你能做些什么？

o.en: I can't hire on any more administrators at the moment.
o.zh: 目前我无法聘用更多的管理员了。

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

$personName looks you over appraisingly.

"Heard you might be looking to take on some help."
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

$personName 上下打量了你一番。

"听说你想找些帮手？"

entries.en:
After a short wait, your connection request is accepted.

$personName looks you over in eager appraisal.

"Word is you might be getting into the colony business. If so, I might be of some help - you will find that my credentials are impeccable."
entries.zh:
短暂的等待过后，你的连接请求被接受了。

$personName 饶有兴致地审视着你。

"有传言说你也许会参手殖民地业务。如果是这样，我也许能帮上些忙。你会发现我的资质无可挑剔。"

entries.en:
Your connection request is accepted promptly.

$personName looks you over appraisingly. You get the feeling that $heOrShe could probably guess your credit balance to the nearest hundred-count.

"If you're looking for an experienced freelance officer - on a strictly temporary basis - I'm looking to take on a client. My asking rate is high, but you'd be losing money trusting one of your ships to someone with less experience."
OR
Your comms request is promptly accepted.

$personName looks you over for a moment then nods as if you've passed some kind of test.

"If you are looking to hire an experienced combat officer on a limited-time contract, then you've come to the right place. I think you will find my terms reasonable.  Excellence does not come cheap."
entries.zh:
你的连接请求被迅速接受了。

$personName 上下打量了你一番。你觉得$heOrShe说不定能猜透你的星币余额，偏差不过百位。

"如果你正在寻找一个经验丰富的自由职业军官的话，那正巧，我也在找一个客户，不过仅限临时雇佣。我的要价很高，但把你的船交给那些经验不足的家伙会更加赔钱。"
OR
你的通讯请求被迅速接受了。

$personName 看了你一会儿，然后点了点头，好比你通过了某种考验一样。

"如果你想短期雇佣一名有经验的战斗人员，那么你就找对地方了。我觉得你马上就会发现我的开价并不离谱。毕竟，卓越从不廉价。"

entries.en:
Your connection request is accepted after an extended delay.

$personName looks you over with barely concealed suspicion.

"You have a bit of a reputation in the, ah, freelancing community. But I do need the credits. So: if you need the services of a better ship's captain than you probably deserve, here's your chance. I will, of course, have to charge a premium for the risk entailed by your engagement."
OR
The comms link opens after a significant delay.

$personName looks you over with a flicker of disapproval.

"I've heard of you, $playerName, and despite your... mixed reputation, I am willing to deal. After all," $heOrShe takes a philosophical tone, "I wouldn't be a mercenary if the offer of enough credits didn't turn my head against my better judgment."

"Now impress me."
entries.zh:
你的连接请求在一段漫长的延迟后终于被接受了。

$personName 以不加掩饰的怀疑态度打量着你。

"你的名声在那个，啊，在那个自由佣兵圈子里不太好。不过我现在的确得赚些星币。所以如果你想雇一个活干得好，更配得上你的家伙，那么现在机会来了。当然，我将不得不为受你聘用所带来的风险加收一笔费用。"
OR
通讯链接在经过明显的拖延之后接通了。

$personName 看了看你，眼中带着一丝不满。

"我听说过你，$playerName，尽管你的名声有点... 褒贬不一，但我还是愿意和你谈谈。毕竟，" $heOrShe摆出了一副豁达的口吻，"有钱能使鬼推磨，如果我不是这种人，就不会干雇佣兵这一行。"

"怎样，让我开开眼吧。"

entries.en:
You input the connection request. The standby signal persists for so long you are about to ask comms to check their equipment - and the channel opens.

$personName looks you over with barely concealed hostility.

"Your reputation precedes you, $playerName. Frankly, I don't need your credits. And I don't want to see your face."

$HeOrShe pauses for a moment.

"Safe travels."

$HeOrShe cuts the comm link.
OR
The commlink blinks on standby for a near eternity. Your comms officer indicates that it is indeed working correctly and shrugs. You are about to order the request canceled when the connection opens.

$personName looks to you in mock surprise. "I'm so sorry for the delay, it's just that I've heard all the stories about $playerName, and I couldn't believe it was really you. Contacting me! What luck."

You begin to sense an air of sarcasm as $heOrShe continues, "... Because now I get to tell everyone that I got the chance to tell you to suck vacuum!"

The link is hard-cut while $personName is performing a rude-gesture. Your comms officer keeps a stony face toward their console as they clear the screen.
entries.zh:
你提交了连接请求。待机信号持续了很久，你正准备让通讯军官检查设备时，频道接通了。

$personName 带着几乎毫不掩饰的敌意看了你一眼。

"你已经臭名远扬了，$playerName。老实说，我不需要你的星币。我也不想看到你的脸。"

$HeOrShe停顿了一会儿。

"出门时小心点。"

$HeOrShe切断了通讯链接。
OR
通讯链接的待机画面一直在没完没了地闪烁着。你的通讯军官耸了耸肩，表示它确实在正常工作。你正准备下令取消这个请求时，通讯接通了。

$personName 看向你，装作一副惊讶的样子。"很抱歉耽误了您宝贵的时间，我才刚听说了所有关于 $playerName 的故事，有点不敢相信真的遇到了您。而您居然主动跟我联系？真走运！"

你开始感觉到一种讽刺的气氛，而这时$heOrShe继续说了下去，"... 因为现在我可以和大伙炫耀，我终于有机会对你讲 —— 吸他妈的真空去吧！"

$personName 做出一个粗鲁的手势并强行切断了通讯。你的通讯军官朝着控制台板着脸，把屏幕清空了。

entries.en: You cut the comm link after exchanging a few pleasantries.
entries.zh: 你在寒暄了几句后切断了通讯链接。

entries.en: You look around the bridge. The junior officers are all remarkably busy, with no-one even glancing in your direction.
entries.zh: 你环顾舰桥。下级军官们都不太自然地忙碌着，甚至都没人向你的方向瞟一眼。

entries.en: You cut the comm link after exchanging a few hollow pleasantries.
entries.zh: 你在敷衍地寒暄了几句后切断了通讯链接。

o.en: I can't afford that at the moment.
I'll need to think about this.

entries.en: "That's very unfortunate. I'm certain you're still planning on promptly surrendering the contraband, correct?"
entries.zh: "那还真是不幸。但我相信你还是打算及时交出违禁品，对吧？"

entries.en: "That's very unfortunate. Your failure to pay will be noted in your file."
entries.zh: "那还真是不幸。你无法缴清费用的行为将被记录在案。"

entries.en: "Thank you for your cooperation. It will be noted in your file." $personRank $personName nods and cuts the comm link.
entries.zh: "感谢你的配合，这将记入你的档案。" $personName $personRank 点点头，随即切断了通讯链接。

entries.en: "Thank you for your cooperation." $personRank $personName nods and cuts the comm link.
entries.zh: "感谢你的配合。" $personName $personRank 点点头，随即切断了通讯链接。

entries.en:
"That's something you're going to regret very, very much."

The comm link is cut before you have a chance to respond.
entries.zh:
"你会非常后悔这个决定的。"

没等你做出回应，通讯链接就被切断了。

entries.en: $personName looks at you carefully, and, for whatever reason, doesn't press the issue. After a couple of seconds of silence, you cut the comm link.
entries.zh: $personName 诚惶诚恐地看着你，但总之不管出于什么原因，$heOrShe并没有与你发生争执。经历了几秒钟的沉默之后，你切断了通讯链接。

entries.en:
"That's something you're going to regret."

The comm link is cut before you have a chance to respond.
entries.zh:
"你会后悔的。"

没等你做出回应，通讯链接就被切断了。

entries.en: $personName glares at you, but, for whatever reason, doesn't press the issue. After a couple of seconds of silence, you cut the comm link.
entries.zh: $personName 瞪着你，但出于某些原因没有开口与你争执。经历了几秒钟的沉默之后，你切断了通讯链接。

o.en: Use the local facilities to refit your $shipOrFleet
o.zh: 使用本地的设施改装你的$shipOrFleet

entries.en:
"Wait." $HeOrShe looks at you disapprovingly. "Aren't you the spacer that tried to shoot Moroz? I'd be careful showing my face around here, if I were you."
OR
After a moment a dark look crosses the $rank's face. "I recognize you. There was a bulletin from munisec. You're that spacer that pulled on a gun on Moroz."
OR
The $post does a double-take.

"Hey! You're that crazy spacer that pulled on Maeus Moroz when he had his back turned... like a coward."
entries.zh:
"等等。\"$HeOrShe不以为然地打量你。\"你不就是那个想开枪打 Moroz 的太空佬？换作我，在这儿露脸会小心点。"
OR
片刻之后，$rank 脸上掠过一道阴沉的阴影。"我认得你。治安局发过通报。你就是那个拔枪对着 Moroz 的太空佬。"
OR
$post 愣了一下，又猛地看回来。

"嘿！你就是那个疯子太空佬，趁 Maeus Moroz 背对着你的时候拔枪...像个懦夫。"

entries.en:
"Wait." $HeOrShe looks at you disapprovingly. "You're not that spacer that shot Moroz in the back, are you? You've got some nerve showing your face around here."
OR
After a moment a dark look crosses the $rank's face. "I recognize you. There was a bulletin from munisec. You're that spacer that shot Moroz!"
OR
The $post does a double-take.

"You're that crazy spacer that shot Maeus Moroz in the back... like a coward."
entries.zh:
"等等。\"$HeOrShe不以为然地打量你。\"你不会就是那个从背后开枪打 Moroz 的太空佬吧？你还敢在这儿露面，胆子倒不小。"
OR
片刻之后，$rank 脸上掠过一道阴沉的阴影。"我认得你。治安局发过通报。你就是那个开枪打 Moroz 的太空佬！"
OR
$post 愣了一下，又猛地看回来。

"你就是那个疯子太空佬，从背后开枪打了 Maeus Moroz...像个懦夫。"

entries.en:
"And if that wasn't enough, you blew his fleet out of the sky." $HeOrShe shakes $hisOrHer head, making $hisOrHer feelings on the matter quite clear.
OR
"Then you ambushed his fleet in orbit to finish the job." $HeOrShe shakes $hisOrHer head at the injustice.
OR
"If that wasn't enough, you attacked him in orbit. It's amazing you weren't declared pirate then and there."
entries.zh:
"这还不够，你把他整支舰队从天上打了下来。"$HeOrShe摇着$hisOrHer的头，$hisOrHer对此事的态度再清楚不过。
OR
"然后你又在轨道上伏击了他的舰队，好把事做绝。"$HeOrShe为这桩不公摇着$hisOrHer的头。
OR
"这还不算，你还在轨道上袭击了他。你当场没被宣布为海盗，真是奇迹。"

o.en: He wanted someone to blame and was going to attack me! It was self defense.
o.zh: 他想找个人顶罪，还打算动手杀我！那是自卫。

o.en: I'm not going to apologize, so don't ask.
o.zh: 我不会道歉，所以别开口。

o.en: Don't talk to me about Moroz.

entries.en:
"Maybe he wanted someone to blame," $heOrShe concedes. "But you can't just gun people down."

"Anyway, I don't want to hear your excuses. Let's just get this over with so you can burn nice and bright... away from Orthrus."
entries.zh:
"也许他确实想找个人顶罪，\"$heOrShe让步道，\"可你不能就这么开枪把人打死。"

"总之，我不想听你的借口。赶紧把事办完了，好让你烧得亮亮堂堂...离 Orthrus 远些。"

entries.en:
"I didn't," $heOrShe says coldly.

"Now, can we conclude whatever business you have here? Quickly?"
entries.zh:
"我没有，"$heOrShe冷冷地说。

"现在，能不能把你在这里的事办完？快点。"

entries.en:
$HeOrShe takes a deep breath.

"What do you want? Let's get this over with."
entries.zh:
$HeOrShe深吸一口气。

"你到底要什么？把事了了吧。"

entries.en: "Wow." She hands the sample container back to you.
entries.zh: "哇哦。" 她把样本容器递还给你。

entries.en: "Wow. Guess that explains why the newscasts have been so boring today. Luddics, right?" She hands the sample container back to you.
entries.zh: "哇哦，难怪今天的新闻这么无聊。卢德佬，对吧？" 她把样本容器递还给你。

entries.en:
"You find some interesting stuff out there if you don't mind me saying so, captain."

She nods approvingly. "Thank you for the subsidy. I'll be sure to enjoy myself once I wrap up this miserable Asher contract."
entries.zh:
"如果你不介意我直说的话 —— 舰长，你在外面总能发现些有趣玩意儿。"

她赞许地点点头，"感谢你的资助。等结束这份该死的 Asher 合同后，我肯定会好好享受一番。"

entries.en: Senior Engineer Tanaica sends you on your way back to orbit with no more farewell than a succinct "Right then."
entries.zh: 高级工程师 Tanaica 只简短地说了句 "那就这样"，便将你送返了轨道。

entries.en:
"Alright."

She glances aside, not bothering to hide that she's checking the time.
entries.zh:
"行吧。"

她瞥向一旁，毫不掩饰地查看着时间。

entries.en: She shrugs. "It's your credits."
entries.zh: 她耸耸肩。"随你，反正是你的星币。"

o.en: I'd like you to look at a material sample. I'll pay.
o.zh: 我希望你分析一份材料样本，我会付钱。

entries.en:
"Hmm," she gives you a renewed look of interest. "You're the one who had the glove. Right."

"Well you had me at 'pay', captain. Come on down and we'll have a look at... what did you say you had?"
entries.zh:
"嗯，" 她重新显露出感兴趣的神色，"你就是那个持有手套的人。对吧。"

"好吧，'付钱' 这词就够打动我了，舰长。过来吧，我们瞧瞧...你刚说有什么来着？"

entries.en:
Descending to Asher, you glance out the viewport of your shuttle.

Stars disappear from the black tapestry of space as it begins to glow with a deep violet-blue before sinking into dim, ruddy brown.

The thick clouds of suspended fines are whipped away by the shuttle's flight through cold winds, and the shadow is replaced by the generalized sandy murk of Asher.
entries.zh:
在降向 Asher 的途中，你透过穿梭机的舷窗向外看去。

星辰从太空的漆黑色织锦中逐渐消失，深邃的紫蓝色光芒开始蔓延，最终沉入昏暗的红褐色朦胧中。

悬浮的细尘云层被穿梭机在寒风中疾驰的轨迹搅散，阴影被 Asher 遍布的沙尘迷雾所取代。

entries.en:
"The Abyss?" Her eyes widen. "You're braver than you look. Or stupider."

"Anyway, come on down. I'll feed some excuse to traffic control."
entries.zh:
"深渊？" 她睁大眼睛，"你比看上去更勇敢，或者更愚蠢。"

"总之，下来吧。我会给交通管制编个借口。"

o.en: Shuttle down with the armor sample
o.zh: 携带装甲样本乘坐穿梭机降落

o.en: A piece of modular armor found in the Abyss.
o.zh: 一块在深渊中发现的模块化装甲。

entries.en:
* * *

"Doesn't look like much, does it," says Senior Engineer Tanaica as she takes the sample from you - a block of armor composite, edges rough from the salvors' plasma cutters.

She places the sample onto a shelf which retracts into the towering white casing of the analysis suite. Transparent panes reveal the machine's arcane inner workings.

"You found it in the Abyss, you said?"

A containment shield drops over the sample port with a satisfying clunk.
entries.zh:
* * *

"看着没什么特别，是吧，" 高级工程师 Tanaica 说着从你手中接过样本 —— 一块装甲复合材料，其边缘因打捞员们的等离子切割而粗糙不平。

她将样本放入一个隔层，隔层随即缩进高耸的白色分析套件外壳中。透明面板展示着仪器精密的内部构造。

"你说这是在深渊发现的？"

一道防护罩咔嗒一声落在样品端口上方，发出利落的声响。

o.en: A planetoid in the Abyss. Some nameless rock.
o.zh: 深渊里的一颗小行星。一颗无名岩质星球。

entries.en:
"Most of 'em are, aren't they."

She manipulates the controls, evacuating the atmo from the sample container. Then she stops to look at you.

"If this is just a chunk of starship armor, I can tell you that for free. Saves you 10,000 credits."

"But if you want me to look real close and do some professional speculation," she holds out her datapad, ready to receive payment.
entries.zh:
"多数样本不都这样吗。"

她操作着控制台，抽空样本容器的空气，随后停下手看向你。

"如果这只是块星舰装甲的碎片，我现在就能免费告诉你答案。帮你省下 10,000 星币。"

"但如果你要我仔细检验并给出专业推测，" 她递出数据平板，准备接收付款。

o.en: It's a piece of armor. I'll take it and go.
o.zh: 这只是块装甲，我带走它就是了。

o.en: I'll consider it. If I find out more
o.zh: 我会考虑的，如果我有进一步发现。

o.en: Have you heard of the Onslaught mk.I?
o.zh: 你听说过 攻势 Mk.I 吗？

entries.en:
The sample emerges, and - more gingerly, now - Senior Engineer Tanaica pulls on some gloves and places it back in your sample container.

"You find some interesting stuff out there if you don't mind me saying so, captain."

She nods approvingly. "Thank you for the subsidy. I'll be sure to enjoy myself once I wrap up this miserable Asher contract."
entries.zh:
随着样本重新出现，高级工程师 Tanaica 此时更加谨慎地戴上手套，将其放回你的样本容器。

"如果你不介意我直说的话 —— 舰长，你在外面总能发现些有趣玩意儿。"

她赞许地点点头，"感谢你的资助。等结束这份该死的 Asher 合同后，我肯定会好好享受一番。"

entries.en:
Your TriPad pings confirmation, and hers responds cheerfully.

"Right then," she says, equally cheerful.

Tanaica's datapad disappears as she turns back to the controls. A loud humming grows - it feels almost ticklish in your teeth for a moment as she adjusts power levels.

Displays bloom with readouts, cheerful greens abounding. A holo of the sample flickers into being.
entries.zh:
你的 TriPad 响起确认的提示音，她的设备也欢快地进行了回应。

"那好，" 她同样愉快地说道。

随着数据平板在手中消失，Tanaica 转身开始操作控制台。一阵响亮的嗡鸣声逐渐响起 —— 当她调整功率时，那种震动感几乎让你的牙根发痒。

显示屏绽放出读数，满目皆是欢快的绿色指示，样本的全息影像闪烁成形。

entries.en:
The machine's hum drops an octave, and loses some of its urgency.

"Huh," she says. She wears a look of blank unease.

"Weird."
entries.zh:
机器的嗡鸣声降低了几分，紧迫感也减弱了不少。

"哈，" 她说道，脸上带着茫然的困惑。

"奇怪。"

entries.en:
Tanaica manipulates her controls and a small cutaway pulls out of the rough block of armor. It scales to fill the volume of the holo.

Another segmentation of scale iterates, then another as Tanaica brings the resolution to the nearly-atomic. Patterns of false colour flash highlighting pseudo-crystals, various regular - and irregular - structures, as well as flaws.

"It's the damnedest thing, isn't it," she says, attention focused on the display.
entries.zh:
Tanaica 操作着控制台，一小块剖面从粗糙的装甲块中被提取出来。它被逐渐放大，直至填满整个全息投影空间

又一次尺度分割迭代，接着又一次，Tanaica 将分辨率提升到近原子级别。伪彩色图样闪烁着，高亮显示出伪晶体、各种规则与不规则结构，以及瑕疵。

"这可真够邪门的，是吧，" 她说道，注意力完全集中在显示屏上。

o.en: Definitely. Wow. Look at that. The... ah...
o.zh: 绝对如此。哇哦，看那个，这...呃...

entries.en:
"Sorry, cap," she says. "I should be thinking out loud, you paid good credits for this after all."

She licks her lips, then releases a breath.
entries.zh:
"抱歉，舰长，" 她说道，"我该把我的想法说出来的，毕竟你付了不少钱。"

她舔了舔嘴唇，然后呼出一口气。

entries.en:
"It's nanoforged. Obvious stuff, look at that drift," she taps something and a distortion in the material structure becomes exaggerated.

"Crude, relatively speaking. Modern forges won't do it like this. Hm. 'Modern' meaning anything from the last thousand cycles. Seems like you found a genuine museum piece. Not unheard of 'course. Scavengers pull in bits of old sporeships and Explorarium junk often enough. Saw a bit of cryosleeper scanned when I was in training. Fascinating stuff."

She taps not the controls, but the casing of the analysis suite. "So it's old, but that's not what's strange."
entries.zh:
"它是经过纳米锻造的。很明显，看这个偏移，" 她轻点某处，材料结构中的一处畸变被放大显示。

"粗糙，相对而言。现代锻炉不会这样处理。嗯，'现代' 是指过去一千个星历年内的技术，看来你找到了真正的博物馆藏品。当然也不稀奇，拾荒者也没少打捞到旧孢子母舰和开拓者垃圾的碎片。我在受训时曾扫描过一小块低温休眠舰的残骸，那才叫迷人。"

她敲击的不是控制台，而是分析套件的外壳。"所以它很古老，但奇怪的不在于此。"

o.en: You like drawing this out for maximum drama, don't you.
o.zh: 你就爱吊人胃口，制造最大的悬念，对吧。

entries.en: She turns to look at you, raising an eyebrow.
entries.zh: 她转过头看向你，同时扬起一侧眉毛。

entries.en:
"Ha!" She smiles, if uneasily. "Got me. It's boring as dirt here in Luddie-land, gotta make my own fun."

"Still, this really is interesting... There's no embedded fabrication-rights!"

She looks at you significantly, as if this means something important.
entries.zh:
"哈！" 她微笑着，尽管有些不安。"被你看穿了。卢德佬的地盘无聊透顶，我总得自己找点乐子。"

"不过，这确实很有趣...它没有内嵌的制造权限！"

她意味深长地看着你，仿佛这一点意义重大。

o.en: So? A hacked pirate forge will strip out the FRM.
o.zh: 所以呢？被黑掉的海盗锻炉也会剥去制造权限。

entries.en:
"There are no embedded fabrication-rights!"

She looks at you as if this means something important, and you're supposed to respond.
entries.zh:
"它没有内嵌的制造权限！"

她看着你，仿佛这意义重大，而你理应有所反应。

o.en: So? A hacked pirate forge will strip out the FRM.
o.zh: 所以呢？被黑掉的海盗锻炉也会剥去制造权限。

entries.en:
"Sure. And they've been churning out garbage for 200 cycles. But what we see here is that this was made by a very old, very large forge. Probably top of the line for the time. And your sample has been exposed to space for a long, long time. And no FRM."

"Haven't seen this before." She rubs her fingers together, thinking. "Either someone was running a starsystem polity-level illicit forge a couple thousand cycles ago and you found the results, or... hm, you found something really weird."

She turns to you. "Where'd you find this? Some rock in the Abyss?"
entries.zh:
"没错。而且他们在 200 个星历年以来一直在产出垃圾。但我们在这里看到的是：这件制品出自一台非常古老、非常庞大的锻炉，在当时可能是顶级设备。而你的样本暴露在太空中已经很久很久了，并且没有制造权限。"

"我以前没见过这种情况。" 她摩挲着手指，一边思考着，"要么是几千个星历年前就有人在运营星系级规模的非法锻炉，而你找到了它的产物；要么...嗯，你找到了真正诡异的东西。"

她转向你，"你在哪儿找到的？深渊里的某颗岩质天体？"

o.en: Some rock. Why can't it have been legally forged with no FRM?
o.zh: 一颗岩体天体。为什么它不能是合法锻造的但没有制造权限呢？

entries.en:
"That's... that'd be insane. The whole point of the Domain was to control this stuff! Well," she concedes to herself, "Maybe the Gate Network was point number one."

"But regulating the nanoforges would have been two. Maybe three. Definitely important. Everything is stamped and tracked, that way you know who made what, where it ends up, when to collect forge-taxes, and who to blame when things go wrong."

"It was..." She shakes her hands at the analysis suite in an odd gesture, emphasizing the size of the concept. "It was the basis for interstellar civilization itself!"
entries.zh:
"那...那简直是疯了。人之领 的核心要义就是控制这些东西！好吧，" 她自言自语地让步，"也许星门网络才是第一要务。"

"但监管纳米锻炉肯定是第二，也许是第三，但绝对至关重要。所有东西都要打标追踪，这样才能知道谁制造了什么、最终流向何处、何时收取锻炉税，以及出问题时该找谁问责。"

"这是..." 她朝分析套件古怪地挥动着手势，以强调这个概念的重要性，"这是星际文明本身的基石！"

entries.en:
She takes a deep breath, looking self-conscious at her own outburst, then busies herself with flicking at some controls; the machine slows its hum to a dull whine and then a sudden unsettling absence of a background noise you weren't even conscious of hearing.

"Some rebel polity in the Domain-era I guess? Maybe they had some frontier-freedom notions before the Domain Armada re-stomped them into compliance. I'd pay good credits myself to learn how in Ludd's seven hells it ended up on some rock in the Abyss!"

She catches herself, then grins. "Uh, not that I wouldn't appreciate that answer for free if you happen to solve it."
entries.zh:
她深吸一口气，为自己刚才的激动显得有些难为情，随即忙乱地拨弄起控制按钮；机器的嗡鸣声渐渐降为沉闷的低吟声，接着连背景噪音也突然消失，那种你甚至没意识到自己一直在听的声音的缺席，此刻竟如此令人不安。

"是 人之领 时代的某个反叛政体吧，我猜？也许他们在 人之领 舰队重新踩平他们之前，有过些边疆自由理念。我自己都想花大价钱来弄明白，这玩意儿到底是怎么从他妈的卢德的七重地狱中跑到深渊的岩质天体上去的！"

她突然打住，咧嘴笑了笑，"呃，当然如果你碰巧解开了这个谜题，我也很乐意从你那免费听取答案。"

entries.en:
She shrugs, and reverses the sample insertion procedure.

Senior Engineer Tanaica sends you on your way back to orbit with no more farewell than a succinct "Right then."
entries.zh:
她耸耸肩，反向执行了样本收纳程序。

高级工程师 Tanaica 只简短地说了句 "那就这样"，便将你送返了轨道。

entries.en:
"Oh sure," she says.

The sample emerges, and - more gingerly, now - Senior Engineer Tanaica pulls on some gloves and places it back in your sample container.

"Wait." She looks at the sample container. "Really?"
entries.zh:
"哦，当然，" 她说道。

随着样本重新出现，高级工程师 Tanaica 此时更加谨慎地戴上手套，将其放回你的样本容器。

"等等。" 她看着样本容器，"真的假的？"

o.en: Really. I have one in orbit.
o.zh: 真的，而且我在轨道上就有一艘。

entries.en:
Arroyo barks a laugh. "After what Gargoyle chiseled me for on your behalf? Not happening. Good-bye, captain. I'll have the Astraia files for you after some roach-eating brigand shows up on my comm trying to blackmail me."

He disconnects his feed, leaving you with a spinning Tri-Tachyon franchise logo.
entries.zh:
Arroyo 大笑："在 Gargoyle 为了你敲诈了我之后？算了吧。拜了个拜，舰长。要是哪个吃蟑螂的土匪出现在我的通讯系统里勒索我了，我再把 Astraia 的资料给你。"

他切断了通讯，在你面前留下了旋转着的 速子科技 商标。

entries.en:
Gargoyle gives you an appalled look, and says aside, "... They let this one captain a starship?"

The hacker sighs dramatically, flopping back as if stunned. "... 'likes me', by Ludd's AI core, I can't even... okay, focus."

Gargoyle sits back up. "Baird doesn't do 'like'. She decides what you are going to be to her, and that's it. Anyway, haven't you figured this out yet?"
entries.zh:
Gargoyle 对你摆出了一副惊恐万分的表情，自语到："...他们居然敢让这家伙指挥星舰？"

这黑客夸张地叹了口气，像是被打晕了一样向后软塌了下去："...'挺喜欢我'，卢德的 AI 核心在上哟，我简直没法...算了，算了，集中注意力。"

Gargoyle 重新坐直了回来："Baird 的脑袋里可没有 '喜欢' 这个程序。她只 '决定' 你对她的用途，仅此而已。都这么久了你居然没搞明白这事？"

o.zh: Baird 在利用我，我明白这一点。

entries.en:
Gargoyle gives you a look of extreme skepticism.

"Baird doesn't really do 'coming around'. She decides what you are once she thinks she knows what you are, and that's it. Anyway, haven't you figured this out yet?"
entries.zh:
Gargoyle 满脸狐疑地看着你。

"Baird 并不会 '想通' 什么。一旦她认为她自己知道你是怎样的人，她就会把你扔去做怎样的事。事已至此，你还没想明白吗？"

o.zh: Baird 在利用我，我明白这一点。

entries.en:
"Yeah, well," the hacker starts getting distracted, reading something on a secondary display.

"Have some fun with it, at least. Did you comms me for a reason or were you just lonely for some mental stimulation after having robotic underlings salute you all day?"
entries.zh:
"啊，好吧。" 黑客开始有些心不在焉了，在另一个显示器上读起什么东西来。

"至少你玩的还挺开心。你呼叫我是想问什么吗？又或者只是在机器人下属向你敬礼了一整天之后，你因为精神刺激而感到孤独，想找个人聊聊？"

entries.en: Gargoyle shrugs, "Baird doesn't really do 'nice', does she. Have you figured it out yet?"
entries.zh: Gargoyle 耸了耸肩：" Baird 并不是个好人，你难道还没发现这一点？"

entries.en: Gargoyle looks up at you, "Yeah?"
entries.zh: Gargoyle 抬头看着你："喔？真的？"

o.zh: 我觉得你应该有一些专业的看法。

o.en: If you just want to whine about it, I can be on my way.
o.zh: 如果你只是想抱怨的话，我想我可以离开了。
什么都不说，就这么看着他

entries.en:
"The provost doesn't think it's important to let me explain," Gargoyle scoffs, "Maybe you should just fly off to Hybrasil without knowing anything but the name of one crackpot weapons engineer. No, go ahead! I'll wait. Tell me how it goes."

The silence draws out for nearly three seconds before Gargoyle begins ranting again.

"Imagine! Letting you con me into the data heist of a lifetime - set a nice fire under the High Hegemon's chair, didn't it! - then I decrypt the precious archive of the guy whose job she stole, and not asking what I thought of the contents? Which I read. Mostly. Can you believe it? Typical. She thinks she knows everything."

The hacker slumps, sulking.
entries.zh:
"院长认为我的解释不重要，她也许认为你应该在只知道自己要找一个疯子武器工程师的情况下就跑到 Hybrasil 星系去。" Gargoyle 嘲笑道，说着说着他就装出了院长的样子，"哇！这计划真是完美无缺！我会在这里等着的，记得告诉我进展如何。"

你们大眼瞪小眼，瞪了好一会后 Gargoyle 又开始咆哮。

"想象一下！院长让你把我骗进了一场令人毕生难忘的数据劫案 —— 还是在 霸主 的眼皮子底下！然后她又让我解密那个被她偷了饭碗的人的珍贵档案，到头来却不问已经将档案中大部分内容浏览完毕的我对其中内容的看法？她以为自己什么都知道！典中典！"

说完后黑客垂头丧气，不难看出他在生闷气。

o.en: I would like to hear about what you found, Gargoyle.
If you just want to whine about it, I can be on my way.
o.zh: 如果你只是想抱怨的话，我想我可以离开了。
什么都不说，就这么看着他

entries.en: "The logs were scrubbed pretty hard before even Kallichore got them. I mean, there are the logs between the Tri-Tach contacts and Kallichore, and then there's a whole other set of internal Tri-Tach comms. Must have had some good connections, probably a mole or three. Those execs would throw each other out the airlock in a second if they thought it'd boost their own career. And it might!"
entries.zh: "在 Kallichore 拿到这些日志之前，它们已经被清理得很干净了。这里有 速子科技 的联络人和 Kallichore 之间的通话记录，也有一整套 速子科技 内部的通讯记录，这其中肯定有一些关联。那些高管们会马上把对手扔出气闸，只要他们觉得这样能促进自己的事业 —— 或许确实真的可以。"

entries.en:
"Anyway," Gargoyle leans in, speaking with quiet drama, "Project Ziggurat scared them. If you read between the lines," the hacker makes a self satisfied expression, "The initial phase of the project utilized a handful of AI cores of various grades. Guess what? Self-deleted. Tri-Tachyon thinks they're not supposed to be able to do that, but," a wobbly hand gesture, "Eh. Negotiable. Amazing what seemingly innocuous hardware can be made to do when you think outside the box."

"But what makes an AI delete itself?" Gargoyle leans in closer, "Whatever Project Ziggurat is, that's what. Spooky, right?"
entries.zh:
"总之，通灵塔计划可把他们吓坏了，这你从字里行间可以看出来。" Gargoyle 倾身向前，神秘兮兮地说，"在一开始，他们使用了几个不同等级的 AI 核心。你猜接下来发生了什么？这些核心自我删除了，速子科技 可没想到它们能做到自毁...不，哪怕是跳出条条框框思考，抛开理论只是用常识想想，也没人能料到这些东西会做出这样的事情。"

"但究竟是什么能让 AI 自毁呢？" Gargoyle 靠得更近了，"不管通灵塔计划是什么，它做到了这一点。真是怪事，对吧？"

o.en: You've given me a lot to think about.
o.zh: 你提供的信息够我消化一阵子了。

entries.en: "You're welcome, captain!" Gargoyle leans back, grinning again, and flips through floating holodisplays.
entries.zh: "不用客气，舰长！" Gargoyle 靠回了椅背，又咧嘴笑了起来，他的影像在漂浮的全息显示屏上翻动了一阵。

entries.en: Gargoyle sits up, "Thank-you captain. Project Ziggurat, now that's a story!"
entries.zh: Gargoyle 坐了起来："多谢了，舰长。通灵塔计划是吧？让我来告诉你一些关于这玩意儿的事。"

entries.en: "Ludd's commode, this is boring." Gargoyle sits up, "You wanted to know about Project Ziggurat, right? Now that's a story!"
entries.zh: "卢德在上，你真是太无聊了。" Gargoyle 坐了起来，"你想知道通灵塔计划，对吗？行吧，来听听故事。"

entries.en: Silence. Gargoyle's hand starts tapping on a stray datapad.
entries.zh: 在一片沉默中，Gargoyle 玩起了他的数据平板。

o.zh: 我觉得你应该有一些专业的看法。

entries.en:
"Fine. I'm sure you'll do great and make Baird very happy and get lots of credits."

Gargoyle looks at you darkly, and says quietly, "You'll never be like Coureuse to her, you know. You're just muscle. A tool. A killer. Once you've served your purpose?"

Gargoyle turns away and flips a hand dismissively at you; the comms line goes black.
entries.zh:
"很好。我相信你会做得很好，你会让 Baird 非常高兴，然后拿到很多的报酬。"

Gargoyle 阴沉地看着你，幽幽地说："我想你也心知肚明，在她眼里，你永远不会拥有 Coureuse 那样的地位。你只是一个杀手，一个工具，而一旦你完成了你的使命..."

Gargoyle 转过身，轻蔑地朝你甩了甩手，接着通讯就被切断了。

entries.en:
"May the Path be r-" The $post's eyes go suddenly wide at a red flash from a secondary display.

They return to the comm-link, fixed with fear... and hatred.
entries.zh:
"愿卢德之道永 ——" $post 突然瞪大了双眼看向旁边显示屏所显示的红色警告。

转回通讯界面的视线凝结着恐惧... 与憎恨。

entries.en:
"Servant of Moloch! Redemption is not- is not..."

The Pather's eyes go wide at a red flash from a secondary display.

"By Ludd's hells, it is..." $HeOrShe returns to stare, horrified, through the comm-link. $HisOrHer face is full of terror... and hatred.
OR
"Submit and repent! Your use of sinful technologies may- may..."

The Pather's eyes go wide at a red flash from a secondary display.

"By the blessed stars is that..." $HisOrHer eyes return to the comm-link, fixed with horror... and hatred.
entries.zh:
"恶魔摩洛克的奴仆！或许救赎对 —— 对..."

左径分子因为一块副屏上闪的红光而瞪大了眼。

"卢德的地狱在上啊，这是..." $HeOrShe转而惊恐地盯着通讯链接。$HisOrHer的脸上满是恐惧... 与憎恨。
OR
"服从并忏悔！你们需要献上 —— 献上..."

左径分子因为一块副屏上闪的红光而瞪大了眼。

"群星在上，那是..." $HisOrHer的双眼看回了通讯链接，目光中凝着惊骇... 与憎恨。

entries.en:
"May the Path be r-" The $post's eyes go suddenly wide at a red flash from a secondary display.

"Blessed Ludd!" $heOrShe gasps.
entries.zh:
"愿卢德之道永 ——" $post 突然瞪大了双眼看向旁边显示屏所显示的红色警告。

"圣卢德啊！" $heOrShe倒抽一口冷气。

entries.en:
"Befouler, defiler, sinful spite-God! Demoniac!" The look of rage and religious mania pulls the $post's face into a devilish mask as $heOrShe shouts.

"What work-of-Moloch $shipOrFleet is this? What unholy combination of human craft and abomination? You are to be destroyed on sight, accursed by God and all who follow the Path of our faith!"

Targeting alerts chime from your tactical officer's console.
OR
"You accursed meddler, servant of Moloch! What unnatural work have you wrought in the shadow so far from the Path?"

Targeting alerts chime from your tactical officer's console.

"I name you abomination, adversary, god-spite! It is my holy duty to destroy your infernal $shipOrFleet," $heOrShe shouts, flecks of spittle flashing in the holo. "-And you as well before you slither back into the abyss whence you spawned!"
entries.zh:
"污秽者、亵渎者、罪恶的渎神者！恶魔！" 随着 $post 的叫喊，暴怒与宗教狂热的神情将$heOrShe的脸扭曲成了一副魔鬼般的面具。

"这$shipOrFleet是何等恶魔摩洛克的造物？是何等亵渎的人造工艺和畸形之物的结合？你这被神与所有信众诅咒的存在，应当格杀勿论！"

目标锁定的警报声从你战术军官的控制台传来。
OR
"你这该死的捣乱者，恶魔摩洛克的仆从！你都从远离卢德之道的阴影中制造了怎样的孽物？"

目标锁定的警报声从你战术军官的控制台传来。

"我将视你为怪物、大敌、渎神者！我神圣的职责就是摧毁你这可恶的$shipOrFleet，" $heOrShe吆喝着，唾沫星子在全息影像中闪烁着。"—— 还有你，在你爬回你的深渊老家之前！"

o.en: Hold a moment, let us talk this through.
o.zh: 等会，让我们先好好谈谈。

o.en: You should calm down before doing something you'll regret.
o.zh: 冷静，在你做一些会让你后悔的事之前。

o.en: Funny way to ask for a bribe, but let's talk credits...
o.zh: 真是有趣的索贿手段，不过让我们谈谈价钱...

o.en: Enough of this. Battle stations! (cut comms)
o.zh: 够了。战斗准备！ (切断通讯)

entries.en:
"Before me I saw evil incarnate, and I stood strong..." The Pather's words are for $hisOrHer crew, not you.

The link shudders into static, the last image is of hands clasped in a brief prayer.
OR
"Before me I saw evil incarnate, and-"

The Pather's words are lost in static as you hit the comms-cutoff.
entries.zh:
"我亲眼得见邪恶化身，而我屹立不摧..." 左径分子此言是说给$hisOrHer的船员所说，而非对你。

通讯链接噼啪作响，化作一片雪花，最后一幕是双手合十的短暂祈祷画面。
OR
"我亲眼得见邪恶化身，而 ——"

随着你切断通讯，左径分子的声音消失于静电杂音中。

They return to the comm-link, fixed with fear... and hatred.
OR
"May the Path be r-" The $post's eyes go suddenly wide at a red flash from a secondary display.

"Blessed Ludd!" $heOrShe gasps.

"愿卢德之道永 ——" $post 突然瞪大了双眼看向旁边显示屏所显示的红色警告。

对方转回了通讯界面，目光中凝着恐惧... 与憎恨。
OR
"愿卢德之道永 ——" $post 突然瞪大了双眼看向旁边显示屏所显示的红色警告。

"圣卢德啊！" $heOrShe倒抽一口冷气。

The link shudders into static, the last image is of hands clasped in a brief prayer.

通讯链接噼啪作响，化作一片雪花，最后一幕是双手合十的短暂祈祷画面。

"Before me I saw evil incarnate, and-"

The Pather's words are lost in static as you hit the comms-cutoff.

"我亲眼得见邪恶化身，而 ——"

随着你切断通讯，左径分子的声音消失于静电杂音中。

entries.en:
"An abomination, a devil-$shipOrFleet from Hell itself is before us! We pray to Providence to pass this test which has been given unto our unworthy-"

The $post's words are for $hisOrHer crew, not you, and the link shudders into static. The last image you see are hands clasped in prayer.
entries.zh:
"一具污秽的造物，一支来自地狱本身的魔鬼$shipOrFleet就在我们眼前！我们祈求天命让我们这些卑微者通过这降临的考验 ——"

$post 此言是对$hisOrHer的船员所说，而非对你。随后，通讯链接在噼啪作响中化作一片雪花，最后一幕是双手合十的短暂祈祷画面。
