Then a reasonable yet concerned look comes over him. "I understand now - you wish to avoid appearing as though you must beg. Perhaps my people could set up some kind of arrears system? Quietly, of course. No outsiders need know of your troubles."

He smiles.
entries.zh:
"哦？如果你濒临破产，我可以跟一些投资者谈谈。当然，这是出于个人情谊。" 他流露出一种贵族般的义务感，对你的处境进行了思考。

然后，他脸上浮现出一种既理智又关切的表情。"我明白了 —— 你不希望显得像是在乞求。或许我的人可以设立某种延期付款机制？当然，要悄悄地。不让其他人知道你的困境。"

他笑了笑。

o.en: I'm not asking for help. I'm telling you the payments end. Now.
o.zh: 我不是在寻求帮助。我是在告诉你，付款到此为止。现在。

entries.en:
The comms connects instantly, forwarding your link to a holding pattern. After a minute, an excruciatingly perfect-looking secretary answers.

"Office of Gens Hannan. How may I assist you?"
entries.zh:
通讯立即接通，将你的链接转入等候界面。一分钟后，一位长相极尽完美的秘书对你应答。

"这里是 Hannan 氏族办公室。我能帮您什么忙？"

o.en: I have business with Reynard Hannan.
o.zh: 我和 Reynard Hannan 有笔生意要谈一下。

entries.en:
"Of course, $playerName. One moment please."

The secretary switches your link back to a holding pattern, the crest of the office of Prime Demarchon entwined with that of Gens Hannan.
entries.zh:
"当然，$playerName。请稍等。"

秘书将你的链接再次转入等候界面，屏幕上大统领办公室的徽标与 Hannan 氏族的徽标交织在一起。

entries.en:
After a few minutes, Reynard Hannan himself appears before you, effortlessly regal.

"$PlayerName," he says.
entries.zh:
几分钟后，Reynard Hannan 本人出现在你面前，浑身散发着不怒自威的气质。

"$PlayerName，" 他说道。

entries.en:
After a few minutes, Reynard Hannan himself appears before you, effortlessly regal.

"$PlayerName," he says. The contempt in his voice is unmistakable.
entries.zh:
过了几分钟，Reynard Hannan 本人出现在你面前，那份气派浑然天成。

"$PlayerName，" 他开口道，语气里的不屑再明白不过。

entries.en:
After a few minutes, Reynard Hannan himself appears before you. He regards you with casual regality.

"$playerName," he says. "Welcome to Kazeron."
entries.zh:
几分钟后，Reynard Hannan 本人出现在你面前，浑身散发着不怒自威的气质。

"$PlayerName，" 他说道。"欢迎来到 Kazeron。"

entries.en:
After a few minutes, Reynard Hannan himself appears before you. He regards you with casual regality.

"$playerName," he says. "Welcome to Kazeron."
entries.zh:
几分钟后，Reynard Hannan 本人出现在你面前，浑身散发着不怒自威的气质。

"$PlayerName，" 他说道。"欢迎来到 Kazeron。"

entries.en:
"Of course, the Prime Demarchon will be right with you."

The secretary taps at an interface and the image flickers; Reynard Hannan appears before you, effortlessly regal. He looks up and through the link.

"$TitlePL $playerLastName," he says, giving a small nod.
entries.zh:
"当然，大统领这就来见您。"

秘书在界面上点了几下，画面一闪；Reynard Hannan 出现在你面前，那份气派浑然天成。他抬眼，目光透过通讯落过来。

"$TitlePL $playerLastName，" 他略一点头。

entries.en:
After a few minutes the secretary reappears.

"I'm sorry," they say, smiling. "But the Prime Demarchon is unavailable. Would you like to leave a message?"
entries.zh:
片刻过后，秘书再度现身。

"很抱歉，" 对方微笑着说道，"大统领暂时无法接见。您需要留言吗？"

o.en: >> dev No, really, I must insist.
o.zh: DEV 不，说真的，我必须坚持。

o.en: I have important information concerning the Gates to discuss with the Prime Demarchon.
o.zh: 我有关于星门的重要信息需要与大统领讨论。

o.en: I have important information concerning the Gates to discuss with the Prime Demarchon.
o.zh: 我有关于星门的重要信息需要与大统领讨论。

entries.en:
"Captain." Reynard gives you a pitying look.

His message is clear: You should know better than to ask. And in asking, you've wasted both his time and your own.

But more importantly, his.
entries.zh:
"舰长。" Reynard 向你投去同情的目光。

他的意思很明确：你本应更明智些，不问这个问题。而你这么一问，既浪费了他的时间，也浪费了你自己的时间。

但更重要的是他的时间。

entries.en:
"I-" he begins, then manages to just suppress a yawn.

"You must forgive me, captain. The League Council sessions can run late." He resettles himself, adjusting his overcoat back into carelessly perfect disarray.

"Pardon my forgetfulness, did you have a matter of pressing concern to discuss?"
entries.zh:
"我 —— " 他刚开口，就努力忍住了一个哈欠。

"请您原谅，舰长。联盟理事会的会议可能结束的有点晚。" 他重新调整了一下自己，不经意间把大衣随意地整理成一种完美的凌乱状态。

"抱歉，我这人就是健忘，你是不是有什么紧急的事情要讨论来着？"

entries.en:
Reynard begins to yawn loudly again, interrupting your explanation.

He halts suddenly in the middle of the act - for it is an act - to give you an impatient look.

"As I've explained, captain," that lowly title used as reprimand, "I don't wish to discuss such matters with you."
entries.zh:
Reynard 开始大声地打起哈欠来，打断了你的解释。

他突然在打到一半的时候停了下来 —— 本来就是故意的 —— 然后给你一个不耐烦的眼神。

"就像我已经说过的，舰长，" 他用这个卑微的称呼来作为责备，"我不想和你讨论这些事情。"

entries.en: "Are you going to tell me that Horus Yaribay is attempting to conspire with High Hegemon Baikal Daud?"
entries.zh: "你是不是要告诉我 Horus Yaribay 正在试图与至高霸主 Baikal Daud 密谋？"

entries.en: "I am touched by your concern, captain," Reynard says with too-practiced warmth. "But trust that I have a handle on the intrigues of my good friend Horus."
entries.zh: "你的关心令我感动，舰长。" Reynard 相当老练地扮出一副热情的样子，"可你得相信我，我真能处理我那位 Horus 好友的密谋。"

entries.en: "I am touched by your concern, captain," Reynard says, as if indulging a bright student. "But you may trust that I have a handle on the intrigues of my good friend Horus."
entries.zh: "你的关心令我感动，舰长。" Reynard 谆谆教诲道，仿佛在教育某个好学生，"但你可以相信我，我真能处理我那位 Horus 好友的密谋。"

entries.en: "I'm sure it is," Reynard says easily, as if indulging a bright student. "Which is why I have several intelligence networks keeping an eye on the intrigues of my good friend Horus."
entries.zh: "肯定有的。" Reynard 放松地讲，仿佛在教育某个好学生，"所以我手下才有好几个情报网全都盯着我那位好友 Horus 的密谋呢。"

entries.en: He spreads his hands, ever-generous of spirit. "You need not give me his cryptokey or anything so gauche as that. Besides, it would hurt Horus to be so betrayed."
entries.zh: 他摊开双手，带着似乎与生俱来的慷慨大方。"你有他的加密秘钥或者别的蠢东西的话，就不要给我了。Horus 要是被背叛到这种份上的话，可是会很受伤的。"

entries.en: "Did you," he says rather than asks, making it clear that he did not receive any message. And if he did, he wouldn't have troubled to remember it.
entries.zh: "你真的给我留言了吗？" 与其说他是在询问，不如说他是在陈述，清楚地表明他并没有收到任何信息。就算他收到了，他也不会费心去记住的。

entries.en:
"If you are looking for a job, then I suggest you go find a spacer bar and 'ask around'."

He dances his fingers at these last words, like he's discussing something far, far beneath his interest.
entries.zh:
"如果你在找工作，我建议你去找个太空佬酒吧 '四处打听打听'。"

在说到最后几个字的时候，他轻轻摆动着手指，就好像是在谈论一件令他无趣的事情。

o.en: I left a message with your secretary. Have you given it thought?
o.zh: 我给你的秘书留了消息。你考虑过了吗？

o.en: I have important information to discuss concerning the future of the Persean Sector itself!
o.zh: 我有关于 英仙座星域 未来的重要消息需要讨论。

o.en: This information is very important, it concerns the Gate system and the Galatia Academy. (explain)
o.zh: 这条信息非常重要，它关乎着星门系统和 Galatia 学院。 (解释)

o.en: Do you even read your messages?
o.zh: 你甚至都不看你的消息吗？

o.en: I wish to discuss... a delicate matter involving Horus Yaribay's activities.
o.zh: 我想讨论...一件涉及 Horus Yaribay 活动的微妙事宜。

entries.en:
Reynard puts a finger to his lips, his face tilting downward in thought for a moment.

"I'm afraid I don't recall any messages," he says with an appropriately generous air of apology... tempered by the merest hint of dismissal.

"What did you wish to discuss?"
entries.zh:
Reynard 把一根手指放在嘴唇上，脸上微微向下倾斜，沉思了片刻。"恐怕我不记得有什么消息了。" 他带着一种得体而大方的歉意说道...隐约透露着不屑。

"你想讨论什么？"

o.en: I inquired about joining the Persean League.
o.zh: 我询问了关于加入 英仙座联盟 的事。

o.en: I left some messages with your secretary. Have you given them thought?
o.zh: 我给你的秘书留了几条消息。你考虑过了吗？

o.en: I said I would offer my services to Gens Hannan.
o.zh: 我说我会为 Hannan 氏族效力。

o.en: I'm looking for Scylla Coureuse. I believe she is on Laicaille Habitat.
o.zh: 我正在寻找 Scylla Coureuse，我确定她正在 Laicaille 栖息地上。

o.en: I wish to discuss a delicate matter concerning Horus Yaribay.
o.zh: 我想谈谈某个和 Horus Yaribay 有关的敏感问题。

o.en: I would like to speak with the Prime Demarchon about joining the Persean League.
o.zh: 我想和大统领谈谈加入 英仙座联盟 的事。

o.en: I would like to offer my services to Reynard Hannan. My reputation should speak for itself.
o.zh: 我希望能为 Reynard Hannan 效力。我的名声应该足以证明我的实力。

entries.en:
A polite, but ever-so-slightly condescending smile appears on the secretary's face.

"I'm sorry, but the Prime Demarchon is busy right now. Would you like to leave a message?"
entries.zh:
秘书的脸上浮现出礼貌却略带轻蔑的微笑。

"很抱歉，大统领现在很忙。您要留言吗？"

entries.en:
The secretary nods attentively, hands unmoving. Accessing some kind of implant?

"Wonderful. I'll let the Prime Demarchon know as soon as he's available."
entries.zh:
秘书专注地点点头，双手一动不动。是在通过某种植入体传讯吗？

"很好。大统领一有空，我会立即告知他。"

entries.en:
The secretary nods attentively, again.

"Fantastic. I'll inform the Prime Demarchon as soon as he's free."
entries.zh:
秘书再次专注地点了点头。

"太好了。大统领一有空闲，我会立刻通知他。"

entries.en:
Ever pleasant and responsive, the secretary nods with that hint of a smile.

"Of course, thank you $playerSirOrMadam. I'm sure the Prime Demarchon will contact you as soon as he's able."
entries.zh:
秘书一如既往地亲切且反应迅速，带着一丝微笑点了点头。

"当然，谢谢您，$playerSirOrMadam。我相信大统领一有空就会联系您。"

entries.en: The secretary nods pleasantly, as usual, repeating assurances that the Prime Demarchon will respond as soon as he can.
entries.zh: 秘书一如既往地愉快点头，再次保证大统领会尽快给予回复。

entries.en:
The secretary nods pleasantly, as usual, repeating assurances that the Prime Demarchon will respond as soon as he can.

You have a growing feeling that you are not being taken seriously.
entries.zh:
秘书像往常一样愉快地点了点头，再次保证大统领会尽快回复。

你越来越觉得他们在敷衍你。

entries.en:
"The League has an obligation to protect all free peoples of the Persean Sector, captain." Reynard speaks with the bland moral superiority of a consummate politician. "It is our very purpose to secure universal freedom."

Then, he allows that persona fall away.

"Of course you don't believe that, do you."
entries.zh:
"联盟有义务保护英仙座星域所有自由的人民，舰长。" Reynard 用一位老练政治家特有的、不带感情色彩的道德优越感说道，"确保所有人的自由正是我们的宗旨。"

然后，他收敛起那副姿态。

"你并不相信这些，对吧。"

o.en: Of course not, I'm no fool. What's your game, Hannan?
o.zh: 当然不信，我又不是傻子。Hannan，你到底在玩什么把戏？

o.en: I would rather like to believe that the ideals of the League meant something.
o.zh: 我倒宁愿相信联盟的理念还是有点意义的。

o.en: I absolutely believe in freedom. What you're doing is not it.
o.zh: 我当然相信自由。但你们所做的并不是真正的自由。

entries.en:
"The Persean Sector is precariously balanced. If your part in it fell to the wrong side of that balance..."

He closes his eyes for a moment, shaking his head delicately.

The Prime Demarchon looks to you. "Consider this an assertive recommendation to join the League."
entries.zh:
"整片英仙座星域正处于微妙的平衡之中。如果你在这平衡中扮演的角色偏向了错误的一方..."

他闭上眼睛片刻，轻轻地摇了摇头。

大统领看着你，说："一个诚挚的建议，加入联盟吧。"

o.en: I'll join - to vote you out of office.
o.zh: 我会加入 —— 目的是把你从位子上投下去。

o.en: The waste of human life is unbelievably cynical.
o.zh: 如此漠视人命，简直冷血得令人难以置信。

o.en: Why are League fleets harassing my colonies?
o.zh: 为什么联盟舰队在骚扰我的殖民地？

entries.en: "We might just be able to work together, captain." He smiles indulgently, then adds softly "And yet I do believe. If I tell you only one truth, it is that I do believe."
entries.zh: "我们也许可以合作，舰长。" 他宽容地笑了笑，然后轻声补充道，"而且我真的相信。如果我只能告诉你一个真相，那就是我真的相信。"

entries.en:
"You and I both, captain," he says coldly. "It is simply your convenience to judge to unpracticed ideals from the outside."

"The League, captain, is everything! It is everything to me, to Gens Hannan. Our excellence blossoms within the freedom of the League. I have earned the fruit and I have built them to towering heights - look upon proud Kazeron. No mere backwater, it is a barycenter of power!"

Reynard pauses, looking away for a moment. "What have you built, captain? Do not speak to me of ideals; show me."
entries.zh:
"你我都一样，舰长，" 他冷冷地说，"你只是从外部轻易评判那些未经实践的理想罢了。"

"联盟，舰长，就是一切！它对我来说就是一切，对 Hannan 氏族来说也是一切。我们的卓越在联盟的自由中绽放。我取得了成果，并将它们推向了顶峰 —— 看看骄傲的 Kazeron 吧。它可不是什么偏僻之地，而是权力的中心！"

Reynard 停顿了一下，目光移开了一会儿。"你建立了什么，舰长？别跟我谈理想；展示给我看。"

entries.en:
"And what is freedom to you?" he says, suddenly intense. "You. An outsider, a barbarian at the gates, at the head of a warfleet threatening this precious thing we have built. Who are you to speak of freedom?"

"My freedom," he hits the table with two fingers, "I have given it for my world and for my Gens; look upon proud Kazeron! I have earned everything you see before you. The League gave me that freedom, and the League has prospered for it!"

Reynard pauses, taking a breath and allowing a brittle calm to re-settle. "Do not speak of ideals. Show me."
entries.zh:
"自由对你来说意味着什么？" 他突然变得激动起来，"你，一个外来者，一个站在我们门外的野蛮人，率领着一支战舰舰队威胁着我们千辛万苦建立的一切。你有什么资格谈论自由？"

"我的自由，" 他用两根手指敲打着桌子，"我将我的自由交付给了我的家园和我的氏族；看看骄傲的 Kazeron 吧！你所看到的一切都是我应得的。联盟给了我那份自由，而联盟也因此而繁荣！"

Reynard 停顿了一下，深吸了一口气，让自己重新回到一种易碎的平静。"别跟我谈理想。直接展示给我看。"

entries.en: "Duly," he says with a smirk.
entries.zh: "没问题，" 他带着讥笑说道。

entries.en:
A glimmer of mirth enters his eyes.

"I would savor your attempt."
entries.zh:
他的眼中闪过一丝愉悦。

"我会细细品味你的尝试。"

entries.en: "Pure hearts are for martyrs and poets, I'm afraid. Considering your pocket empire," he says with a smirk, "I don't take you for either."
entries.zh: "恐怕纯洁的心灵只属于烈士和诗人。考虑到你的小小帝国，" 他讥笑着说，"我认为你两者都不是。"

entries.en: DEV added +1 to dealArgumentsMade, value is now: $dealArgumentsMade
entries.zh: DEV 已给 dealArgumentsMade 加 1，当前值为：$dealArgumentsMade

entries.en:
To ensure everything goes smoothly, you take personal command of the lead transport shuttle.

There's a mere flicker of targeting lasers and a sweep or two of radar. Nothing to worry about, you calmly assure your pilot, who looks to be breaking out in sweat.

Your landing is met by little more than a large, armored cargo-hatch opening from under an overhang; an invitation.
entries.zh:
为确保一切顺利，你亲自带领穿梭机出发。

只有微弱的指示激光照射和一两次雷达扫描，没什么可担心的。你平静地向你的飞行员保证，尽管他看起来有点汗流浃背了。

你们着陆时，只见一个巨大的装甲货物舱门从一处悬挑下方缓缓打开；仿佛是在邀请你们进入。

entries.en:
Your party is armed and armored, but respectfully - these are underworld criminals who wish to be considered dangerous - but not indecently. Over-icing the cake, as it were, would appear suspicious; there's a delicate balance to navigate when it comes to these things, you explain to your nervous crew. You take care not to mention the recessed autoturrets that have been tracking your shuttle.

Confidence is the word.
entries.zh:
你们的小队全副武装，但请注意 —— 你们是希望被视为危险人物的地下犯罪分子，但又不能太过张扬。就像给蛋糕加太多糖霜会显得可疑一样，在处理这些事情时需要把握微妙的平衡，你向紧张的船员们解释道。你谨慎的没有提及那些一直在追踪你们穿梭机的隐蔽自动炮塔。

信心是关键。

entries.en:
The local boss left in charge of this depressing cave has the pale, antsy look of an underling who has been cooped up for too long with little to do but gamble and use.

He wipes a greasy lock of hair from his forehead and looks at you suspiciously. His stinking underlings finger their short, brutish guns.

"You're not Skinny Diego," he says.

"I was told Diego was doing the pickup. Where's Diego?"
entries.zh:
负责看守这个阴郁洞穴的当地头目，面色苍白，眼神焦虑，看起来像一个被长期囚禁、除了赌博和嗑药外无事可做的喽啰。

他抹掉前额上油腻的一缕头发，用怀疑的眼光打量着你。他那些臭气熏天的小弟们则用手指摩挲着他们短小粗陋的武器。

"你不是 Skinny Diego，" 他说道。

"上面告诉我来接头的是 Diego。Diego 在哪里？"

o.en: Diego couldn't make it, friend. He told me to give you his regards. (lie)
o.zh: Diego 来不了了，朋友。他让我代他向你问好。 (说谎)

o.en: I'm afraid Diego had a little accident. Boss is getting me to fill in. (lie)
o.zh: Diego 遇到点小麻烦。头儿让我来代替他。 (说谎)

o.en: Diego and the boss had a disagreement, so now I'm your Diego. (lie)
o.zh: Diego 和老大闹翻了，所以现在我就是你要等的 Diego 了。 (说谎)

entries.en: "Diego said that?" His beady little eyes scrunch up, his hands tense. "Diego hates my guts. He'd never say that."
entries.zh: "Diego 是这么说的？" 他眯起眼睛，双手紧绷。"Diego 恨死我了。他绝不会这么说的。"

o.en: Between you and me, I think he meant it ironically, like.
o.zh: 这里就你和我，我觉得他在说反话，你懂吧。

entries.en:
"An accident? How? Where?" The man's hands tense. "Diego never has accidents. He's careful."

A thought congeals, slowly but surely.

"Well. I suppose he's not that careful. But he's lucky, always lucky. What happened?"
entries.zh:
"一次意外？怎么发生的？在哪里？" 男人的手紧张地攥了起来，"Diego 从不会出意外。他很谨慎。"

一个念头似乎在他心中缓慢但坚定地凝聚起来。

"好吧。我想他也没那么谨慎。但他运气很好，总是很走运。到底发生了什么？"

o.en: Ever seen a cheap agrav plate overload? Should fail-safe. Unless...
o.zh: 你见过廉价的反重力装置过载的样子吗？通常它具备故障安全机制。除非...

entries.en:
"A disagreement?" The man looks more than shocked; appalled. "But Diego's his own brother, his blood. He'd never cut Diego out of a job. Never! Never ever."

He looks unsteady, physically unwell, as if what was solid hullplate turned out to be little more than ration-wrappings.

"What could be so terrible? Diego, Diego..." He shakes his head, almost in tears.
entries.zh:
"闹翻了？" 男人看起来不仅仅是震惊，简直是惊骇，"但 Diego 是他的亲兄弟，他的血亲。他绝不会把 Diego 从岗位上赶走。绝不会！永远也不会。"

他看上去身体不适，摇摇晃晃，就好像原本坚实的船体甲板突然变成了脆弱不堪的包装纸。

"到底发生了什么可怕的事情？Diego，Diego..." 他摇着头，几乎要哭出来了。

o.en: It's bad. Couldn't tell it... not without a drink.
o.zh: 糟透了。我实在说不出口...除非喝上一杯。

entries.en:
"Yeah?" He licks his lips, taking a moment to revel in a growing anger.

"Diego can eat rads and burn in vacuum, for all I care. Think's he's too fancy to come out here and do a bit of grunt work? Just like Diego."

He jabs a finger at you, "You can tell him I said that, too. I don't even care."
entries.zh:
"是吗？"他舔了舔嘴唇，在逐渐升腾的愤怒中沉浸片刻。

"Diego 就算被辐射烤焦，在真空里烧成灰，我也不在乎。觉得自己太了不起，不肯到这儿来干点苦活？就像 Diego 一样。"

他用手指着你，"你也可以告诉他我是怎么说的。我压根不在乎。"

o.en: Gladly! It's about time someone told Diego how it is.
o.zh: 当然！是时候让 Diego 面对现实了。

entries.en:
"Unless..." the man looks at you, strung along on your words. He takes a few moments to pick up on your implication.

To help him understand, you give a concerned look and dart your eyes around. Then, in low words, you explain that perhaps it should be discussed later. 'Accidents' like that don't just happen without someone wanting them to happen, and who knows if there aren't more snakes in the organization? Someone must be making a move - but we can't let them know that we know, much less let them know we know they know we know.

The boss nods along, now looking at even his own crew suspiciously.
entries.zh:
"除非..." 男人紧盯着你，被你的话所吸引。他花了几秒钟的时间来理解你的言外之意。

为了帮助他理解，你投去了一个关切的眼神，并环顾四周。然后，你低声解释道，这件事应该稍后再讨论。像那样的 "意外" 不会无缘无故地发生，谁知道组织里还有没有更多的毒蛇呢？一定有人在暗中行动 —— 但我们不能让他们知道我们已经察觉，更不能让他们知道我们知道他们知道我们已经察觉。

走私者老大一边点头，一边开始连自己的手下也怀疑起来了。

o.en: Let's get the cargo loading. I'll fill you in.
o.zh: 先让我们装货。待会儿细说。

entries.en:
"Of course, of course," the boss says, putting a hand on your shoulder. Now that you can smell the metabolic byproducts - and spillage - of hard, bad liquor, you would suppose that he has a hangover to drink away.

"I've right forgot my welcome, haven't I. Come, come! I've got a bottle open. It's good stuff. Put your crew to work loading and we can talk about what happened. Stars above, Diego..." he shakes his head, wanting to disbelieve, but unable.
entries.zh:
"当然，当然，" 走私者老大说着，把手搭在你的肩上。此刻，你能闻到他身上因大量饮用劣质烈酒而散发的代谢废物和呕吐物的气味，你猜他可能是想用酒精来驱散宿醉。

"我竟然忘了好好招待你，真是失礼了。来，来！我这儿已经开了一瓶好酒。这可是上等货。让你的手下先去装货，我们可以聊聊发生了什么。天哪，Diego..." 他摇着脑袋，心里不愿相信，但又没法否认。

o.en: Order your crew to work. And gird your liver.
o.zh: 让你的手下开始干活，同时让你的肝做好战斗准备。

entries.en:
"It is, isn't it," the man says slowly.

He looks at you with a new sense of self-confidence.

"You're not afraid to get your hands dirty, are you cap," he says with a gleam in his eye. Or maybe it's a pre-hangover glaze, judging from his shaky posture. "I had a good feeling about you as soon as I saw you weren't Diego."
entries.zh:
"确实如此，不是吗？" 这个男人缓缓说道。

他换了种欣赏的眼神看着你。

"你不怕亲自动手干脏活，对吧，老兄？" 他眼中闪烁着光芒。不过，从他摇摇晃晃的站姿来看，那也可能只是宿醉前的恍惚。"我一见你不是 Diego，就对你有好感了。"

o.en: Me, uh, too. Now then! There's work to do...
o.zh: 呃...我也是。那么现在！该干活了...

entries.en:
He takes you to a grubby office, a utility nook really, overlooking the main bay as your crews get to work loading the $rsom_product.

A bottle of something strong and cheap appears, and you do your part in pretending to drink it as you fill his head with paranoid half-truths built on details he reveals.
entries.zh:
他把你带到一间肮脏的办公室，更像一个杂物间，从这里可以俯瞰到主要港口，你的船员正在那里忙着装载那些 $rsom_product。

这时，一瓶廉价而烈性的酒出现了，你一边假装喝酒，一边根据他透露的细节，向他灌输一系列误导性的半真半假的信息。

entries.en:
Some time later, a polite, slightly embarrassed junior logistics technician from your crew gently knocks and informs you that the cargo is fully loaded.

You act as if you've had much more than you actually imbibed and make your excuses and promises as you pretend-stumble back to your transport shuttle.

Once the doors close, you stand up straight, dropping the act. The junior logistics technician does her best not to look too relieved.
entries.zh:
一段时间后，你手下一位礼貌而又略显拘谨的年轻物流专员轻轻敲门，告诉你货物已经全部装载完毕。

你装作自己已经喝得烂醉，边道歉边许诺，同时假装摇摇晃晃地走回你的运输穿梭机。

舱门一关闭，你立刻挺直身子，不再伪装。那名下级物流专员尽力不让自己显得太过放松。

entries.en:
It's not quite the bloody job your contact $rsom_contactName had in mind, but such a shocking display of incompetence is sure to cause a shake-up in whichever criminal enterprise this lot is - or, soon, was - involved with.

And now you've got a hold full of hot $rsom_product to unload.
entries.zh:
这可不是你联络人 $rsom_contactName 心中所想的那份血腥差事，但如此令人震惊的无能表现，定会在这帮家伙所涉及的，或即将涉及的任何犯罪组织中引起轩然大波。

而现在，你手里有一大堆烫手的 $rsom_product 等待处理。

entries.en:
You manage to decline repeated offers to share a bottle of 'the good stuff' while the boss iterates Diego's many failings. You nod and agree in vague but enthusiastic terms, performing your emotional support role with aplomb.

Some time later, a polite, slightly embarrassed junior logistics technician knocks on the open doorway - there's no door - of the utility nook that passes for the boss's office to inform you that the cargo is fully loaded.

He insists on personally escorting you, a little unsteadily, to your shuttle's airlock and shakes your hand before you step inside. "It's people like you that make this job worth it, cap. Solid, trustworthy. Willing to step up."

The door seals with a thunk you feel through your boots; finally, relief.
entries.zh:
你巧妙地回绝了走私者老大一再提出的共饮 "佳酿" 的邀请，而他则反复诉说着 Diego 的种种不足。你含糊其辞却又不失热情地点头应和，完美地扮演了情感支持者的角色，从容不迫。

不多时，一名礼貌而又略显拘谨的年轻物流专员，在那充当老板办公室的狭小工具间前 —— 那里根本没有门可敲，只是象征性地做了个敲门的动作 —— 通知你货物已经装载完毕。

尽管脚步略显踉跄，他坚持要亲自将你护送至穿梭机的气闸，并在你踏入之前紧紧握住你的手。"正是有了像你这样的人，这份工作才变得有意义，舰长。你稳重、可靠，勇于担当。"

随着气闸门 "嘭" 地一声封闭，你脚下的震动清晰可感；终于，你松了一口气。

entries.en: "A rival has established a secret outpost to move a large quantity of $rsom_product. I'd like you to ruin their plans for me."
entries.zh: "有一位竞争对手已经建立了一座秘密据点，意图转运大批量的 $rsom_product 。我希望你能破坏那个人的计划。"

entries.en:
It was the bloody job your contact $rsom_contactName had in mind. Such a shocking display of incompetence is sure to cause a shake-up in whichever criminal enterprise this lot is - was, rather - involved with.

And now you've got a hold full of hot $rsom_product to unload.
entries.zh:
这正是你联系人 $rsom_contactName 心中所想的那份血腥差事。但如此令人震惊的无能表现，定会在这帮家伙所涉及的，或已经涉及的任何犯罪组织中引起轩然大波。

而现在，你手里有一大堆烫手的 $rsom_product 等待处理。

entries.en:
A flight of shuttles is deployed, armed lightly enough to show respect to the smugglers but without being outwardly conspicuous. What appears to be a motley logistics crew with token guards approach the armored doors of the hidden base, hauling their basic cargo-moving tools: robotic lifts and agrav-fitted pallets, the usual.

Upon entrance, at the signal, weapons-fire erupts from the entire party. False air tanks conceal light arms and single-shot anti-armor tubes; utility panniers are stuffed with grenades and miniature assault drones. All are loosed in a few seconds of blinding violence which catch the smugglers completely off-guard.

After the initial shock comes the grind, and your marines pay for lack of heavy armor as they face recessed auto-turrets and not more than a few heavily armed criminals hiding in the worm-tunnels which loop through and around the rotten stone.
entries.zh:
一组穿梭机被部署出去，它们只有轻量的武装，既表现出对走私者的尊重，又不至于太过显眼。一支看似由杂牌后勤人员和几名象征性的守卫组成的队伍，正朝着隐藏基地的装甲大门靠近，他们拖拽着基础的货物搬运工具：机器人升降机和装有反重力装置的托盘，这些都是再平常不过的东西。

一进入基地，接到信号后，整支队伍立即开火。伪装的氧气罐中藏着轻武器和单发反装甲炮；杂物袋里塞满了手榴弹和迷你攻击无人机。在短短几秒内，就发生了一场令人眼花缭乱的火力倾泻，走私者们完全措手不及。

最初的震惊过后，便是艰苦的鏖战，面对着隐蔽的自动炮塔，还有大量藏在蜿蜒曲折、遍布泥浆的虫穴中全副武装的犯罪分子，你的陆战队员因为缺乏重型装甲而付出了代价。

entries.en:
$HisOrHer expression cools. "I trust my methods, captain," $heOrShe says.

"You can trust me, as you have in the past. You will be rewarded. Just as you have in the past."
entries.zh:
$HisOrHer的表情变得冷淡。"舰长，我相信的是我的手段。" $heOrShe说道。

"你可以像过去一样相信我，你会得到报酬的。就像过去一样。"

o.en: It's not about trust, it's about the lies a 'source' might provide. It could be a trap.
o.zh: 这无关信任，而是关于一个'线人'可能会提供的虚假情报。这可能是个陷阱。

entries.en:
"Then decline my generous offer," the $post says testily.

"If you're afraid of a little risk, I'll find someone who is up for the job."
entries.zh:
"那就拒绝我这慷慨的提议吧，" $post 不耐烦的说。

"如果你连这点风险都害怕，我可以去找其他人来完成这个任务。"

o.en: Ask about ruining $hisOrHer rival's secret outpost
o.zh: 询问摧毁$hisOrHer竞争对手秘密据点任务的细节

entries.en:
"You've earned a degree of my trust," $heOrShe says. "I would ask you to help me send a," $heOrShe chuckles, "very important message."

"One of my rivals has established a staging point, a secret outpost, on the planet $rsom_planetName in the $rsom_systemName, which is $rsom_dist light-years away. They've stashed a lot of $rsom_product there, awaiting transport. I'm not sure where they got it all, maybe an old cache, or it's a transit point from some other supplier. What I do know," $heOrShe growls, "is that they're severely undercutting the prices we've all worked so hard to keep at sustainable levels."

"Raid the outpost. Plunder the $rsom_product. Sell the loot at whatever black market you like - at market rate. It will be your payment."

"My source suggests that the outpost will be lightly defended. $rsom_marinesReq marines should be sufficient to neutralize the protection."
entries.zh:
"你已经赢得了我部分信任，" $heOrShe说道，"我想请你帮我传递一个，嗯..." $heOrShe轻笑一声，"非常重要的消息。"

"我的一个竞争对手在 $rsom_systemName 中的 $rsom_planetName 上建立了一个秘密据点，距离这里 $rsom_dist 光年。那个人在那里囤积了大量的 $rsom_product，正等待转运。我不清楚那家伙是从哪里弄来的这些货物，可能是某个旧仓库的存货，或者是从其他经销商那里转运过来的。但有一点我非常清楚，" $heOrShe开始咆哮，"那个逼正在以远低于我们辛苦维持的、保证长久发展的价格进行倾销！"

"劫掠那个据点。带走那些 $rsom_product。你可以在任何你喜欢的黑市上以市场价出售这些战利品。这就是你的报酬。"

"我的线人透露，那个据点的防御力量相当薄弱。派遣 $rsom_marinesReq 陆战队员应该就足以摧毁它的安保力量了。"

o.en: Any hostile fleets to look out for? Ground batteries?
o.zh: 有需要注意的敌对舰队或者地面炮台吗？

entries.en:
"My rival only dabbles in starships, so little to worry about there. But, yes, there are concealed batteries. They may not stop a proper warfleet, but they're an inconvenience."

"My, ah, source on this intel was 'convinced' to provide codes you will use to bypass their IFF." A slow, toothy smile builds on $hisOrHer face. "Use their codes. They'll think you're doing a pickup as you drop the shuttle cargo doors and marines pour fire into the unsuspecting fools."

$HeOrShe gets a distant, pleased look as $heOrShe imagines the slaughter.
entries.zh:
"我的竞争对手缺乏星舰，所以不用太担心这个。但是，没错，那里确实有隐蔽的地面炮台。它们或许无法阻挡一支真正的舰队，但确实会造成一些麻烦。"

"我那个...呃...提供情报的线人已经被 '说服'，并交出了用来绕过对方 IFF 的代码以供你们使用。" $hisOrHer的脸上缓慢地浮现出带着狡黠的笑容，"只要用了他们的密钥。当你的陆战队员打开穿梭机的货舱门向那些毫无防备的笨蛋倾泻火力时，他们都只会以为你们是来取货的。"

$HeOrShe走神了片刻，想象着那场即将到来的屠杀，$HeOrShe的脸上浮现出一种满足的神情。

o.en: And you trust this, ah, source?

entries.en: A nearby hostile fleet is tracking your movements, making a ground operation impossible.
entries.zh: 附近的一支敌对舰队正在追踪你的动向，使你无法开展地面行动。

o.en: Talk your way in, and out, of the secret outpost
o.zh: 发挥你的口才，潜入并撤离那个秘密据点

entries.en:
The planet below appears to lack any settlements or open comms transmissions. You have your comms officer do a broad transmission of the IFF codes, and a simple ping of approval is returned.

The source of the ping is an outcrop overlooking a plausibly natural-looking plateau. You couldn't ask for a more perfect site to land a shuttle, nor one more exposed to weapon emplacements which would be concealed in the surrounding bluffs.
entries.zh:
下方的行星似乎没有任何定居点或开放的通讯传输。你让通讯军官广播了 IFF 代码，随后收到了一个简短的批准回应。

回应信号源自一处俯瞰自然高原的岩脊。你找不到比这更完美的穿梭机降落地点了，但同样，这里也暴露在可能隐藏在周围悬崖上的武器阵地之下。

entries.en: The shielded crate shuts with the sound of powered bolts sliding home. It sends off a one-time coded hyperwave burst. Confirmation, you suppose. It would have been good of that scientist to warn you about this little trick; hopefully no pirates - or anything else - was listening nearby.
entries.zh: 屏蔽箱在电动闩滑动就位的声响中锁死了。这时它送出了一个一次性编码的超波突发通信。应该是确认讯号，你猜想到。但如果那个学者能提前跟你提一下这个小把戏就好了，现在只能希望附近没有海盗或是其他什么东西正在监听。

o.en: Loot the rest of the cache
o.zh: 把藏匿处的其他东西带走

entries.en:
Your $shipOrFleet arrives at the coordinates provided by the scientist $saic_marketOnOrAt $saic_marketName, and just as $saic_heOrShe said, there is an impressive bounty of Domain-era goods and technology in nearly pristine condition. And in the middle of it all your salvage crew reports a cargo case bearing a Tri-Tachyon logo. It's emitting a bizarre, dynamic magnetic field extending two meters beyond the casing.

It's amazing that no one found this cache before, but then the long-range sensors did read it as a worthless debris cloud at first. The question is now, do you close the AI core into the shielded crate and send it off from your next port stop, or do you keep it for yourself? That scientist was surely no one important.
entries.zh:
你的$shipOrFleet到达了之前在 $saic_marketName 酒吧里遇到的学者所提供的坐标位置。如$saic_heOrShe所言，这里简直是塞满 人之领 时期的货物和科技物品的宝库，且基本上原封未动。你的一名打捞人员向你汇报，在这些物件之中发现了一个带有 速子科技 标志的上了锁的小箱子。它产生了一个奇怪的动态磁场，范围延伸到箱外两米左右。

令人惊讶的是，之前居然没有任何人发现这个藏匿处。不过刚开始的时候从远程传感器的读数上看，这里的确是被误判成了毫无价值的残骸区。现在眼下的问题是，你是打算把 AI 核心封入屏蔽箱，在下次靠港时将它快递寄走，还是说你打算把它据为己有？毕竟那个学者肯定只是个无足轻重的角色。

o.en: Place the Tri-Tachyon case into the shielded crate and send it off as soon as possible
o.zh: 将核心放入学者提供的屏蔽箱内，并尽快寄出

o.en: Take the AI core for yourself
o.zh: 将 AI 核心据为己有

entries.en: You open the Tri-Tachyon case and retrieve a single Alpha Core. It pulses with activity, and your smile is underlit by the cold, alien thoughts of the core. You order the scientist's shielded crate tossed out the airlock. If you want something done in this world, you'd best do it yourself.
entries.zh: 你打开了这曾属于 速子科技 的箱子，从中收获了一枚 Alpha 核心。核心的光芒随着它的运作不断地脉动，那冰冷的非人类思维因而照亮了你的笑脸。你下令把学者的屏蔽箱扔出气闸 —— 如果想在这乱世中办妥什么事，那最好别把它托给别人。

o.en: Loot the rest of the cache
o.zh: 把藏匿处的其他东西带走

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet finishes its approach to the $nameInText without further incident.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet成功抵近了$nameInText，再未发生任何变故。

entries.en:
As your $shipOrFleet finishes mopping up the automated defenses, a weak hyperwave ping is detected coming from the $shortName. It's unclear if this is random noise from a dying subsystem or some kind of encrypted signal.

Your $shipOrFleet finishes its approach to the $nameInText without further incident.
entries.zh:
在你的$shipOrFleet清理掉自动化防御系统的时候，侦测到$shortName中发出了一个微弱的超波连通请求。尚不清楚这是子系统失效时的随机噪声，还是某种加密信号。

你的$shipOrFleet成功抵近了$nameInText，再未发生任何变故。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet approaches $aOrAn $nameInText.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet靠近了 $aOrAn $nameInText。

entries.en: Salvage crews set targeting beacons at key points in the structure.
entries.zh: 打捞人员在结构的关键点设置了瞄准信标。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet approaches $aOrAn $nameInText left from the initial Domain exploration of the Sector.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet靠近了自人之领首次探索本星域时就一直遗留在此的一艘$nameInText。

entries.en: Sensor returns indicate unusually short-lived charged particles near the derelict. Density distribution in the internal structure has also changed from patterns extrapolated from your previous encounters with Domain-era exploration vessels, as if internal masses have been removed or intentionally redistributed.
entries.zh: 传感器反馈显示在残骸附近存在异常的短半衰期带电粒子。残骸的内部结构密度分布也与你之前遇到过 人之领 时代勘探船的推断模式不符，似乎其内部质量遭到了移除或被特意重新分配过。

o.en: Consider whether special measures might be taken to recover this ship
o.zh: 考虑是否采取特别措施来恢复这艘船

o.en: Consider whether special measures might be taken to recover this ship
o.zh: 考虑是否采取特殊手段抢救这艘船

entries.en:
You request a salvage plan, giving due consideration to the likely difficulty of your request.

Before long, you hear back from your chief engineer - mumbling something about not being a miracle worker to someone offscreen before noticing you've accepted the link request.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam." They have the self-awareness to look appropriately embarassed but the professionalism not to let it interrupt a report. "With apologies, no can do. It'd take days just to catalogue all the different critical-level defects. This hull is destined for the scrappers, $playerSirOrMadam."
entries.zh:
你要求拿出一份打捞方案，并充分考虑这一请求多半有多棘手。

没多久，你的轮机长回了话 —— 察觉到你已接通链接之前，还正冲着画面外什么人嘟囔自己又不是能起死回生的神仙。

"$PlayerSirOrMadam。\" 对方还算有自知之明，露出恰到好处的窘态，却又职业地没让这打断汇报，\"恕难从命，长官。光是把各种致命级别的故障清点一遍就得花上好几天。这船壳注定是进拆解场的命，$playerSirOrMadam。"

entries.en: A nearby hostile fleet is tracking your movements, making exploration impossible.
entries.zh: 附近的一支敌对舰队正在追踪你的动向，使你无法进行勘探行动。

entries.en:
The form matches the general pattern of Domain-era mining station designs, but with absolutely no provisions made for human occupation. No hab ring, no life support module, no shuttle receiving bays.

Instead, inactive drone rigs cluster around the ring-trusses. Ore receiving bays lay dark; an agglomeration of zero-G fabricators sprouts from the central spire over the tiers of darkened hangars and warehouses.

Despite the darkened exterior, sensors reports a mix of minor energy readings and the gentle ticking of particles which suggest a stock of concentrated transplutonics.
entries.zh:
面前的物体看上去大致符合 人之领 时代的采矿空间站设计，但是完全没有任何为了人类居住所作的准备。没有居民环，没有维生系统，也没有穿梭机降落台。

取而代之的是环状桁架上四散的无人钻机。矿石接收仓隐藏在黑暗之中；一系列零重力制造厂点缀着中央尖塔，凌驾于漆黑一片的库房和机库之上。

虽然外部漆黑一片，传感器报告显示出一系列微弱的能量反应和轻微的粒子波动，表明此处聚集着密集的稀有元素。

entries.en: The vast bulk of the automated exploration mothership is burned and battered by centuries of service to the Domain, a drifting forgotten hulk, though sensors indicate that some systems are still nominally active.
entries.zh: 这艘巨大的自动化勘探母舰为 人之领 服务了几个世纪的岁月，遭受了数不尽的灼烧和撞击，最终成为了被人遗忘的漂流废船。不过传感器指出，其上的一些系统似乎仍依照设计持续运行着。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, new energy signatures are detected near a larger piece of debris.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，一块大型残骸附近出现了新的能量信号。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, new energy signatures are detected near the $shortName.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，$shortName 附近出现了新的能量信号。

entries.en: Pitted by small impacts, the probe's hull displays iridescence typical of fearsome radiation scarring. Though this probe's manufacture could well date to a thousand cycles ago, some systems are still nominally active.
entries.zh: 这艘探测器的外壳不止被微撞击弄得坑坑洼洼，还出现了因遭受骇人的辐射灼烧所留下的虹彩。尽管这艘探测器的制造时间也许可以追溯到千年以前，但其上的一些系统似乎仍勉强维持着运转。

entries.en: Your $shipOrFleet assumes a stable orbit relative to the debris field.
entries.zh: 你的$shipOrFleet正相对于残骸区保持着稳定轨道。

entries.en: The ancient Domain-era automated survey ship has been ravaged by centuries of exposure to charged particles and high velocity impacts of interstellar dust. Some systems still appear to be nominally active.
entries.zh: 这艘古老的人之领时代自动化勘探舰一直暴露在带电粒子和高速星际尘埃的冲击下，饱受蹂躏了几个世纪。但其上的一些系统似乎仍依照设计持续运行着。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, numerous strong energy signatures are detected coming online inside the darkened work-bays of the mothership's vast hulk. Your sensors also detect several weapon emplacements powering up on the mothership itself.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，母舰庞大舰体内部那些昏暗的工作舱中出现了大量强劲的能量信号。你的传感器还检测到母舰本体上的数个武器装置正在启动供能。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, numerous strong energy signatures are detected coming online inside the darkened work-bays of the mothership's vast hulk.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，母舰庞大舰体内部那些昏暗的工作舱中出现了大量强劲的能量信号。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, your sensors detect several weapon emplacements powering up in darkened crevasses on the mothership's vast hulk.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，你的传感器检测到母舰庞大舰体上的那些阴暗裂缝中有数个武器装置正在启动供能。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, several energy signatures are detected coming online inside the probe's hold.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，侦测到这艘探测器的货舱内出现了数个能量信号。

entries.en: As your $shipOrFleet moves in closer, multiple energy signatures are detected coming online from various points on and within the flayed hull of the survey ship.
entries.zh: 当你的$shipOrFleet靠近时，勘测舰剥落的船体各处及内部出现了多个新的能量信号。

entries.en:
An abandoned orbital habitat, thought to be cold and dead for tens of cycles at least, possibly hundreds.

You visited here and your salvors found a tiny bubble of life sustaining itself off the backup of a backup powered by a fission battery. You found it to be a precious thing, a miracle of life, and declared that there would be no salvage.

Knowing now what exactly to look for, your sensors officers confirms that a tiny green window still glows on the inside hub of this orbital habitat, despite all odds.
entries.zh:
废弃的轨道居住站，推测已经被遗弃了数十、甚至几百星历年。

你曾造访此地，你的打捞员们发现了一处微小的生命泡泡，它依靠着由裂变电池驱动的备用系统的备用系统维持着自身。你认为那是珍贵的生命奇迹，并宣布禁止进行任何打捞作业。

如今明确了搜寻目标后，你的传感器技官确认 —— 尽管概率微乎其微 —— 这座轨道居住站的内部枢纽上，仍有一扇微小的绿色窗口在发光。

entries.en:
A close approach by salvor teams shows a heat source, and glint of artificial light. An anomalous pocket of operational life-support, the emergency subsection backup of a backup somehow running for tens, hundreds of cycles? It is unlikely.

Your officers always perform the standard transponder pings at the start of a salvage operation; it is part of the ritual of legal salvage (though records of legality are fabricated easily enough, when required, and doing a good job of it is a sign of respect appreciated by customs officers across the Persean Sector).

It would be awkward to stumble into some hermit's cell, ideologue's oubliette, or pirate holdfast unannounced, so your comms officer takes charge of a new signalling attempt with a full range of communication protocols, from an overpowered standard holo-link to mere radio, laser staccato, and even an esoteric grav-pulse relay.
entries.zh:
打捞小组抵近勘察后发现了一处热源与人造光源的反光。一个异常运行的生命维持系统气穴，某套备用系统的紧急子模块竟持续运转了数十乃至数百个星历年？这极不寻常。

你的军官在打捞作业前总会执行标准的应答器脉冲扫描 —— 这是合法打捞作业的一部分 (尽管在必要时可以轻松伪造合法性记录，但做好这点会赢得英仙座星域各地海关官员的尊重)。

贸然闯入某个隐士居所、狂热者地牢或海盗据点将十分尴尬，因此你的通讯军官主导了一次全协议频段的新信号尝试：从超功率标准全息链接到普通无线电、激光断续信号，甚至动用了深奥的重力脉冲中继器。

o.zh: 通讯军官，有什么要汇报的吗？

entries.en:
"No, $playerSirOrMadam," Comms replies. "Nothing. With your permission, I've got an idea..."

An acoustic inducer-transponder, normally used in mining surveys, is tenderly attached to the hab's structure by a discreet remote probe. It thuds out a code, and detects only a tiny, noisy, rhythmic vibration in return. Something tapping on the hullplate with slow, clock-like regularity.

It doesn't change.
entries.zh:
"没有，$playerSirOrMadam，" 通讯军官答道，"没有任何回应。如果您允许的话，我有个想法..."

通常用于矿业勘探的声波感应应答器，通过隐蔽的远程探测器轻柔附着在居住站的结构上。它发出了编码震动，并且只探测到微弱、嘈杂且有节奏的振动反馈，某种以缓慢如钟表般的规律敲击外壳板的声响。

这声音毫无变化。

entries.en:
Your Ops chief oversees a careful breach of the habitat, wary both for traps and the need to not disrupt the surviving bubble of life-support. Survivors make salvage rights more complex, but they're generally thankful enough for rescue to come to a profitable accommodation.

Salvors attach temporary bubble-locks around the entry points, inflate them with the ubiquitous portable atmo units, and perform a cold-cut on sealed emergency doors. Slow and safe. Ops nods, satisfied with the work proceeding on the shared display.
entries.zh:
你的行动长官监督着对居住站的谨慎破拆作业，既要警惕陷阱，也需避免破坏残存的生命维持泡泡。幸存者的存在会让打捞权复杂化，但他们通常会对救援感恩戴德，愿意达成互利协议。

打捞员在入口处安装了临时气密舱，用便携式大气单元充气，并对密封的应急门进行冷切割。过程缓慢而稳妥，行动长官点头表示满意，共享显示屏上的作业也正按计划推进。

entries.en:
A spot of green-yellow brightness at the end of a foggy corridor; the image stabilizer kicks in, cancelling the jerky hop-step of the lead salvor's micro-g movement.

A tiny garden grows wild within this celestial tomb. Some kind of fissile backup battery has survived, clicking away the decay of heavy elements to heat and light a tiny bubble of life. Moisture condenses in a murky lens of slush on a hubward window, then falls slowly in huge drops through the micro-g of the habitat's spin, past the glowplates, toward the mosses and molds and tiny flowers growing on the warm heaps of droppings and husks of vermin.

On a life-giving terran world, this would be nothing more than a dank pit. Here, it is a miracle.
entries.zh:
雾蒙蒙的走廊尽头有一点黄绿色的光斑；随着图像稳定器的启动，领队打捞员在微重力环境中跳跃式前进的抖动也被抵消。

在这座天体坟墓中，有一小片花园在恣意生长。某种裂变备用电池仍在运作，以重元素衰变释放的热量与光线维持着这微小的生命气泡。水汽在朝向枢纽的窗户上凝结成浑浊的冰泥透镜，随后在聚居地自转的微重力环境中化为巨大液滴缓缓坠落，掠过发光板，洒向暖烘烘的粪堆与害虫空壳上滋生的苔藓、霉菌与细小花丛。

若在适宜生命的类地行星上，这不过是个潮湿的坑洼。但在此地，却堪称奇迹。

entries.en: "$PlayerSirOrMadam," your ops chief responds, the very hint of a question in their tone.
entries.zh: "$playerSirOrMadam，" 你的行动长官回复道，语气中带着一丝疑问。

o.en: We shall leave this place as it is. No salvage.
o.zh: 我们不应该打扰此地，停止打捞。

o.en: You may proceed with the operation.

entries.en: "$PlayerSirOrMadam." Your ops chief acknowledges your command as a law unyielding as gravity itself, and orders the salvors to withdraw without disturbing anything. They know better than to clutter the chief's comms with questions, so they respond quietly and efficiently.
entries.zh: "$playerSirOrMadam。" 你的行动长官将你的指令奉若重如地心引力的铁律，下令打捞员们原地撤离且不得触碰任何物品。他们深知不可用疑问扰乱长官的通讯，因此悄然而高效地执行着指令。

o.en: 'Where there is life, that is the throne of God...'
o.zh: '凡有普罗众生之处，皆为神的宝座所在...'

entries.en: "$PlayerSirOrMadam." Your ops chief acknowledges your command and begins ordering the dance of surveying, inventorying, extraction, and transport.
entries.zh: "$playerSirOrMadam。" 你的行动长官确认了你的指令，随即开始指挥勘察、清点、开采与运输等一系列作业。

entries.en:
Upon entry, your salvors discover first one, then many of the same portrait adorning the interior sections of the hab. Smashed busts line the primary reception concourse. Above all stood a statue of the selfsame likeness churned out of a simple rock-foam fabricator, polished, and gilded; it now lies face-planted into the deckplates, the gilding half-stripped.

All bear the face of a strong-jawed man who looks down upon the empty halls and dead plazas of the hab, his gaze fatherly; stern, and proud. And in all cases defaced: the nose smashed off, crude words painted or, more often, burnt across his image.

Even his name, whatever it was, has been erased from every databank by a spitefully determined noise-wipe virus.
entries.zh:
进入后，救援人员先发现一幅，继而发现多幅相同的肖像装饰着居住站的内部区域。破碎的半身像沿着主接收港区排列，最显眼处矗立着一座由简易岩石泡沫制造机批量生产的同款雕像，经打磨与镀金；如今它面朝下瘫倒在甲板上，镀金层已半剥落。

所有雕像皆刻画着同一位颌骨坚毅的男子，他俯视着居住站空荡的走廊与死寂的广场，目光如父辈般慈爱，却又严厉而骄傲。每尊雕像都遭到了玷污：鼻子被砸碎，粗鄙的涂鸦，更多是烧灼的痕迹，这些都遍布在他的形象上。

就连他的名字 —— 无论曾是何名 —— 也被某种恶意十足的噪声擦除病毒从所有数据库中彻底抹去。

entries.en:
Exploring further, the salvor teams discover the remains of a palace dominating an entire section of the hab.

Once a vast construction, now just two blackened support legs remain amidst the rubble of its shattered visage. Parklands, now reduced to lone and level ash, follow the curve of the habitat's shell.

Whoever the man was, he was first exalted and then hated in equal measure.
entries.zh:
在进一步的探索中，打捞小组发现一座宫殿遗迹占据了居住站的整个区域。

这座曾经宏伟的建筑，如今仅剩两根焦黑的支撑柱伫立在残破的废墟中。依照居住站外壳曲线延伸的园林，已化作孤寂而平坦的灰烬。

无论此人是谁，可以推测他曾被极度尊崇，随后又遭到同等程度的憎恨。

entries.en: The ruins on the surface of $marketName have been stripped of anything easily accessible, and further exploitation requires a permanent presence.
entries.zh: $marketName 地表废墟中容易回收的物件已经搜刮殆尽。进一步的探索需要建立长期设施进行支持。

entries.en: Ruined cities can be found across the surface of $marketName, spilling from their broken hearts pitted roadways and crumbling magrail lines to the skeletons of factories, aquaponics domes, and comm-towers.
entries.zh: 破败的城市废墟遍布于 $marketName 地表。以它们为中心，失修的道路和损坏的磁轨线四向放射出去，连接着只剩下遗骸的制造厂房，水培建筑和通讯塔楼。

entries.en: A nearby hostile fleet is tracking your movements, making exploration of the planet impossible.
entries.zh: 附近的一支敌对舰队正在追踪你的动向，使你无法进行勘探行动。

entries.en: While long-term exploitation of the resources in these ruins requires a colony, a salvage team can conduct a search for anything of immediate value.
entries.zh: 派出打捞小组能马上搜寻并回收所有可以直接利用的东西，而长期开发这些废墟中的资源需要建立一个殖民地。

entries.en: Scattered, broken domes dot the planet's surface, perchance holding lost caches of valuable materials.
entries.zh: 少量破损的穹状建筑零星散布在星球地表，也许里面还藏有些有价值的物资。

entries.en: $marketName is covered in vast ruins; cities, factories, mines, farms, homes. The dead are in dread abundance, entwined with salvageable materials, goods, tools, and weapons. This world is a tomb for the hubris of the Domain's project of galactic colonization and hegemony.
entries.zh: $marketName 被大量的城市遗迹、工厂废墟、矿山残骸、农场遗址和住宅碎片覆盖。死者不计其数，尸体与可回收的材料、货物、工具和武器交缠在一起，触目惊心。这个世界是一座坟墓，人之领 狂妄的银河殖民统治计划被埋葬于此。

entries.en: Widespread ruins, blips from radiation sources, and the distinctive burred radar-ping of foamed cerametal structures can be found across $marketName, evidence of a small but concerted colonization effort dating to the late expansion period of the Domain.
entries.zh: 大量的废墟、辐射源讯号与泡沫陶化金属建筑物的独特雷达回波一起广泛地分布在 $marketName 上，印证了这里曾进行过殖民活动。时间可追溯到 人之领 扩张纪元末期。规模虽小但运作协调。

entries.en: The ruins in low orbit of $marketName have been stripped of anything easily accessible. Further exploitation of abandoned buoyant structures requires a permanent presence.
entries.zh: $marketName 的低轨道废墟中容易回收的物件已经搜刮殆尽。对废弃漂浮建筑的进一步探索需要建立长期设施进行支持。

entries.en: Ruined buoyant cities and factories can be seen in the clouds of $marketName, slowly sinking into the crushing depths, trailing kilometers of tether. Low-orbit factories, ring-habs, and comm-relays slowly succumb to atmospheric drag and occasionally but dramatically burn a line across the swirling face of the planet.
entries.zh: 悬浮都市和浮游工厂的废墟在 $marketName 的云层中依稀可见。它们拖着几公里长的系绳，缓慢地向着压力能粉碎一切深度沉下去。低轨道工厂、环形居住舱和通信中继站逐渐屈服于大气阻力，时不时地划过星球表面的巨大漩涡，留下壮观的火流星尾迹。

entries.en: Scattered, sinking buoyant platforms dot the clouds of $marketName, perchance holding lost caches of valuable materials.
entries.zh: 正在下沉的漂浮平台零散地分布在 $marketName 的云层中，也许上面还藏有些有价值的物资。

entries.en: The clouds of $marketName are filled with the vast ruins of buoyant sky-cities, dead jewels of farms, habitats, and transport hubs trailing on near-invisible tethers. Low-orbit factories, hab-rings, and power transmitters sparkle in the twilight, a steady slew of debris catching in the atmosphere and burning lines on the face of the planet. The dead are in dread abundance, entwined with salvageable materials, goods, tools, and weapons. This world is a stormy tomb for the hubris of the Domain's project of galactic colonization and hegemony.
entries.zh: 宏伟的浮空城市曾主宰 $marketName 的云层，如今它们犹如蒙尘的珠宝待人挖掘。毫无生气的农场、居住区和交通枢纽等设施被几乎不可见的系绳拴在一起，低轨道工厂、居住环和电力传输器在暮色中不时闪烁。时刻都有大量的残骸坠入大气层，化做火雨划过行星表面。死者不计其数，尸体与可回收的材料、货物、工具和武器交缠在一起，令人触目惊心。无尽的风暴吹打着这座坟墓，将 人之领 狂妄的银河殖民统治计划埋葬于此。

entries.en: Low-orbit platforms blip with radiation sources and the distinctive burred radar-ping of foamed cerametal can be found widespread through the clouds of $marketName, evidence of a small but concerted colonization effort dating to the late expansion period of the Domain.
entries.zh: 低轨道平台发出的辐射源讯号与泡沫陶化金属建筑物的独特雷达回波一起广泛地分布在 $marketName 上，印证了这里曾进行过殖民活动。时间可追溯到 人之领 扩张纪元末期。规模虽小但运作协调。

entries.en:
Your salvors fan out through the station, discovering makeshift barricades around the access tubes to the executive and security modules. There's interior combat damage caused by handheld weapons, many of which appear to have been adapted from mining tools. A strike turned deadly.

The security forces employed riot-suppression armaments at first, then rapidly escalated to their cache of "vac-safe" weapons intended for boarding and infantry action within ship hulls or station modules.

The miners appear to have responded by up-armoring standard haz suits, adding breastplates worked from mining drones' blast panels, slotted visors cut from rolls of nuke-rated anti-spall sheeting, and much other imaginative makeshift panoply.
entries.zh:
你的打捞员们在空间站内散开搜查，发现通往行政与安防模块的通道管周围设有临时路障。内部存在手持武器造成的战斗痕迹 —— 其中许多显然由采矿工具改装而成。一场罢工演变为了致命冲突。

安保部队起初使用的是防暴武器，随后迅速升级为 "真空安全" 级别军火库 —— 这类装备本用于舰船舱内或空间站模块的登船与步兵作战。

矿工们的回应则是强化版的标准防护服：加装采矿无人机防爆板改造的胸甲、核爆级防碎片卷材切割而成的槽缝面罩，以及其他充满想象力的临时武装。

entries.en:
With the tides turning against them once more, security forces fought a break-out action toward central life support.

Successful, they choked off atmo and water to those modules held by the strikers. This won the fight, if the heavily armored but nonetheless desiccated corpses floating through the corridors have anything to say about it, but the war was still lost.

The station appears to have been abandoned as-is, too much of a scandal to reactivate or, perhaps, merely a write-off.
entries.zh:
在局势再度逆转后，安保部队发起了突围行动，向中央生命维持系统推进。

他们成功切断了罢工者控制模块的大气与水供应。如果走廊里漂浮的那些身着重甲却已干瘪的尸体能够开口，他们会证明此举赢得了一时的战斗，但整场战争却早已彻底失败。

空间站显然被原封不动地遗弃了，或许是因为丑闻影响过大，又或许仅仅是被当作一笔坏账。

entries.en:
Your salvors spread out through the $nameInText in teams under the gruff direction of your Ops Chief. Salvage is rapidly identified, assessed, logged, and tagged with trackers, when appropriate, for follow-up teams to extract.

Computers and datastores are accessed via disposable interfacers, rough and quick hardware jobs that send back any information they can lift from poorly shielded databanks. Back on your $shipOrFleet, your tech teams crack security and decrypts anything they can, forwarding useful information - maps, cargo manifests, engineering diagrams - back to the salvors to use.
entries.zh:
你的打捞员们在行动长官粗声粗气的指挥下，以小组的形式分散至 $nameInText 各处。他们迅速识别、评估并记录着打捞物资，并在适当时加装追踪器以供后续小组提取。

通过一次性接口设备，计算机与数据存储系统被成功骇入 —— 这些简陋而高效的硬件装置能从防护薄弱的数据库中窃取所有可获取的信息。在你的$shipOrFleet上，你的技官团队负责破解加密，将任何可解译的有用信息 —— 地图、货单、工程图纸，悉数转发给打捞员们参考。

entries.en:
These teams are experts at rapidly reconstructing the relevant events of a starship or space station's demise; such a narrative provides useful information about dangers and valuables.

Here, comms logs and surveillance gives meaning to the evidence of scattered damage caused by light firearms - local security was in the process of a major crackdown on a drug smuggling operation, and in an explosive confrontation appears to have caused a blowout of the primary hab section. This seems to have tipped the state of the station, already precarious, into a full evacuation.

The rest of the story is mere salvage for your waiting holds.
entries.zh:
这些小组擅长快速重建星舰或空间站覆灭的关键事件脉络；这类叙事能提供有关危险与贵重物资的重要信息。

在这里，通讯记录与监控资料为轻型枪械造成的零星损伤提供了背景：当地安保部门当时正对毒品走私活动展开大规模打击，一场爆炸性的冲突似乎导致主要居住舱段发生破裂。这显然使本已岌岌可危的空间站状况彻底恶化，最终引发了全面撤离。

至于余下的故事，不过是你待装货舱中的普通打捞物罢了。

entries.en:
Your salvors discover that comms and anti-collision weapon emplacements have been deliberately destroyed by careful strikes.

Closer examination shows evidence that a pirate ship docked - the brutal hull markings and garish paint job of the gutted hulk are a giveaway - but was completely disabled in the cargo bay by some kind of makeshift explosive adapted from on-hand mining equipment.

Their plundering mothership destroyed, the remaining pirates - operating a handful of light frigates and a wing of fighters - appear to have taken out their anger by strafing the station's hab modules and life support before going on their way.

The few miners who survived the immediate attack were doomed to a slow death.
entries.zh:
你的打捞员们发现通讯阵列与防撞武器平台均已被精心策划的打击蓄意摧毁。

进一步勘察显示曾有海盗舰船停靠于此 —— 残骸上粗暴的船体标记与花哨涂装是明显的证据 —— 但该舰船在货舱中被某种由现成采矿设备改装的临时爆炸装置完全瘫痪。

随着劫掠母船被毁，驾驶着数艘轻型护卫舰与一支战机编队的残余海盗，似乎将怒火倾泻在空间站的居住模块与生命维持系统上，并在进行完扫射攻击后扬长而去。

少数在直接袭击中幸存的矿工，最终仍难逃缓慢死亡的命运。

entries.en: Your ops chief also remembers, it seems, for they meet your eye just briefly as they give orders for the salvor teams to adjust dispositions in response to this discovery.
entries.zh: 你的行动长官显然也记着，因为他短暂地与你对视了一眼，随即下令调整打捞小组的部署以应对这一发现。

entries.en: Your ops chief also remembers, it seems, for they meet your eye just briefly as they give orders for the salvor teams to adjust dispositions in response to this discovery.
entries.zh: 你的行动长官显然也记着，因为他短暂地与你对视了一眼，随即下令调整打捞小组的部署以应对这一发现。

entries.en:
Your ops chief also remembers, it seems, for they meet your eye just briefly as they give orders for the salvor teams to adjust dispositions in response to this discovery. As you recall, Ops didn't even smile. They never joke about procedure.

Never.
entries.zh:
你的行动长官显然也记着，因为他短暂地与你对视了一眼，随即下令调整打捞小组的部署以应对这一发现。如你所忆，行动长甚至没有露出一丝笑意，他从不在流程规范上开玩笑。

绝不。

entries.en:
Your salvors proceed with a routine ingress, by-the-book under the suspicious eyes of your ops chief.

An atmo sample of a trapped pocket - a tedious checklist task - pull up bright orange and green on the shared display: extreme biohazard. The salvor working the derelict almost drops the sampler-drill in surprise; Ops barks sharp orders, reiterating the hazardous environment recovery ingress checklist with effortless recall.
entries.zh:
你的打捞员们按常规程序进入，在你行动长官警惕的目光下严格遵循操作手册开始作业。

对一处封闭气穴大气采样作业 —— 原本只清单上的例行琐事而已 —— 却突然在共享显示器上亮起了刺目的橙绿警告：极端生物危害。正在废船内作业的打捞员差点就要在惊慌中抛下采样钻；行动长厉声呵斥之后，熟练地背诵出了危险环境回收作业的入舱检查清单。

entries.en: It's an unusual reading, but not dangerous if containment procedures are followed to the letter.
entries.zh: 这是个异常读数，但只要严格遵守封存流程便没有危险。

entries.en:
It's an unusual reading, and you recall the harsh words Ops gave you after returning to your $shipOrFleet after you exposed yourself to the xenolife of Jangala, albeit wearing a mask.

You also remember...
entries.zh:
这是个异常读数，而你也回忆起自己暴露在 Jangala 的异种生命中后 —— 尽管戴着防护面罩 —— 再返回$shipOrFleet时，行动长对你的严厉训斥。

你还记起...

o.en: Interrupting the tirade to inform them that you are the sole executive authority on this $shipOrFleet.
o.zh: 打断训斥，并告知他你才是$shipOrFleet的唯一最高指挥官。

o.en: Thanking them for emphasizing procedure, but to be mindful of their tone in front of crew.
o.zh: 感谢他对流程规范的强调，但提醒其注意在船员面前的语气。

o.en: Making a crack about 'containment procedures' and visiting spacer bars which made the crew laugh.
o.zh: 拿 "封存流程" 和逛太空酒吧开玩笑，逗得船员们哈哈大笑。

entries.en:
It's an unusual reading, and you'll never forget the dressing-down Ops gave you after returning to your $shipOrFleet after you exposed yourself to the xenolife of Jangala without even the benefit of a mask.

You also remember...
entries.zh:
这是个异常读数，而你也忘不了自己暴露在 Jangala 的异种生命中后 —— 而且连面罩都没戴 —— 再返回$shipOrFleet时，行动长对你的那顿痛斥。

你还记起...

o.en: Interrupting the tirade to inform them that you are the sole executive authority on this $shipOrFleet.
o.zh: 打断训斥，并告知他你才是$shipOrFleet的唯一最高指挥官。

o.en: Thanking them for emphasizing procedure, but to be mindful of their tone in front of crew.
o.zh: 感谢他对流程规范的强调，但提醒其注意在船员面前的语气。

o.en: Making a crack about 'containment procedures' and visiting spacer bars which made the crew laugh.
o.zh: 拿 "封存流程" 和逛太空酒吧开玩笑，逗得船员们哈哈大笑。

entries.en:
One particular module of this research station appears to have been a bioweapons laboratory. The lab is - rather, was - hermetically sealed, and contains the ruins of state-of-the-art containment and decontamination facilities.

Naturally, something went terribly wrong.

And as your techies analyze telemetry and what raw surveillance buffers the salvors on-station are able to transmit back to your $shipOrFleet, the disaster begins to look distinctly unnatural.
entries.zh:
该研究站的某个特定模块似乎是生物武器实验室。实验室原本是 —— 或者说曾是 —— 气密封闭的，且其内部仍残留着尖端水平的封存与净化设施遗迹。

显然，某些环节出现了灾难性故障。

而随着你的技术小组开始分析遥测数据，以及站内打捞员设法传把原始监控缓冲记录输回$shipOrFleet后，这场灾难开始显现出明显的人为痕迹。

o.zh: 行动长，是什么导致了这种情况？

entries.en:
"Sabotage," your ops chief mutters darkly.

The patchy surveillance shows a rapid spread of violent, painful demise beginning in atmospheric processing and spreading outward at the speed of fresh air through atmo conduits, tripping the broad-spectrum biohazard sensors one by one as the agent suffused through the station. But no alarm sounded for human ears.

Your salvage chief orders all remaining pockets of atmo purged, and strict quarantine procedures followed.

The bioweapons lab's computer core destroyed itself with a small bomb when a timed dead man's switch was not reset, so nothing of salable value remains, if indeed a buyer could be found for whatever biochemical horror was conjured here.
entries.zh:
"蓄意破坏，" 你的行动长官阴沉地低语道。

断续的监控画面显示，一场迅猛而痛苦的死亡从大气处理系统爆发，以新鲜空气通过通气管道扩散的速度向外蔓延。当毒剂弥漫整个空间站时，广谱生物危害传感器接连被触发，但未响起任何人类可闻的警报。

你的打捞长官下令净化所有的残留气穴，并严格执行隔离程序。

生物武器实验室的计算机核心因定时自毁装置未被重置而通过小型炸弹进行了自毁，因此这里已不存在任何具有出售价值的物品 —— 即便真的有人愿意购买此处制造的生化恐怖产物。

entries.en:
A precise decapitation strike appears to have targeted the command and control module of this station, likely a clutch of military-grade torpedoes unleashed at close range by an unsuspected vessel.

Security systems were tight and highly hierarchical; once the central C&C went down, automatic lockdown procedures trapped the occupants of the station in their sections - habitation, labs, research, recreation, life support, cargo handling, storage, engineering, cooling, and so on.

Now each is a locked tomb preserving evidence of the final hours, sometimes days, of the occupants.
entries.zh:
一次精准的斩首式打击似乎击中了该空间站的指挥控制模块，很可能是由一艘未被察觉的舰船在近距离释放的一簇军用级鱼雷。

此处的安防系统十分严密且高度层级化；一旦中央指挥控制模块瘫痪，自动封锁程序便将站内人员困在各个分区 —— 居住舱、实验室、研究区、娱乐设施、生命维持系统、货舱处理区、存储库、工程区、冷却单元等等。

如今每个分区都成了锁闭的坟墓，封存着居住者临终数时乃至数日的痕迹。

entries.en: Your salvor teams do not tarry to ponder the fate of these unfortunate souls, each miserable in its own way, as they cut through the lockdown doors to assess valuables.
entries.zh: 你的打捞小组无暇思索这些以各自的可悲方式死去的灵魂的命运，他们径直切割开封锁的舱门以评估有价值的物资。

entries.en:
Salvor teams cut through fused locks and infiltrate the station. They find researchers, administrators, technicians down to the lowliest access-tunnel scrubber at their work-stations, or near enough. Quite dead, however. And even those who remained in pockets of viable atmo are surprisingly undecayed.

Their end was not pleasant, but it appears to have at least been very, very quick.

Your salvors and tech teams assemble evidence to reconstruct the event: a massive radiation pulse centered on Experiment Module B, which, judging from the gap between the ruins of Modules A and C, was almost entirely vaporized by the event.
entries.zh:
打捞小组切开熔合的锁具并进入了空间站。他们发现研究员、行政人员、技术员乃至最低级的通道清洁工都倒在了工作岗位或附近区域，无一例外已经死亡。而即便是那些残留在可呼吸气穴中的人员，尸身也异常地并未腐烂。

他们的结局并不安详，但至少看来非常，非常迅速。

你的打捞员们与技术小组开始整合证据并重建事件：一场巨大辐射脉冲曾以 B 实验模块为中心爆发，根据 A 模块与 C 模块废墟间的缺口判断，该模块几乎在此事件中完全汽化。

o.en: Any sign of what they were trying to do?
o.zh: 有什么迹象表明他们当时的企图吗？

entries.en:
Your tech officer shakes their head, showing characteristic frustration at having their curiosity unfulfilled.

No relevant monitoring and computer system from Module B survived, and the general practice of this station appears to have involved heavy siloing of information even up to the level of the executive command section, so it's impossible to say what exactly the research being pursued involved or, indeed, whether the event was an accident or something more sinister.

Whatever it was, at least it happened a long time ago.
entries.zh:
你的技术军官摇摇头，显露出好奇心未得满足时特有的沮丧。

B 模块的相关监控与计算机系统无一幸存，且该空间站的普遍操作似乎涉及严格的信息隔离，甚至延伸至执行指挥层级，因此无法断定其具体的研究内容，也无法确认这次事件是事故还是更险恶的阴谋。

无论如何，至少那是很久以前的事了。

entries.en:
Although superficially intact, salvor teams soon find evidence of light weapons fire and the resulting carnage, thankfully long desiccated, decayed, and/or frozen depending on the run-down time of life support in any particular sector.

The seemingly random spread and directionlessness of the violence suggests that the security systems of this station turned on its occupants all at once. The catastrophic results were not helped by the unusually strong internal security measures: hidden autoturrets set to kill, powered lockdown curtains which indiscriminately scissored obstructions, and nests of mobile suppression drones which could traverse small conduits and air ducts to find and "neutralize" any survivors.

Thankfully, the last of these measures has long run out of power.
entries.zh:
尽管表面完好无损，打捞小组很快发现了轻武器射击的痕迹以及其造成的惨状，所幸这些遗骸因生命维持系统在不同区域的衰竭时间差异而早已干枯、腐烂或冻结。

暴力事件看上去似乎是随机蔓延且毫无方向性的，也暗示该空间站的安保系统曾集体反噬其居住者。这灾难性后果因异常严密的内部安防措施雪上加霜：暗藏的自动炮塔被设定为杀伤模式，动力封锁帘无差别地剪切着障碍物，成群的机动压制无人机能穿越狭窄的管道与风道，追踪并 "清除" 了任何幸存者。

谢天谢地，这套系统最后早已耗尽了能源。

entries.en:
Despite the station's reactor being run down, and the power network itself highly degraded, your salvors are understandably paranoid. Your Ops Chief is more than satisfied to use their fear to emphasize the necessity of strict and systematic recovery protocols in this - and indeed every - recovery operation.

Try as they might to piece something together from station logs, it remains unclear to your tech team what precisely used the chief administrator's executive access codes to turn the security systems inward.
entries.zh:
尽管空间站的反应堆已经停运，电力网络也严重衰变，但你的打捞员们仍难免草木皆兵。你的行动长官非常乐意利用这种恐惧心理，来强调此次 —— 实际上是每次 —— 打捞行动中严格执行系统性回收规程的必要性。

你的技术小组竭力拼凑着空间站日志，但仍然无法确切查明究竟是什么利用首席管理员的高级权限密码，将安防系统转向了内部。

entries.en:
You manage to convince the patrol commander that $heOrShe would get in trouble with $hisOrHer superiors if $heOrShe pressed the issue.
OR
The patrol commander appears to have a venal streak a mile wide, and some vague promises of favors owed and eventual compensation convince $himOrHer to look the other way.
entries.zh:
你设法让巡逻队指挥官相信，如果$heOrShe坚持要惹事的话，$hisOrHer的上司就会让$heOrShe吃不了兜着走。
OR
看来巡逻队的指挥官早就贪腐成性，在一些诸如欠个人情以后必有重谢之类的含糊承诺之下，$himOrHer睁一只眼闭一只眼放了你一马。

o.en: Offer to pay for charts of local hyperspace and slipstream routes
o.zh: 提出愿意购买附近的超空间和滑流路径图

entries.en:
You discuss the data the scavenger has available in the roundabout telling-but-not-telling these sorts of negotiations entail, and eventually settle on a price of $ht_dataCost credits.

The dataset includes the locations of all slipstreams within $ht_dataRange lights of your current location, and useful information about hyperspace topography.
entries.zh:
你和拾荒者讨论着他们出售的数据，在话中有话的谈判过程中周旋着讨价还价，最终你们把价格定在 $ht_dataCost 星币。

这组数据里有附近 $ht_dataRange 光年所有的滑流位置，还包括了关于当地超空间测绘的有用信息。

entries.en:
You discuss the data the scavenger has available in the roundabout way these sorts of negotiations entail, eventually settling on a price of $ht_dataCost credits. The dataset includes the locations of all slipstreams within $ht_dataRange lights of your current location.

You've recently acquired hypertopographic data not too far from your current hyperspace location, so this new data would not meaningfully contribute to your overall charts.
entries.zh:
你和拾荒者讨论着他们出售的数据，在一番周旋与讨价还价过后，最终你们把价格定在 $ht_dataCost 星币。这组数据里有附近 $ht_dataRange 光年所有的滑流位置，还包括了关于当地超空间测绘的有用信息。

你最近得到过距你现在位置不远处的超空间测绘，所以这组新数据并 不会 为你的总体地图提供有效更新。

o.en: I found Achilles Andrada. He's working with Gens Kato... (explain)
o.zh: 我找到了 Achilles Andrada。他正跟 Kato 氏族 合作... (解释)

o.en: I found Hector Andrada in the Hybrasil system... (explain)
o.zh: 我在 Hybrasil 星系找到了 Hector Andrada... (解释)

o.en: I'm getting the impression that Tri-Tachyon has been assisting the Sindrian Diktat.
o.zh: 我的感觉是，速子科技一直在协助辛达强权。

o.en: I found Leonidas Andrada. And two AI cores... (explain)
o.zh: 我找到了 Leonidas Andrada。还有两个 AI 核心... (解释)

o.en: How much do you know about the contents of these files?
o.zh: 关于这些文件的内容，你知道多少？

o.en: If you're not working with Macario, how do you know the contents of these files?
o.zh: 既然你不替 Macario 做事，那你怎么会知道这些文件的内容？

o.en: I'd like to talk about something else.

entries.en:
He tilts his head ever so slightly, gaze locked through the comms.

Making a point of giving you no answer.
entries.zh:
他极轻微地偏了偏头，目光透过通讯链接钉在你身上。

摆明了不打算答你。

entries.en:
He looks over you for a long moment before responding.

"That's what lots of people heard."
entries.zh:
他打量了你许久，才开口。

"很多人听到的就是这个版本。"

o.zh: 你是说那件事根本没发生？

entries.en:
"Not like that." He pauses for a moment, then says, "What is it you want, spacer."

The latent irritation makes his question into a demand: explain yourself.
entries.zh:
"不是那么回事。\"他顿了顿，才说，\"你想要什么，太空佬。"

那股按着的火气把他的问话压成了一道命令：说清楚你的来意。

entries.en:
He looks over you for a long moment before responding.

"They told everyone it was a bar fight." After another pause, he speaks, "What is it you want, spacer."

The latent irritation makes his question into a demand: explain yourself.
entries.zh:
他打量了你许久，才开口。

"他们对外说那是一场酒吧斗殴。\"又停了一阵，他才开口，\"你想要什么，太空佬。"

那股按着的火气把他的问话压成了一道命令：说清楚你的来意。

entries.en:
The touch of a self-satisfied smile appears. Achilles nods; a gesture of respect for catching on so quickly.

"I suspected," he says. "So did Fleet Intel, for quite some time. Siyavong confirmed it when he finally contacted me."
entries.zh:
他唇上浮起一丝自得的笑。Achilles 点了点头——那是敬你反应这么快的意思。

"我早怀疑过。\"他说。\"舰队情报部也是，已经很久了。Siyavong 终于联系上我的时候，把这件事确认了下来。"

entries.en:
"Help me." His words are deadpan, unbelieving.

"Why would you help me? Who even are you?"
entries.zh:
"帮帮我。"他的语气平板，透着不信。

"你为什么要帮我？你到底是什么人？"

entries.en:
"Help me." His words are deadpan, unbelieving.

"Why would you help me? Who even are you?"
entries.zh:
"帮帮我。"他的语气平板，透着不信。

"你为什么要帮我？你到底是什么人？"

entries.en:
The comms stall on the crest of the Persean League navy.

No one is accepting a connection.
entries.zh:
通讯请求卡在英仙座联盟海军的徽标画面上，迟迟不通。

没有一个人接听。

entries.en:
The link snaps into an active connection. The young man looks impatient.

"Yes, what do you want?"

His face is familiar from the intel reports. And historical holos.

Once you know what, who, you're looking at, it's impossible to unsee. But, strikingly, in a Persean League Fleet uniform rather than that of a Hegemony officer. It feels quite wrong.
entries.zh:
通讯链接啪地接通。对面的年轻人一脸不耐烦。

"说吧，什么事？"

那张脸你在情报报告里见过。也在历史全息影像里见过。

一旦你认出眼前这个人是谁，这相似就再也躲不开。可最扎眼的是那一身英仙座联盟舰队制服，而不是霸主的军官装。看着实在不对劲。

o.en: Is the Persean League going to back you? Do you trust them?
o.zh: 英仙座联盟会支持你吗？你信得过他们？

o.en: Kazeron is going to use you up. Like it uses everyone.
o.zh: Kazeron 会把你榨干。就像它榨干每一个人。

o.en: You're going to need help, Achilles. Allies.
Kazeron is going to use you up. Like it uses everyone.
o.zh: Kazeron 会把你榨干。就像它榨干每一个人。

o.en: You're going to need help, Achilles. Allies.
You can't do this without serious financial backing, Achilles.
o.zh: 没有雄厚的财力撑着，你办不成这件事，Achilles。

o.en: Another one of you is already making a move. Macario's pawn.
o.zh: 另一个你已经在行动了。Macario 的棋子。

o.en: You need to go into hiding. The Hegemony would be willing to assist.
o.zh: 你需要躲起来。霸主愿意出手相助。

o.en: You need to go into hiding. Fleet Intel is sure to help you.
o.zh: 你需要躲起来。舰队情报部一定会帮你。

o.en: You've the blood of Andrada. Do you understand what that means?
o.zh: 你身上流着 Andrada 的血。你明白这意味着什么吗？

o.en: The Sindrian Diktat needs a leader. You could be the one.
o.zh: 辛达强权需要一位领袖。你可以是那个人。

entries.en:
"Everyone is someone's pawn, captain," he says. A touch of amusement appears on his lips. "Until they're not."

His eyes drill into you. It's that intense Andrada look, familiar from the propaganda holos. Self-confident to the point of hubris. The eyes that watched as fleets burned in the skies of Askonia.
entries.zh:
"每个人都是某人的棋子，舰长。\"他说，唇边浮起一点玩味。\"直到不再是为止。"

他的目光钉进你眼里。那是 Andrada 家特有的逼人眼神，宣传全息里常见的那种。自信到近乎狂妄。就是这双眼睛，看着舰队在 Askonia 诸世界的天空中烧成火海。

entries.en:
The link snaps into an active connection. The young man looks impatient.

"Yes, what do you want?"

His face is familiar from the intel reports. And historical holos.

Once you know what, who, you're looking at, it's impossible to unsee. But, strikingly, in a Persean League Fleet uniform rather than that of a Hegemony officer. It feels quite wrong.
entries.zh:
通讯链接啪地接通。对面的年轻人一脸不耐烦。

"说吧，什么事？"

那张脸你在情报报告里见过。也在历史全息影像里见过。

一旦你认出眼前这个人是谁，这相似就再也躲不开。可最扎眼的是那一身英仙座联盟舰队制服，而不是霸主的军官装。看着实在不对劲。

o.en: I heard you got into a bar fight.
o.zh: 听说你卷进了一场酒吧斗殴。

o.en: I heard someone tried to assassinate you.

entries.en:
"I am well aware," he says, unflinching.

"And who are you to come here, to Yesod, and tell me this?"
entries.zh:
"我很清楚。"他说，面不改色。

"那你又是谁，跑到 Yesod 来，对我说这些？"

o.en: Your life may be in danger, lieutenant.
o.zh: 你的性命可能有危险，上尉。

o.en: Your life is in danger, lieutenant. I'm here to help you.
o.zh: 你的性命有危险，上尉。我是来帮你的。

o.en: Your life is in danger, lieutenant. I'm here to help you. (lie)
o.zh: 你的性命有危险，上尉。我是来帮你的。 (说谎)

o.en: You're a clone of Philip Andrada.
o.zh: 你是 Philip Andrada 的克隆体。

o.en: Fleet Intel knows about you. Are you content to be their pawn?
o.zh: 舰队情报部已经知道你了。你就甘心给他们当棋子？

o.en: You've the blood of Philip Andrada! I am sworn to protect you.
o.zh: 你身上流着 Philip Andrada 的血！我发誓要保护你。

entries.en:
He barely reacts to your assertion.

Instead, his eyes drill into you. It's that intense Andrada look, familiar from the propaganda holos. Self-confident to the point of hubris. The eyes that watched as fleets burned in the skies of Askonian.
entries.zh:
你这话没让他起什么反应。

他只是把目光钉进你眼里。那是 Andrada 家特有的逼人眼神，宣传全息里常见的那种。自信到近乎狂妄。就是这双眼睛，看着舰队在 Askonia 诸世界的天空中烧成火海。

o.en: You... already know. Of course you do.
o.zh: 你...早就知道了。你当然知道。

entries.en:
He barely reacts to your revelation.

Instead, his eyes drill into you. It's that intense Andrada look, familiar from the propaganda holos. Self-confident to the point of hubris. The eyes that watched as fleets burned in the skies of Askonian.
entries.zh:
你揭出的这件事没让他起什么反应。

他只是把目光钉进你眼里。那是 Andrada 家特有的逼人眼神，宣传全息里常见的那种。自信到近乎狂妄。就是这双眼睛，看着舰队在 Askonia 诸世界的天空中烧成火海。

entries.en:
The touch of a self-satisfied smile appears on his lips, and Achilles nods; a gesture of respect for catching on.

"I suspected," he says. "So did Fleet Intel, for some time. Their agent contacted me and confirmed it."
entries.zh:
他唇上浮起一丝自得的笑，Achilles 点了点头——那是敬你一点就透的意思。

"我早怀疑过。\"他说。\"舰队情报部也是，已经有一阵了。他们的特工联系上我，确认了这件事。"

o.en: Did someone already come for you? An assassin?
o.zh: 已经有人来找过你了？刺客？

o.en: That was one assassin. Do you have any idea what you're up against?
o.zh: 那只是一个刺客。你知道自己面对的是什么吗？

o.en: I am $playerName. The question is who you are.
Because you're a clone of Philip Andrada.
o.zh: 因为你是 Philip Andrada 的克隆体。

o.en: I am $playerName. And you know you're a clone of Philip Andrada.
o.zh: 我是 $playerName。而你自己清楚，你是 Philip Andrada 的克隆体。

o.en: I am $playerName. The question is, who are you.
Because you're a clone of Philip Andrada.
o.zh: 因为你是 Philip Andrada 的克隆体。

entries.en:
His eyes drill into you.

It's that intense Andrada look, familiar from the propaganda holos. Self-confident to the point of hubris. The eyes that watched as fleets burned in the skies of Askonia.

He knows.
entries.zh:
他的目光钉进你眼里。

那是 Andrada 家特有的逼人眼神，宣传全息里常见的那种。自信到近乎狂妄。就是这双眼睛，看着舰队在 Askonia 诸世界的天空中烧成火海。

他知道了。

entries.en:
His eyes drill into you.

It's that intense Andrada look, familiar from the propaganda holos. Self-confident to the point of hubris. The eyes that watched as fleets burned in the skies of Askonia.
entries.zh:
他的目光钉进你眼里。

那是 Andrada 家特有的逼人眼神，宣传全息里常见的那种。自信到近乎狂妄。就是这双眼睛，看着舰队在 Askonia 诸世界的天空中烧成火海。

o.en: Did Fleet Intelligence tell you? Was it Siyavong?
o.zh: 是舰队情报部告诉你的？Siyavong？

entries.en:
"We should meet," he says. "I find you can only truly sense one's measure in the flesh."

He holds up a hand. "A public place. On Yesod Station."
entries.zh:
"我们该见一面。\"他说。\"我总觉得，只有当面才真能掂出一个人的分量。"

他抬起一只手。"公开场合。就在 Yesod 空间站。"

o.en: I know of a spacer bar...
o.zh: 我知道一家太空佬酒吧...

o.en: It's too risky. You need armed guards.
o.zh: 太冒险了。你需要武装护卫。

o.en: It's too risky. We'll be overheard.
o.zh: 太冒险了。我们会被人听去。

entries.en:
He closes his eyes for a moment, frustration managing to break through his poise.

"No. You don't," he says, the voice of command. "Not yet. Be calm and listen."
entries.zh:
他闭了闭眼，那股懊恼终于从镇定里漏了出来。

"不。别急着起誓。\"他开口，是发号施令的口气。\"还不是时候。冷静，听我说。"

entries.en: He releases a short breath, giving you a reprimanding look.
entries.zh: 他吐出一口气，带着责备看了你一眼。

entries.en: "I have them," he says.
entries.zh: "护卫我有。"他说。

entries.en: "I have means, captain."
entries.zh: "我有门路，舰长。"

entries.en:
"There's a spacer bar," he continues. "You'll know of it. And if you don't, you'll be directed to it. We shall settle what is to be done."

He hits the comms shut-off.
entries.zh:
"有一家太空佬酒吧。\"他接着说。\"你会知道是哪家。就算不知道，也会有人给你指路。该办的事，我们到那儿定。"

他按下了通讯切断键。

o.en: Cut the comm link and shuttle to Yesod Station
o.zh: 切断通讯，坐穿梭机去 Yesod 空间站

entries.en:
"I know of it as well," he says. "We shall settle what is to be done."

He hits the comms shut-off.
entries.zh:
"那家我也知道。\"他说。\"该办的事，我们到那儿定。"

他按下了通讯切断键。

o.en: Cut the comm link and shuttle to Yesod Station
o.zh: 切断通讯，坐穿梭机去 Yesod 空间站

entries.en: His brow raises fractionally, as if to say, you?
entries.zh: 他的眉头抬了抬，仿佛在说：你？

entries.en: His brow raises fractionally, as if to say, you?
entries.zh: 他的眉头抬了抬，仿佛在说：你？

entries.en:
"The Hegemony," he says with a scowl. "Don't be naive. I will not hide."

He re-examines you.
entries.zh:
"霸主。\"他皱眉道。\"别天真了。我不会躲。"

他重新把你打量了一遍。

entries.en: "I will not hide."
entries.zh: "我不会躲。"

entries.en: His expression is level, and stern.
entries.zh: 他的神色平静而严峻。

entries.en: His expression is level, and stern. Truly a young Andrada in the flesh.
entries.zh: 他的神色平静而严峻。活脱脱一个年轻的 Andrada。

entries.en: His lip twitches once, but he remains collected.
entries.zh: 他的嘴唇抽动了一下，随即又恢复镇定。

entries.en: He does not answer; his expression is stern.
entries.zh: 他没有回答，神色严峻。

entries.en: "Let them try," he says softly.
entries.zh: "让他们试试。"他轻声说。

entries.en:
"I am going to ask you a question." He asserts his right to shift the conversation, lifting his gaze slightly.

"I know you bear a commission of the Sindrian Diktat. A pledge of loyalty to the Supreme Executor, my father."

"I understand that he is insensible and close to death."

Achilles betrays no particular emotion as he says this.

"When the time comes, will you honor your pledge - to me? Don't answer yet," he says sharply. "It would be premature."
entries.zh:
"我要问你一个问题。"他略微抬起目光，摆出把话头拿回去的架势。

"我知道你持着辛达强权的委任状。那是对最高元首——我父亲——的效忠宣誓。"

"我也清楚，他已经神志不清，离死不远。"

说这话时，Achilles 没露出任何情绪。

"等到那一天，你会履行你的誓言吗——对我？先别回答。\"他语气陡然一紧。\"现在说还太早。"

entries.en:
You pull up the workspace to review the possibilities for decrypting the ANDRADA files.

The inviolate files taunt you. Seven names lead by the surname of the Lion of Sindria, the Supreme Executor.
entries.zh:
你调出工作区，逐一审视破解 ANDRADA 文件的可行路径。

那些尚未被攻破的文件在嘲弄你。七个名字，全冠着辛达瑞亚之狮、最高元首的姓氏。

entries.en: Soon their contents will be yours. You have only to carry out your chosen course of action.
entries.zh: 很快，其中的内容就会落到你手里。你只须把选定的那条路走完。

entries.en: You pull up the ANDRADA files. There are seven archives filled with timestamped data: Names, locations, status reports, receipts, medical analysis, surveillance.
entries.zh: 你调出 ANDRADA 文件。七个档案，塞满了带时间戳的数据：姓名、地点、状态报告、收据、医学分析、监视记录。

entries.en:
"Intel files," he repeats your words with more than a dash of skepticism.

"Whose?"
entries.zh:
"情报文件，"他把你的话重复了一遍，怀疑不止一点点。

"谁的？"

o.en: I think they belong to Dolos Macario. You've heard of him?
o.zh: 我想它们属于 Dolos Macario。你听说过他吗？

o.en: They concern the Sindrian Diktat. Philip Andrada, actually, in particular.
o.zh: 它们事关辛达强权。确切地说，尤其是 Philip Andrada。

o.en: It's probably best if I don't tell you.
o.zh: 这事我最好还是别告诉你。

entries.en: "Yes." He rubs his temples. "I've heard of him."
entries.zh: "是啊。\"他揉了揉太阳穴，\"我听说过他。"

entries.en: "Yes." He rubs his temples. "They would, wouldn't they."
entries.zh: "是啊。\"他揉了揉太阳穴，\"他们干得出来，不是吗。"

entries.en: "Yes." He rubs his temples. "It probably is."
entries.zh: "是啊。\"他揉了揉太阳穴，\"多半就是这样。"

entries.en: "You know what I'm going to say, right?"
entries.zh: "你知道我要说什么，对吧？"

o.en: 'I'm going to explain to you how we're going to short volatiles futures.'
o.zh: '我来给你讲讲，我们怎么去做空挥发物期货。'

entries.en:
"Correct," he says. "Then I say that this is probably the sort of stupid scheme Gargoyle would love."

Arroyo cuts the comms.
entries.zh:
"没错，\"他说，\"然后我会说，这多半正是 Gargoyle 会喜欢的那种蠢主意。"

Arroyo 切断了通讯。

entries.en:
"Well done," he says.

Arroyo cuts the comms.
entries.zh:
"说得对，"他说道。

Arroyo 切断了通讯。

entries.en:
"No," he says. "The answer was 'no'. Then I say that this is probably the sort of stupid scheme Gargoyle would love."

Arroyo cuts the comms.
entries.zh:
"不对，\"他说，\"答案就是'不'。然后我会说，这多半正是 Gargoyle 会喜欢的那种蠢主意。"

Arroyo 切断了通讯。

entries.en:
This catches him off-guard.

"Maybe you're not as hopeless as I thought," he says. "I still don't want to be involved. Take this to Gargoyle, it sounds like the sort of stupid scheme they'd love."

"Now get out of here," he turns away. "I need to comms my volatiles guy."

Arroyo cuts the feed.
entries.zh:
这话让他一时没接上。

"也许你没我想的那么没救，\"他说，\"但我还是不想掺和。拿去找 Gargoyle 吧，听起来正对他们那种爱干蠢事的胃口。"

"现在滚吧，\"他转过身去，\"我得联络一下我那个做挥发物的经纪人。"

Arroyo 切断了画面。

o.en: I'd like your advice concerning a... development in the Sindrian Diktat.
o.zh: 我想听听你的意见，关于辛达强权那边的一桩...新动向。

o.en: I need your help decrypting a set of secret intel files.
o.zh: 我需要你帮忙解一批机密情报文件。

entries.en:
As you put the question to your first target, a technician in a well-worn Mbaye-Gogol jumpsuit, they simply push their seat back with a scrape and leave the bar without a word.

Their drink was almost, but not quite, finished.
entries.zh:
你向第一个目标开口——一个穿着磨旧了 Mbaye-Gogol 连体工装的技术员——对方只是把座椅向后一推，椅子刮着地面发出一声刺响，然后一言不发地离开了酒吧。

那杯酒快喝完了，但还差那么一点。

o.en: Try asking another group of employees

entries.en:
One of them just shakes her head, not meeting your eyes.

The second, the friendliest-looking, says "Look captain - it's captain, isn't it? - it's against company policy to discuss work with outsiders. Mbaye-Gogol pays good, and besides..." their eyes dart up, then back to yours.

The third gives you a suspicious glare as he takes a long draught, then sets his glass down heavily. He silently waits for you to leave.
entries.zh:
其中一人只是摇了摇头，没有迎上你的目光。

第二个看起来最和善的开口了："我说舰长——是舰长吧？——跟外人谈工作，是违反公司规定的。Mbaye-Gogol 给的工钱不错，再说..."说到这里，目光往上一飘，又落回你身上。

第三个人一边怀疑地盯着你，一边仰头灌了一大口，然后把杯子重重放下，沉默地等着你走开。

o.en: I see. You've all been... helpful.
o.zh: 我明白了。诸位真是... 帮了大忙。

entries.en:
You sit for a moment to rally after that disappointing foray. What looks like a small independent owner-operator sits beside you, sliding a small, cheap drink over.

"Buncha icecubes, aren't they." He glances at the M-B employees. "I hear they do a psych test to get ones who won't talk. I'd fail like that," he snaps his fingers and grins.

"So what's your business? Meat trade? Or you lookin' to, ya'know-" he plinks an icecube with a finger.
entries.zh:
那一番碰壁之后，你坐下来缓了缓神。一个看上去像是小本个体经营者的人坐到旁边，推过来一杯便宜的小酒。

"一帮冰疙瘩，是不是。"他瞥了一眼 M-B 的员工。"听说他们招人要做心理测试，专挑那些嘴严的。换我，啪一下就被刷掉，"他打了个响指，咧嘴笑了。

"那么，你是做什么的？'卖肉'的？还是想，你懂的——"他用手指弹了一下杯里的冰块。

entries.en: You have a lovely but uninformative chat with the independent captain who is, if nothing else, thankful for some more talkative company before heading back to his ship to catch a sleep shift.
entries.zh: 你跟那名独立舰长聊得挺愉快，却什么也没问出来。那人别的没有，至少很感激碰上了一个话更多些的伴，随后便回船赶睡眠班去了。

entries.en:
"Cydonia." He sits back. "Yeah, I've heard of 'im."

"That's Warlord Kanta's new... not sure what to call it, exactly. Cydonia talks for her when she holds court, like she does."

He gives you a nervous glance.

"So I hear. Not personally witnessed, mind. Heard from another captain what was big in the meat trade; smuggling, you know. Anyway, maybe Cydonia's working on keeping her - Kanta, that is - alive for another hundred cycles. Cybernetics, augments, fringe stuff."
entries.zh:
"Cydonia。\"他往后一靠。\"嗯，听说过他。"

"那是军阀 Kanta 新收的... 我说不准该叫什么。Kanta 坐朝听政的时候，Cydonia 替她开口——她本人也是这么办的。"

他不安地瞥了你一眼。

"我听到的说法是这样。不过我没亲眼见过。是从另一个'卖肉'做得很大的舰长那儿听来的，走私，你懂的。总之，也许 Cydonia 正在想办法让她——我是说 Kanta——再活一百个星历年。控制论、强化改造，都是些偏门东西。"

entries.en:
"Non-ethical, you might say," he says, waggling his eyebrows evocatively. "Live specimens, it's said. Taken apart, hooked up to tubes and machines, injected with nanos and what-not. Testing theories, treatments."

He grabs a handful of salty snacks and puts them in his mouth, crunching away unselfconsciously.
entries.zh:
"你也可以说，是不讲伦理的那种，\"他说着，意味深长地挑了挑眉毛。\"听说是活体标本。拆开来，接上管子和机器，注射纳米之类的玩意儿。验证理论，试疗法。"

他抓了一把咸味零嘴塞进嘴里，毫无顾忌地大嚼起来。

entries.en:
"Cydonia, here?" He looks taken aback. "I know of a Doctor Cydonia - everyone hears stories, you know. But he's over with Kanta, maybe working on keeping her alive another hundred cycles. Cybernetics, augments, fringe stuff."

"Non-ethical, you might say," he says, waggling his eyebrows evocatively. "Live specimens, it's said. Taken apart, hooked up to tubes and machines, injected with nanos and what-not. Meat trade makes good money selling to his agents, but... it ain't clean."

He grabs a handful of salty snacks and puts them in his mouth, crunching away unselfconsciously.
entries.zh:
"Cydonia，在这儿？\"他明显一愣。\"我倒是知道一个 Cydonia 博士——这种故事谁没听过。但他人在 Kanta 那边，也许正琢磨着让她再活一百个星历年。控制论、强化改造，都是些偏门东西。"

"你也可以说，是不讲伦理的那种，\"他说着，意味深长地挑了挑眉毛。\"听说是活体标本。拆开来，接上管子和机器，注射纳米之类的玩意儿。'卖肉'这行把货卖给他的手底下人，钱是真好赚，可... 这活儿不干净。"

他抓了一把咸味零嘴塞进嘴里，毫无顾忌地大嚼起来。

entries.en:
"Now, I know they do something akin of that here. Living longer, you know. Grow you a new body if your last one wore out, making it all work right and proper and better than before even."

He takes a long draught from his drink.

"But here it's clean work." A small belch interrupts. "-And maybe it's not always what them Heggies might consider strictly lawful, but it's done proper and polite. High-class, top credits. I could see Cydonia wanting the respect of a place like this, but he'd never get it. He's a back-corridor cutter, even if he's the king of 'em."
entries.zh:
"不过呢，我知道这儿也做类似的事。活得久一点，你懂的。上一具身子用废了，就给你长一具新的，弄得好好的、规规矩矩的，甚至比原来还强。"

他仰头灌了一大口酒。

"但这儿做的是干净活儿。\"他打了个小小的嗝。\"——也许不总是霸主那帮人眼里完全合法的勾当，可办得体面、讲礼数。上等货色，顶级的星币。我看得出 Cydonia 想要这种地方给的体面，可他永远得不到。他就是个在后巷里动刀子的，哪怕他是那行里的王。"

entries.en:
The independent captain takes your snub in stride and has one last, long draw from his drink.
